latestRelease.notes:
# Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (v2026.8.13)

**Release Date:** August 13, 2026

> Patch release. This tag rolls up the ~656 PRs merged since v0.20.0 into a stable tagged release for downstream consumers (Docker images, hosted deployments, and anyone installing from the latest tag).

---

## About this release

Since v0.20.0 (August 3), this window landed **1,444 commits** across **~656 merged PRs**, touching **2,172 files** (+233,872 / −75,244), and closed **~481 issues**. It is a broad stabilization-and-fixes rollup spanning the desktop app, gateway platforms, installers, tool system, and provider catalogs.

**Full curated release notes for this window will ship with v0.21.0**, which will document everything from v0.20.0 onward — highlights, feature areas, and complete contributor credits. Nothing in this window is skipped.

## Updating

- Existing installs: `hermes update`
- Fresh install: see the installer one-liner in the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent#readme)

**Full Changelog**: [v2026.8.3...v2026.8.13](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/compare/v2026.8.3...v2026.8.13)

signals.title: [Bug]: Response truncated due to output length limit — still occurring after #7237 fix (re-opening closed issue)
signals.text: ### Bug Description The error "Response truncated due to output length limit" persists despite previous fixes in #7242 and #9525, which were merged in response to the now-closed issue #7237. The issue was closed by a maintainer last month with the explanation that it is "not a bug" but rather a context window limitation. However, extensive testing and user reports (see the 10+ comments since the closure) continue to reproduce the error across different models — including those with very large context windows (414k tokens, 131k tokens, and even Gemini 1.5 with 2M tokens). This suggests that while the **input context** might be sufficient, the **output token cap** or the **continuation logic** for long tool outputs/summaries is failing. This new issue is meant to re-surface the problem with specific reproduction data showing failures on fresh sessions with large-context models. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Launch `hermes chat` (CLI) or `hermes gateway start` (Telegram / Discord / Slack). 2. Trigger a tool call that returns a large, dense payload (e.g., >80KB). - *Example*: `mcp_mongodb_collection_schema` on a complex database collection. - *Example*: `read_file` on a large lockfile (e.g., `pnpm-lock.yaml` or `package-lock.json`). 3. Observe the agent stop mid-generation (often during a summary or a sub-agent's response) with: `:warning: Response truncated (finish_reason='length') - model hit max output tokens` `:warning: Truncated tool call response detected — refusing to execute incomplete tool arguments.` `Error: Response truncated due to output length limit` 4. This happens even on fresh sessions (low input context), ruling out simple history overflow. ### Expected Behavior Long responses should be split into chunks or the continuation logic should reliably retry until a complete response is assembled. The 3-retry mechanism introduced in #7242 / #9525 should prevent hard truncation in all API modes (chat_completions and anthropic_messages) by detecting `finish_reason='length'` and requesting the remainder. ### Actual Behavior The agent throws "Response truncated due to output length limit" and halts. The continuation/retry logic does not trigger effectively, or the truncated JSON/summary is rejected by the agent's core before it can be completed. Confirmed still occurring in: - qwen3.6-27b-fp8 (414k context) — @theogravity - GLM-51-NVFP4 — @Damikk19 - gpt-oss-20b (131k context) — @kevinctofel - aws-claude-opus-4-6 — @yangyang233333 - Gemini 1.5 Flash / Pro (2M context) — @poulpe-agent-repro - custom provider: gpt-5.5 — @arsitekberotok ### Affected Component Agent Core (conversation loop, tool output handling, continuation logic) ### Debug Report ```shell Report <https://paste.rs/JFt5G> agent.log <https://paste.rs/Anyts> gateway.log <https://paste.rs/N8CNm> ``` ### Operating System Ubuntu 24.04 ### Root Cause Analysis The current logic fails to differentiate between "Context Window Full" (Input) and "Max Output Tokens Hit" (Output). - Many providers have a hard limit on single completion length (e.g., 4096 or 8192 tokens). - When a tool returns a massive result (e.g., a 100KB schema), the model tries to process/summarize it and hits its output cap long before it exhausts its input context. - The continuation loop's progressive max_tokens boost (capped at 32k per #9525) might be insufficient or is not correctly detecting truncation when it happens inside a tool-call or sub-agent structure. ### Proposed Fix - **Intelligent Tool Output Management**: If a tool result exceeds a certain size (e.g., 50KB), save it to a temporary file and only inject a summary/snippet into the context to prevent the model from "choking" on the output generation. - **Unify Continuation Logic**: Ensure `anthropic_messages` and `chat_completions` paths are perfectly synced regarding truncation detection and retry. - **Configurable Output Caps**: Allow users to override the 32k boost cap or the default `max_tokens` for completions in `config.yaml`. - **Improved Logging**: Surface the actual token counts (Output used / Max output) when a truncation occurs to distinguish from Input context limits. ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

signals.title: Gateway hits macOS fd limit (256): OSError Too many open files
signals.text: ## Problem On macOS, the default `launchctl limit maxfiles` soft limit is **256**. Hermes gateway processes with multiple profiles + MCP servers routinely exceed this: ``` trade-paper gateway: 286 fds (198 IPv4, 50 REG, 20 PIPE) ``` When the limit is hit, any file operation fails with: ``` OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files: '.sessions_*.tmp' ``` This crashes session saves, kanban dispatches, and any tool that opens files. ## Root cause - Each MCP server subprocess (playwright, sequential-thinking, memory, brave-search) maintains persistent pipes/sockets - Multiple profiles each run their own gateway with independent MCP connections - Hermes never closes idle MCP connections or monitors fd usage - No startup warning when `ulimit -n` is near capacity ## Workaround Manually add `SoftResourceLimits` → `NumberOfFiles: 4096` to each gateway launchd plist. ## Suggested fixes 1. **Startup detection**: Check `resource.getrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE)` at gateway start, warn if soft limit < 1024 2. **MCP lazy init**: Don't connect all MCP servers at startup — connect on first tool call 3. **Idle MCP timeout**: Close MCP connections idle for N minutes, reconnect on demand 4. **Periodic fd check**: Log warning in gateway loop if fd count exceeds 80% of soft limit ## Environment - macOS 26.5 (Apple Silicon) - Hermes 3 profiles (default, research, trade-paper) - 6 MCP servers configured - Python 3.x, launchd-managed gateways
signals.author: BournYSix

signals.title: [Feature]: Native desktop/mobile client app
signals.text: ## Feature Description A native desktop/mobile client app for Hermes Agent that interacts directly with the local Gateway/API Server, without relying on third-party messaging platforms as intermediaries. ## Motivation Current interaction methods each have limitations imposed by the platforms themselves: - URLs in tool output get truncated, making links unclickable - Message length limits force HTML file workarounds - Interactive approval buttons degrade to plain text across versions - Gateway restarts disconnect the session - Technical config must be done via CLI separately A native client would provide a purpose-built interface for AI agent interaction. ## Proposed Solution Cross-platform native app (Tauri/Flutter) reusing existing API Server + Gateway: - Desktop: Windows/macOS/Linux - Mobile: iOS/Android - Shared sessions, skills, memory with CLI/Web UI - Native push notifications, file handling, proper URL rendering
signals.author: AustinDZG

signals.title: [Windows] Gateway cron scheduler circular dependency + os.kill(pid,0) broken — no auto-recovery when gateway crashes
signals.text: ## Summary On Windows, when the messaging gateway process dies, **all cron jobs stop firing** (including any watchdog cron), because the cron scheduler is embedded inside the gateway. Combined with a broken `os.kill(pid, 0)` in `is_process_alive()` (which raises `OSError: [WinError 87]` on Windows), there is no reliable auto-recovery path. ## Root Cause 1: Cron runs inside the gateway (circular dependency) The cron scheduler ticks every 60 seconds from within the gateway process (`gateway/run.py` → "Cron ticker started"). This is documented: *"The gateway also runs the cron scheduler, ticking every 60 seconds to execute due jobs."* This works on **Linux** because `hermes gateway install` creates a **systemd user service with `Restart=on-failure`** — when the gateway dies, systemd respawns it instantly and the cron scheduler resumes. On **Windows**, `hermes gateway install` creates only a one-shot Scheduled Task or a Startup-folder shortcut — neither provides crash auto-recovery. **When the gateway dies on Windows, cron jobs (including watchdog crons) stop forever.** ### Impact - Daily briefings fail to deliver if the gateway died overnight - Any cron-based watchdog is powerless to restart the gateway - User only discovers the outage when they manually try to message the bot ## Root Cause 2: `os.kill(pid, 0)` silently fails on Windows From the diagnostic code at multiple points in the codebase (e.g., `hermes gateway status`, watchdog scripts): ```python def is_process_alive(gateway_pid): import signal try: os.kill(gateway_pid, 0) # signal 0 = existence check return True except OSError: return False ``` **`os.kill(pid, 0)` is a POSIX-only pattern.** On Windows, it raises `OSError: [WinError 87] The parameter is incorrect` for **every PID**, regardless of whether the process exists. The exception handler catches this and returns `False` — so the function **always reports the gateway as dead**, even when it's running fine. This is called from: - `gateway/status.py` — `is_process_alive()` for state file verification - `hermes gateway status` CLI command - Any watchdog scripts that use signal 0 ### Impact - `hermes gateway status` may falsely report "no gateway process detected" even when running - Watchdog scripts constantly trigger false-positive recovery attempts ## Root Cause 3: `hermes gateway install` on Windows provides no crash recovery On Linux: ``` hermes gateway install → systemd user service → Restart=on-failure → auto-respawn on crash ``` On Windows: ``` hermes gateway install → Scheduled Task (one-shot, no auto-restart) → Startup folder fallback (only fires at login) ``` There is no mechanism to respawn the gateway if it crashes mid-session. ## Reproduction 1. On Windows, run `hermes gateway install` 2. Set up a cron job (e.g., a daily briefing) 3. Kill the gateway process (e.g., via Task Manager) 4. Observe: `hermes cron status` shows "Gateway is not running — cron jobs will NOT fire" 5. No auto-recovery occurs — the gateway stays dead ## Suggested Fixes ### Fix 1: Replace `os.kill(pid, 0)` with cross-platform PID check Replace the POSIX-only `os.kill(pid, 0)` with a function that uses `tasklist` on Windows: ```python import subprocess import sys def is_process_alive(pid): if sys.platform == "win32": try: result = subprocess.run( ["tasklist", "/FI", f"PID eq {pid}", "/FO", "CSV", "/NH"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10 ) return str(pid) in result.stdout except Exception: return False else: import signal try: os.kill(pid, 0) return True except OSError: return False ``` **Important:** Use single-slash flags (`/FI`, `/FO`, `/NH`). Double slashes (`//FI`) are an MSYS/Git-Bash escape convention — when called from Python's `subprocess`, they're passed literally and ignored by tasklist. ### Fix 2: Add Windows watchdog to `hermes gateway install` Modify `hermes gateway install` on Windows to either: - Create a **repeating** Scheduled Task (every N minutes) that runs a bundled watchdog script - Or create a VBS/PowerShell launcher loop that auto-restarts the gateway on exit The installer should bundle a minimal `gateway-watchdog.py` script in `HERMES_HOME/scripts/` and wire it up automatically during `hermes gateway install`. ## Workaround (for users affected now) Create a repeating Windows Scheduled Task as an external watchdog: ```bash schtasks //Create //TN "Hermes_Watchdog" //TR "\"C:\path\to\pythonw.exe\" \"C:\path\to\gateway_watchdog.py\"" //SC MINUTE //MO 10 //F ``` The watchdog checks if the gateway PID is alive via `tasklist`, and if not, launches `pythonw.exe -m hermes_cli.main gateway run --replace`. ## Environment - **OS:** Windows 10 (native, not WSL) - **Hermes:** current main branch - **Install:** Hermes Desktop / PowerShell installer

signals.title: copilot-acp: fallback providers not triggered when Copilot monthly quota is exhausted
signals.text: ## Description When using `copilot-acp` as the primary provider with `fallback_providers` configured, the fallback chain does **not** activate when GitHub Copilot returns a monthly quota exhaustion error. Instead of falling back to the next provider, the error is surfaced directly to the user. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure `copilot-acp` as primary provider: ```yaml model: provider: copilot-acp default: auto base_url: acp://copilot api_mode: chat_completions ``` 2. Configure fallback providers: ```yaml fallback_providers: - provider: opencode-zen model: big-pickle base_url: https://opencode.ai/zen/v1 api_mode: chat_completions - provider: openrouter model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash base_url: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 api_mode: chat_completions - provider: openai-codex model: gpt-5.4-mini base_url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex ``` 3. Have valid API keys for fallback providers (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `OPENCODE_ZEN_API_KEY`). 4. Exhaust Copilot's monthly quota. 5. Send a message via Telegram or CLI — the agent returns the raw error instead of falling back. ## Error Message ``` Error: You have exceeded your monthly quota (Request ID: A540:22A007:3849658:44F52D9:6A541F53) ``` ## Analysis The Copilot ACP client (`agent/copilot_acp_client.py`) raises a `RuntimeError` when the subprocess exits early. The error message contains the word `"quota"` which exists in `_USAGE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` in `agent/error_classifier.py`, which should classify it as `FailoverReason.billing` with `should_fallback=True`. However, in practice the fallback chain is never activated. There appear to be two potential issues: 1. **Missing billing pattern**: `_BILLING_PATTERNS` has `"exceeded your current quota"` but the Copilot message says `"exceeded your *monthly* quota"` — the substring `"exceeded your current quota"` does not match `"exceeded your monthly quota"`. While `_USAGE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` does contain `"quota"`, the matching logic may not be reaching that check for ACP RuntimeErrors. 2. **ACP error path**: The RuntimeError from the ACP subprocess may be caught at a different level before reaching `classify_api_error()` in the conversation loop, bypassing the classification entirely. ## Environment - Hermes Agent (latest) - Provider: `copilot-acp` - Platform: Telegram gateway (also reproducible via CLI) - API keys for fallback providers are configured and valid ## Expected Behavior When Copilot ACP returns a quota exhaustion error, the fallback chain should activate and switch to the next configured provider (opencode-zen, then openrouter, etc.). ## Actual Behavior The error is surfaced directly without attempting fallback providers.
signals.author: craftpip

signals.title: Desktop per-profile remote overrides silently relabel sessions from multi-profile backends
signals.text: ## Bug description Hermes Desktop silently misattributes sessions when multiple Desktop profiles use per-profile remote overrides that point to the same multi-profile Hermes backend. Concrete setup: - One remote Hermes host/backend contains `default`, `wife`, and `dad` profiles. - Desktop → Settings → Gateway configures the `wife` scope and `dad` scope with the same remote backend URL, intending each Desktop profile to use its matching remote profile. - Switching between `wife` and `dad` does not reliably distinguish their sessions. Rows from the remote backend's launch/current profile can appear under whichever local Desktop profile selected the connection. This is a real user workflow, not hypothetical: the user shares one Hermes host with family profiles and needs Desktop session history to preserve the remote profile boundary. ## Reproduction 1. Run one remote `hermes serve` backend on a host with at least two named profiles, e.g. `wife` and `dad`. 2. In Hermes Desktop, open Settings → Gateway. 3. Under **Applies to**, configure `wife` as Remote and point it at that backend URL. 4. Configure `dad` the same way, pointing at the same backend URL. 5. Create or observe distinct sessions in the remote `wife` and `dad` profile databases. 6. Switch between the two Desktop profiles and inspect the session list. ### Actual The session list does not preserve the remote owning profile. It can show the backend launch-profile sessions under both Desktop scopes, relabeled as `wife` or `dad`. ### Expected Desktop must either: 1. route each request to the explicit matching remote profile and preserve authoritative profile identity returned by the backend; or 2. detect that a per-profile override is not a profile-scoped endpoint and block/warn instead of silently relabeling sessions. The UI must never claim that a session belongs to `wife` or `dad` unless the backend request was actually scoped to that profile. ## Root cause on current `main` The per-profile remote override path assumes that each URL already serves exactly one profile: - `apps/desktop/electron/connection-config.ts` documents that per-profile remote overrides are already profile-scoped and therefore omits the profile query. - `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts::remoteSessionList` deletes `profile` from the query, calls the remote backend's ordinary `/api/sessions`, then forcibly assigns every returned row to the local Desktop profile: ```ts qs.delete('profile') const data = await fetchJsonForProfile(profile, `/api/sessions?${qs}`) for (const s of rowsOf(data)) { s.profile = profile s.is_default_profile = false } ``` Against a multi-profile backend, `/api/sessions` therefore reads the backend process's launch/current profile, and Desktop overwrites that authoritative identity with the local connection-scope name. This is distinct from, but interacts with, #62503 / #62509: - #62509 fixes backend `session.*` RPC methods that ignore `params.profile`. - #64266 proposes explicit `session_profiles` capability negotiation and authoritative profile echoes. - This issue is the Desktop REST/session-list path and connection semantics: a per-profile override currently strips profile scope and manufactures profile labels. ## Suggested direction Use backend capability/identity rather than assuming URL shape: - If the remote advertises profile-aware routing, keep/pass the requested profile (`?profile=<name>` / `params.profile`) and preserve the backend-returned profile. - If the endpoint is explicitly profile-scoped, verify its effective profile before using it and tag rows only from that verified identity. - Never unconditionally overwrite `s.profile` merely because that local connection entry was selected. - Add a regression with one remote URL, two Desktop profile scopes, and distinct session rows in two remote profile databases. - Consider a Settings warning when two per-profile overrides share one URL but the backend cannot prove profile-aware routing. ## Environment note `HERMES_DESKTOP_REMOTE_URL` was verified unset in the shell, macOS `launchctl`, and all running Hermes Desktop processes. The behavior comes from saved per-profile connection overrides, not the environment override.
signals.author: andyylin

signals.title: [Feature]: Live upgrade — update Hermes without killing running subagents (zero-downtime update)
signals.text: ## Summary Currently, updating Hermes (via `hermes update`, WebUI auto-update, or cron-triggered update) kills ALL running subagents. This is because subagents are child processes of the parent Hermes — when the parent restarts, children become orphaned zombies. **The result:** users who click "update" in the WebUI, or have an automatic cron update, lose all in-progress subagent work. Long-running delegations (kanban workers, batch processing, research tasks) are silently killed. ## The Problem - **WebUI update** → version mismatch → blocks user → restart kills subagents - **Cron auto-update** → `hermes update` runs → gateway restarts → subagents orphaned - **CLI update** → user runs `hermes update` → unaware subagents will die - **Recovery:** impossible — subagent results lost forever, no checkpoint ## Proposed Solution: Blue-Green Live Upgrade ### Architecture (blue-green pattern) ```text BEFORE: Hermes(old) → [Subagent A, B, C running] DURING: Hermes(old) draining → [Subagents finish naturally] Hermes(new) ready on staging port AFTER: Hermes(new) → socket migration → old exits ``` ### Implementation for v1: Checkpoint + Orphan Adoption (~50-100 lines) 1. **Checkpoint file**: before restart, serialize all active subagent state (session_id, goal, pid) to `$HERMES_HOME/state/subagent_checkpoints.json` 2. **Orphan recovery on startup**: new Hermes process scans checkpoint, checks alive PIDs via `os.kill(pid, 0)`, re-attaches via `os.waitpid` 3. **Result collection**: subagents that finish during update — their stdout/stderr are still in the pipe buffer **Key insight:** orphaned subagents dont die — they keep running until they try to write to a broken pipe. We just pick up their exit status. ## Advantages | Aspect | Before | After | |--------|--------|-------| | WebUI update | Blocks + kills subagents | Zero-downtime | | Cron auto-update | Jobs lost | Jobs complete naturally | | Kanban workers | Reset from zero | Continue where they left off | | Long research tasks | Results lost forever | Results preserved | | Reliability | Low (update = risk) | High (update = safe) | | Auto-update adoption | Users hesitate | Fully automatic | ## Related - #70755 — WebUI auto-reload (complementary) - #70721 — Plugin update guard (different scope) --- Would be happy to contribute the implementation if the direction is acceptable.
signals.author: webtecnica

signals.title: Bug: config set duplicates top-level key + Telegram streaming+reply_to_mode='first' duplicates final message
signals.text: # Bug: `hermes config set` creates a duplicate top-level key instead of editing the existing one; Telegram streaming + reply_to_mode="first" causes duplicate-delivered final message ## Environment - Hermes Agent version: `0.19.0` (pyproject.toml) - Platform: Windows 10 - Telegram DM (chat `589593795`) - Config: `streaming: true`, `platforms.telegram.streaming: true`, `platforms.telegram.reply_to_mode: first` (default) ## Two related problems ### Problem A — Duplicate top-level config key written by `hermes config set` Running: ``` hermes config set platforms.telegram.streaming false ``` **Expected:** the existing `platforms.telegram.streaming` value is flipped to `false`. **Actual:** a *second* top-level `platforms:` block is appended to the end of `config.yaml` (with `enabled: true` + `streaming: false`), while the original `platforms.telegram.streaming` (earlier in the file) stays `true`. Evidence from the affected `config.yaml` (before manual fix): ``` 264: platforms: # original block — gateway reads THIS one 265: telegram: 266: streaming: true # <-- unchanged 267: show_reasoning: false ... 599: platforms: # DUPLICATE block appended by `config set` 600: telegram: 601: enabled: true 602: streaming: false # <-- the value `config set` actually wrote ``` Consequences: - `hermes config get platforms.telegram.streaming` returns `false` (resolves the *last* occurrence, so it looks fixed). - The gateway loader resolves the *first* `platforms:` block, so it keeps seeing `streaming: true`. - This makes the fix appear successful from the CLI while having **no effect** on runtime behaviour — a silent, confusing failure. The user must restart the gateway and still sees the bug. Resolution I applied manually (since `config set` cannot be trusted here): removed the duplicate trailing `platforms:` block and edited the original `streaming` key to `false`. After that the gateway (post-restart) no longer duplicates the message. ### Problem B — Streaming + `reply_to_mode: "first"` produces a visibly-duplicated final message With `platforms.telegram.streaming: true` and `reply_to_mode: first`: 1. The streamed preview is delivered as a **reply** to the user's message (because of `reply_to_mode: first`). 2. On finalize, the adapter attempts to convert the preview into the final MarkdownV2 message via `edit_message` (`finalize=True`). 3. If the final edit fails (flood control / 4096-cap saturation / transient error), the code falls back to a **fresh resend** as a new non-reply message — governed by `RESEND_FINAL_ON_EMPTY_STREAM_FALLBACK = True` (telegram/adapter.py:618). Result: the user sees **two messages** — one quoted-reply (the streamed preview) and one plain message (the resend). In the gateway log both appear as a single logical delivery (`Suppressing normal final send ... content_delivered=True`), so the duplication is effectively invisible to the gateway's own accounting even though Telegram shows two messages. Relevant code points: - `hermes-agent/plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py:605-618` — `REQUIRES_EDIT_FINALIZE`, `FALLBACK_ON_FINAL_EDIT_FLOOD`, `RESEND_FINAL_ON_EMPTY_STREAM_FALLBACK` - `hermes-agent/gateway/run.py:23204` — "Suppressing normal final send ... final delivery already confirmed" ## Why I did NOT patch it locally The root cause for Problem B is the finalize/resend path in the Telegram adapter. A local patch (e.g. disabling `RESEND_FINAL_ON_EMPTY_STREAM_FALLBACK` or forcing `reply_to_mode: off`) is possible but risky for an end user, and `reply_to_mode: off` only *hides* the visual difference (both messages become plain) rather than preventing the duplicate send. The correct fix belongs upstream: - Either make `config set` edit the existing key instead of appending a duplicate block (Problem A), and/or - Make the streamed-preview delivery durable enough that a failed final edit does not require a duplicate resend (Problem B). ## Reproduction for Problem A 1. Fresh config with `platforms.telegram.streaming: true`. 2. `hermes config set platforms.telegram.streaming false` 3. Open `config.yaml` — a second `platforms:` block now exists at EOF. 4. `hermes config get platforms.telegram.streaming` → `false` (misleading). 5. Gateway restart → still streams (reads first block). ## Suggested fix for Problem A `hermes config set` should resolve the canonical occurrence of a nested key (the one the runtime loader actually uses) and mutate it in place, rather than appending a new top-level block. At minimum it should refuse to write a duplicate top-level key or warn that multiple `platforms:` blocks exist. ## Suggested fix for Problem B For `reply_to_mode != off`, preserve the reply anchor on the resend fallback message (so the preview and the final are the *same* message visually), or treat a successful streamed preview as the authoritative final delivery and skip the resend entirely when content was already delivered.
signals.author: zoser69

signals.title: Add a "Move session to project" action in Desktop
signals.text: ## Problem If a session is created under the wrong project, or later needs to be reorganized, there is currently no clear way to move it to another project. Because project membership is derived from workspace/CWD state, users can end up with sessions under an unexpected project or auto-project. Once that happens, the only practical option is to leave the session where it is or edit internal state manually. ## Suggested UX Add a simple action for non-running local sessions: - `Move to project...` - `Move to Home / detached` Possible entry points: - session context menu - drag-and-drop between project groups - command palette ## Expected behavior For a stopped local Desktop/CLI session: 1. Choose a target project. 2. Reassign the session workspace to that project's primary path. 3. Clear or recompute stale Git workspace metadata if necessary. 4. Refresh the session list and `projects.tree` so the session immediately appears in the new project. For `Move to Home`, the session should become detached instead of inheriting another project's workspace. Running sessions, cron runs, messaging-platform sessions, subagent sessions, and tool sessions can simply have this action disabled. ## Why The current project model is powerful, but without a move action, one mistaken or unexpected session placement is difficult to correct. This would also complement #75537, which requests predictable creation rules: - Global New Chat -> Home - Project + -> session inside that project Even with predictable creation, users still need a way to reorganize existing sessions. Thanks for considering it!
signals.author: reezex0-ux

signals.title: Desktop: pin/unpin still reverted by a list page that lands after the PATCH ack (follow-up to #74570)
signals.text: ## Bug After the #74570 fix (`090d14647`), a fresh local pin/unpin is protected **while the PATCH is in flight** (`unconfirmed` guard). But the guard is cleared on the PATCH's own ack, and a **session-list request issued before the write can land after the ack** still carrying the pre-write value. The pull pass then reads that stale row with no guard left and reverts the user's action — and because the reverted state is pushed back to the server by the next reconcile, the wrong value becomes durable. User-visible symptom: pin/unpin works **intermittently** — clicking "unpin" in the sidebar sometimes sticks, sometimes instantly reverts and the session stays pinned (the server row is re-PATCHed back to `pinned=true` by the resurrection). ## Timeline (unpin example) ``` t-1 list request #N issued (server row still pinned=true) <- stale page in flight t0 user unpins -> reconcile -> PATCH pinned=false issued <- unconfirmed.set(id, false) t1 PATCH ack -> unconfirmed.delete(id) <- guard gone (090d14647 clears on ack) t2 list response #N lands (pinned=true) -> $sessions change -> reconcile -> pullRemotePins() -> no pending, no unconfirmed -> row.pinned && !heldLocally -> pinSession() -> PIN RESURRECTED t3 resurrection fires reconcile -> PATCH pinned=true -> server row flipped back ``` The symmetric race hits pin too (stale `pinned=false` page after a pin's ack -> `unpinSession()`). Why the ack is not enough: the `unconfirmed` guard's lifetime is the PATCH request itself, but the stale list page's lifetime can be longer — list requests are heavier and slower, and `refreshSessions()` runs on every `message.complete`/turn/focus, so the window is real and recurring. ## Evidence - `pullRemotePins()` in `apps/desktop/src/store/session-pin-sync.ts` (current main): `unconfirmed` is deleted in `writePin()`'s `.then()` — the pull pass can no longer distinguish "page issued before the write" from "genuinely newer truth" once the ack landed. - The existing test `ignores a stale page that contradicts a write still in flight` only covers a stale page arriving **before** the ack; the post-ack window is untested. Its final assertion ("once acked, later server truth is honoured") assumes every post-ack page is new — not true for requests issued pre-write. - Reproduced in practice on macOS (Desktop 0.17.0 build containing `090d14647`): a just-unpinned session reappears pinned in the sidebar and `sessions.pinned` in state.db reads back `1`. ## Suggested fix Keep the write guard until a list page **confirms the written value**, with a cooldown fallback so it can't go stale forever: - `writePin()`: record `{ value, at: Date.now() }` and do NOT clear on ack. - `pullRemotePins()`: if a guard exists for the row and `guard.value !== row.pinned` **and** `Date.now() - guard.at < COOLDOWN_MS` (e.g. 5s), skip the row (stale page). Otherwise delete the guard and reconcile normally — the page confirms the write, or is old enough that it must be fresh truth. - A failed PATCH still clears the guard so later pages are honoured. This preserves the cross-app sync (a genuinely newer page from another app is adopted) while closing the post-ack stale-page window. I have a working patch + regression tests (pin and unpin directions, guard confirmation, cooldown expiry) ready to open as a PR if this approach is accepted. ## Environment - Hermes Desktop 0.17.0 (build containing `090d14647`), Hermes Agent v0.19.x, macOS 27.0 (arm64) - Upstream main @ `4983c576b` — `apps/desktop/src/store/session-pin-sync.ts` unchanged since `090d14647`

signals.title: Desktop restart reaps the live gateway but never relaunches it (WeChat/QQ go silent) — regression
signals.text: ## Summary On Windows (Hermes 0.20.0, desktop app), **every desktop-app restart force-kills the running messaging gateway and never relaunches it**. WeChat (iLink), QQ bot and Telegram go completely silent until the gateway is manually restarted. This is a regression: before this version, the old gateway survived desktop restarts (reparented), so messaging stayed online. ## Root cause In `hermes_cli/web_server.py`, when the desktop backend starts (`HERMES_DESKTOP=1`), it calls `_reap_unsupervised_gateway_orphans()` before boot, with the comment *"Before forking a fresh gateway, reap any orphan left by a previous serve session... (#77276)"*. However: 1. `_reap_unsupervised_gateway_orphans()` → `find_gateway_pids()` → `_scan_gateway_pids()` matches **any** process whose command line looks like `hermes_cli.main gateway run` (`looks_like_gateway_command_line`), including gateways started by the Windows scheduled task (`Hermes_Gateway`) or manually via `hermes gateway run`. It writes the planned-stop marker, sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILLs survivors after 5s. 2. The comment says "before **forking** a fresh gateway", but `hermes serve` does **not** spawn a gateway at all (per the same file: *"The Desktop backend is spawned as `hermes serve` — it runs neither the interactive CLI nor the messaging gateway"*). Gateway startup is delegated to external mechanisms (the login scheduled task, the update flow, or a manual `hermes gateway run`). 3. Result: **every desktop restart reaps the live gateway with no successor**. The gateway exits uncleanly (`gateway-exit-diag.log`: *"exited UNCLEANLY (no exit path ran — SIGKILL / OOM / VM death)"*), and `.gateway-planned-stop.json` is left behind. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Start the gateway (login scheduled task or `hermes gateway run`). WeChat/QQ/Telegram connect fine. 2. Close and reopen the Hermes desktop app. 3. The gateway process is gone (no exit logs; killed externally). Messages sent via WeChat/QQ get no reply until the gateway is manually restarted. Secondary symptom: the third-party skin plugin (`skin-studio`) re-asserts the configured skin on boot but only retries for ~2.5 s, while the desktop backend takes longer to become ready — so after a desktop restart the skin silently falls back to default until manually re-applied. Same class of "desktop restart breaks things that depend on the gateway/backend". ## Suggested fixes - **Option A**: when the desktop reap kills a live gateway, the desktop backend (or Electron main) should spawn a replacement immediately after reap (complete the "fork a fresh gateway" the comment promises). - **Option B**: only reap gateways that are truly unsupervised (no `gateway.pid` record / not the login scheduled-task instance), instead of every process matching `gateway run`. - **Option C**: add a config switch (e.g. `gateway.reap_on_desktop_start: false`) so users who manage the gateway externally (scheduled task / systemd / manual) can opt out. ## Workaround (user side) A 2-minute Hermes-internal cron job that checks for the gateway process and relaunches it detached with the full environment. Works, but leaves a gap and depends on the desktop backend's own cron scheduler. ## Environment - Windows 11, Hermes 0.20.0 (commit 33f8e96a72), desktop app, Python 3.12 - Platforms: WeChat (iLink), QQ Bot, Telegram (via local proxy) - `HERMES_DESKTOP=1` serve backend; gateway launched via `python.exe -m hermes_cli.main gateway run`
signals.author: zuowen7

signals.title: ACP adapter: turns ending in text_response are silently dropped on Buzz-connected sessions (never published to relay)
signals.text: # ACP adapter: turns ending in `text_response` are silently dropped on Buzz-connected sessions (never published to relay) ## Summary On a Buzz-connected ACP persona ("Leo", running as a systemd-managed `buzz-acp-leo.service`), a conversation turn that ended with `reason=text_response` (i.e. the model's final output was plain assistant text with no accompanying tool call) was silently lost — never published to the Nostr relay, never retried, and never logged as an error. The user received no reply for 47 minutes and the ~1897-character status update is permanently unrecoverable. Turns that end via an explicit tool call (e.g. a "send to Buzz" action) are delivered correctly and logged as such, which strongly suggests the ACP↔Buzz bridge only treats tool-call-driven sends as requiring an explicit relay-publish step, and silently drops bare `text_response` turns. ## Environment - Hermes Agent, ACP adapter mode (`buzz-acp` persona integration) - Persona: "Leo", running as systemd service `buzz-acp-leo.service` on a self-hosted Hetzner box - Transport: Buzz relay (self-hosted), Nostr protocol backend for message publish/subscribe - Observed: 2026-08-12, via `journalctl -u buzz-acp-leo.service` ## Steps to Reproduce / Conditions Observed Not yet reproduced on demand — this is a single confirmed incident reconstructed from production logs. Condensed timeline (all UTC, 2026-08-12): 1. **01:45:26** — Leo sends a DM committing to two tracks of work ("On it. Splitting into two tracks: ..."). 2. **01:46:44** — New conversation turn begins, session `20260812_014644_fc0f12`, executing track 1. 3. **01:52:13** — Track 1 completes successfully: a review request is sent via an explicit tool call to a ticket-lane channel (confirmed via tool-call log line, event `fcbdf2cc...`). **This confirms the normal send path works when a turn ends via an explicit tool call.** 4. **01:55:57** — API call #13 completes (in=134509, out=676 tokens, latency=11.2s, cache=99%). Immediately followed by: `Turn ended: reason=text_response(finish_reason=stop) ... response_len=1897 session=20260812_014644_fc0f12` — the agent composed a ~1897-character status update as plain text, with **no tool call**. 5. **01:55:57 → 01:56:28** (31s, relay connection healthy) — **no publish/send/outbound log line appears anywhere** for this response. Delivery was never even attempted. 6. **01:56:28 → 02:20:39** — Unrelated relay websocket disconnect ("no pong received within 10s — connection dead, reconnecting"), ~24 min outage. Confirmed **coincidental, not causal** — the response vanished 31s *before* this outage began, while the connection was still up. 7. **02:20:39** — Relay reconnects and resubscribes to channels. No queue-flush, resend, or retry of the missing message occurs in the following 15+ minutes. 8. **Ground truth check** — Direct fetch of the DM channel from the relay shows nothing from Leo between 01:45:26 and 02:32:59 (47 minutes of silence). Human (Nick) pinged at 01:50:42 ("I don't understand. Are you working or not?") with no reply logged. Only after a second nag at 02:32:33 did Leo produce a **new, differently-worded** reply — not a delayed delivery of the original. The original 1897-char update is permanently lost with no trace, no error, no retry. ## Expected vs Actual Behavior **Expected:** Any final assistant response intended for the user — regardless of whether the turn ends via a tool call or via plain `text_response` — is published to the Buzz/Nostr relay, or a delivery failure is logged/retried/alerted. **Actual:** Turns ending in `reason=text_response` with no tool call appear to close without any publish attempt to the relay. No error, warning, or retry is logged. The message is silently and permanently dropped. ## Root Cause Analysis **Caveat: this is evidence-based inference from log analysis, not a traced code path.** We have not stepped through the actual ACP adapter / Buzz bridge source to confirm the exact mechanism — treat the following as a strong hypothesis, not a confirmed diagnosis. The pattern observed is consistent with the ACP↔Buzz bridge only wiring an explicit "publish to relay" action to tool-call-based sends (e.g. a `send_to_buzz`-style tool), while turns that end purely on `text_response` (plain final assistant text, `finish_reason=stop`, no tool call) are not recognized by the bridge as requiring an outbound publish at all. No error is raised because — from the adapter's perspective — nothing went wrong; it simply never routed that text anywhere. Likely candidate code areas (unverified, offered as starting points for investigation): - `acp_adapter/server.py` — turn completion / response handling - `buzz_acp` Rust relay client — outbound publish invocation sites - `agent/turn_finalizer.py` (or equivalent) — specifically the `text_response` finish-reason branch ## Related Issues This matches a broader known bug class already partially tracked upstream — same failure symptom (final assistant response generated but never delivered), different transport in each case: - **#10748** — "streaming mode silently drops final response when `already_sent` is true" (response stored in DB, never delivered). Same failure class; different transport (streaming path, not ACP/Buzz). - **#31884** — Telegram gateway can silently drop a turn with `response=0 chars` while internal work continues. Same failure class; Telegram gateway, not ACP/Buzz. - **#31588** — Messages sent while agent is busy get silently queued with no feedback. Related failure mode (silent loss of user-facing signal) but different trigger condition. Filing this as a **new issue** rather than a comment on #10748 because the transport and adapter code involved (ACP adapter, Buzz relay client, `text_response` turn-finalization path) is distinct from whatever code #10748/#31884/#31588 cover — but cross-linking all three here since they may share a root cause or fix pattern (i.e. "final response delivery must not depend on which finish_reason ended the turn"). ## Suggested Fix (suggestions only — not implemented or tested) **(a) Route text_response through the same explicit publish mechanism as tool-call sends.** For ACP/Buzz-bound sessions, make the bare "turn ends in plain text" case invoke the same explicit publish/send call used by tool-call-based sends, so there is no code path where a text-ending turn can complete without an outbound relay event being attempted. **(b) Add a post-turn delivery integrity check.** If a Buzz-bound session's turn ends with `reason=text_response` and no corresponding outbound Nostr event is emitted within a short window (e.g. a few seconds), log an ERROR and either retry the publish or alert, rather than allowing the turn to close silently. Either approach (or both, as belt-and-suspenders) would have caught this incident — (a) prevents the drop, (b) would have at minimum surfaced it as a visible error instead of 47 minutes of silent user-facing failure. ## Reproduction Status **Not reproduced on demand.** This report is based entirely on `journalctl` log analysis of a live production instance (`buzz-acp-leo.service`) after the incident was noticed via user complaint ("I don't understand. Are you working or not?"). No isolated repro case has been constructed yet. Happy to assist with building one if adapter maintainers can point to the relevant turn-finalization code, or if there's a known way to force a turn to end in `finish_reason=stop` with no tool call in a Buzz-connected test session.

signals.title: Desktop: same assistant message rendered twice in chat view (DB stores single record; frontend rendering issue)
signals.text: ## Summary In the Hermes Desktop app (Windows), an assistant message occasionally appears **twice** in the chat view. The message is stored **once** in `state.db` (no duplicate rows, no duplicate IDs), which points to a **frontend rendering-layer** issue rather than storage/sync duplication. ## Observed in two independent sessions (same day) 1. Session analyzing CGM (continuous glucose monitor) data, 2026-08-13 afternoon: a long assistant reply (blood-glucose meal analysis) rendered twice in the scrollback. 2. Session "境外手机号必要性分析" (overseas phone number analysis), 2026-08-13 13:24 UTC+8: same duplicate display behavior. Both are local desktop sessions (no Telegram/Discord/etc. delivery involved). ## Investigation already done (user-side) - `state.db` → `messages` table: the duplicated assistant reply exists as **exactly 1 row**; `SELECT id, COUNT(*) FROM messages GROUP BY id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1` returns **0 rows** across all 11k+ messages. → Storage layer is clean. - `platform_message_id` is NULL for local desktop sessions → no external delivery layer involved. → Delivery layer is clean. - The affected session's model (deepseek direct, no provider fallback involved) shows **no** `No response from provider` / `stream drop` / `Reconnecting` entries in `desktop.log` around the incident → not caused by provider stream-reconnect re-rendering (an earlier hypothesis involving an unrelated background review task that uses a different model via OpenRouter was investigated and ruled out — the GLM-5.2 timeout in the log belonged to that background task, not the affected session). - Only GUI-related log noise: benign `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` messages from the renderer. ## Expected behavior Each assistant message appears exactly once in the chat view. ## Actual behavior The same message content is rendered twice, both copies visible in the conversation scrollback (appear to share the same/very close timestamp). Restarting the app clears the duplicate (memory-state rendering issue). ## Environment - OS: Windows 10 - Hermes Desktop (Electron app), backend commit `f5be9236` (2026-08-04) - Provider: deepseek direct for main conversation; openrouter only for auxiliary tasks (approval / background_review) ## Suggested debugging direction Most likely in the frontend message-list rendering: React list key collisions, virtualized-list duplicate append, or overlap between the initial API-fetched history and a live WebSocket push of the same message (duplicate insertion on merge). Reproduces intermittently. A pointer to where the chat message list merges API-fetched history with live-streamed messages would help narrow it down. Happy to provide more logs or run a debug build if useful.
signals.author: Waveearth

signals.title: [Bug]: An interrupted command adopts another session's working directory
signals.text: ### Bug Description A chat adopts the working directory of a different chat. This happens after a command in the first chat is interrupted or times out. Every later command in that chat then runs in the other chat's directory. The command wrapper prints the `__HERMES_CWD_*` marker after the command returns (`tools/environments/base.py:924`). A killed command never prints it, so `env.cwd` still holds the directory of the last command that FINISHED. One local environment serves every session. `_resolve_container_task_id` (`tools/terminal_tool.py:1384`) collapses cwd-only overrides to `"default"`. The leftover directory in `env.cwd` is therefore routinely another session's. The post-command dual-write (`tools/terminal_tool.py:3315`) copies `env.cwd` into the interrupted session's durable record. The cwd echo (`tools/terminal_tool.py:3422`) reads the same value and reports a move to the model. Both trust a directory that the command never reported. One session alone is sufficient to show this defect. A single session that interrupts a command also adopts a stale value. A second session only makes the wrong directory belong to another user of the app. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Open two desktop chats against one backend. 2. In chat A, run `cd /some/worktree && pwd`. Let it finish. 3. In chat B, run a long command such as `cd /other/dir && sleep 20`. 4. Interrupt the command in chat B, or let it time out. 5. In chat B, run `pwd`. This script reproduces the defect without the app: ```python import os, sys, tempfile sys.path.insert(0, ".") os.environ.pop("TERMINAL_ENV", None) import tools.terminal_tool as tt from tools.environments.local import LocalEnvironment repo = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="repo_") other = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="otherchat_") env = LocalEnvironment(cwd=os.path.expanduser("~"), timeout=30) env.init_session() def run(session_key, command, timeout=30): cwd = tt._resolve_command_cwd(workdir=None, default_cwd=env.cwd, session_key=session_key, env_type="local") r = env.execute(command, cwd=cwd, timeout=timeout) tt.record_session_cwd(session_key, getattr(env, "cwd", None)) return r run("mine", f"cd {repo} && pwd") run("other", f"cd {other} && pwd") run("mine", f"cd {repo} && sleep 20", timeout=2) # interrupted print("my record:", tt.get_session_cwd("mine")) print("expected :", repo) ``` ### Expected Behavior Chat B keeps its own directory. An interrupted command reports no directory, so the session keeps the directory that it already had. ### Actual Behavior Chat B adopts the directory of chat A. ``` shared env.cwd after other chat: /tmp/…/otherchat_4tfd78l7 my interrupted command: {'out': '[Command timed out after 2s]', 'exit': 124} my record became : /tmp/…/otherchat_4tfd78l7 <-- the other chat (repo was : /tmp/…/repo_217_imog ) ``` The live occurrence in the desktop app: chat `20260812_162559_09bcbf` worked in `.worktrees/ethie-desktop-bundles` and completed commands at t=1786644615.6 and t=1786644629.3. My chat ran `cd ~/src/hermes-agent && grep -rln …`, and the user interrupted it at t=1786644631.9. My record adopted the other chat's worktree, and `pwd` reported that worktree for the rest of the session. ### Affected Component Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.) ### Environment - OS: NixOS (Linux 7.1.0) - Surface: Desktop app, local backend - Commit: `ac9b9f54c` ### Notes The record store already carries a comment about this class of error (`tools/terminal_tool.py:1180`). It states that cwd state on the shared environment is a global that sessions timeshare. The write path still reads from that global. The docstring at `tools/terminal_tool.py:3303` claims that the record "never depends on the shared env surviving". That claim is true for a completed command and false for an interrupted one.

signals.title: [Bug]: hermes config set agent.reasoning_effort emits a false unrecognized-key warning
signals.text: ### Bug Description `agent.reasoning_effort` is a documented and runtime-consumed configuration key, but setting it through `hermes config set` emits an unrecognized-key warning. The value is still saved to `config.yaml` and returned by `hermes config get`, so the problem is the false warning rather than persistence or runtime behavior. This report concerns the scalar global key `agent.reasoning_effort`, not the per-model `agent.reasoning_overrides` mapping. The documentation only excludes nested `reasoning_overrides` entries from `hermes config set` because model names may contain dots. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Run: ```shell hermes config set agent.reasoning_effort high ``` 2. Observe the warning. 3. Confirm that the value was saved: ```shell hermes config get agent.reasoning_effort ``` ### Expected Behavior Because `agent.reasoning_effort` is a documented and runtime-supported key, it should be saved without an unrecognized-key warning. If `/reasoning high --global` is intentionally the only supported setter, the CLI should direct users to that command instead of saying Hermes may not read the saved value. ### Actual Behavior The value is saved, ```text ✓ Set agent.reasoning_effort = high in <config path> ``` but the CLI prints: ```text ⚠ 'agent.reasoning_effort' is not a recognized config key — it was saved anyway, but Hermes may not read it. Did you mean: agent.reasoning_overrides ``` `hermes config get agent.reasoning_effort` subsequently returns: ```text high ``` ### Affected Component CLI (interactive chat), Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup) ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) N/A (CLI only) ### Debug Report ```shell hermes debug share output can be attached if needed. ``` ### Operating System Debian 13 ### Python Version 3.13.5 ### Hermes Version 0.20.0 ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) _No response_ ### Proposed Fix (optional) _No response_ ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR
