signals.title: [Bug]: hermes update stalls at autostash restore prompt on macOS — post-update gateway restart never runs, gateway serves stale code
signals.text: ## Summary On macOS, `hermes update` can stall at the autostash-restore interactive prompt ("Restore local changes now? [Y/n]"). When that happens the process never reaches the post-update gateway-restart block, so a launchd-supervised gateway keeps running with pre-update modules in memory while lazily importing post-update code from disk — a mixed/stale runtime that fails later with confusing errors. ## Environment - macOS (launchd-managed gateway, `ai.hermes.gateway`) - Direct upstream checkout (NOT a fork — the #73108 fork case is a different trigger) - Hermes v0.20.0 (2026.8.3), updated 2026-08-13 to `fa83af3f9` ## Observed timeline (from ~/.hermes/logs/update.log and gateway-exit-diag.log) 1. `2026-08-13T22:25:06` — `hermes update` starts. Local changes detected → autostash created (`hermes-update-autostash-20260813-142640`). Found 4231 new commits, pulled them. 2. Update prints the restore prompt and **stalls there**. `update.log` ends at `Restore local changes now? [Y/n]` — no further output. The stash entry is still present afterwards (`git stash list` shows `stash@{0}: On main: hermes-update-autostash-20260813-142640`), i.e. the update never completed its restore step, hence never reached the restart block. 3. The gateway process (PID 20465, started 2026-08-13 21:45) kept running on the pre-update code for ~12 hours. 4. `2026-08-14 01:40:22 UTC` — gateway exits non-zero (`gateway.exit_nonzero` in gateway-exit-diag.log), 30s later a manual `launchctl kickstart -k` brings it back on the new code. Only then does the mixed-runtime error go away. The same autostash pattern also appears at 07-25 and 05-20 (older `hermes-update-autostash-*` entries), suggesting the prompt regularly stalls when the update runs in a context where stdin is not attended (e.g. run from an IDE/terminal that closed, or a non-interactive wrapper). ## Root cause In `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py`, `_restore_stashed_changes()` blocks on `input()` (or `_gateway_prompt`) before the gateway-restart block in `_cmd_update_impl()` runs. If the prompt never gets a response (closed stdin, unattended terminal, EOF handling paths), the update either hangs or takes the skip-restore path and the **gateway fleet restart is skipped entirely** — there is no timeout on the prompt and no "restart gateways even though restore was skipped" guarantee. The post-update restart logic exists (launchd/systemd/manual-PID branches, added around 84a875ca0 / 988ecc742) but it is downstream of an interactive prompt that can block indefinitely. Related: #73108 is the same symptom family (post-update restart skipped) but triggered by the fork "Already up to date" early-exit; its fix PR #73679 is still open. This report is the direct-upstream counterpart: the restart is skipped whenever the update path is interrupted before the restart block, and the autostash prompt is one such interruption point. ## Expected behavior - The post-update gateway restart should run even when stash restore is skipped or times out (restart is independent of restore). - The autostash prompt should have a timeout / non-interactive default so an unattended `hermes update` does not hang mid-update with a gateway left on stale code. - At minimum, when a running gateway could not be restarted, print explicit guidance (the managed-runtime repair path already does this with "Restart required to finish..." — plain source-tree updates emit neither a warning nor a restart). ## Workaround Manually restart the launchd service after every `hermes update` (e.g. kickstart the `ai.hermes.gateway` label), or chain the restart onto the update command.
signals.author: Feahter

signals.title: session_search discovery hides ALL hits from the current session's own /new-reset lineage (gateway recall goes blind)
signals.text: ## Summary In gateway conversations (QQ/Telegram/etc.), every `/new` creates a child session via `parent_session_id`. `session_search` discovery excludes any hit whose lineage root equals the *current* session's lineage root (`tools/session_search_tool.py`, the `current_lineage_root == lineage_root` guard), on the assumption that same-lineage content is already in the active context. That assumption holds for compression continuations but is false for manual `/new` resets, which carry no transcript. Result: after each `/new`, the agent cannot recall *any* previous session of the same chat — `session_search` returns 0 results even though messages, FTS, and vector indexes are all intact. ## Reproduction (real state.db) Chain: `20260812_152906` → child `20260813_083223` → child `20260814_083525` (current). - `session_search(query="布洛芬")` from the current session → **0 results** - Direct SQL on the same DB: `messages_fts_trigram MATCH '布洛芬'` → 12 rows, all joined correctly to `20260813_083223` - Browse mode (`session_search()` with no args) shows only cron sessions, because every recent interactive session has a `parent_session_id` and is skipped Concrete user impact: the user asked the agent "do you remember what we talked about last night?" — the agent searched, got 0 results, and wrongly concluded no conversation had happened, when in fact a full 167-message session existed. ## Root cause - Discovery guard: `tools/session_search_tool.py` (~L641) `if current_lineage_root and lineage_root == current_lineage_root: continue` - Browse skip: (~L451) `if s.get("parent_session_id"): continue` - `_resolve_lineage()` already computes `has_compression_hop` to distinguish compression splits from other children, but both guards ignore it and treat all lineage children as in-context. ## Expected behavior The current-lineage exclusion should apply only when the lineage hop is a compression continuation (content actually carried forward). `/new`-reset children should be discoverable and browsable like any other session. ## Related, not duplicate - #82988 — browse drops resumed conversations (the list-side symptom) - #6507 — child hit summarized at the lineage root (the transcript-side symptom) - This one is the *current-lineage exclusion* — a third defect in the same neighborhood.
signals.author: Lavinia-ai

signals.title: [Bug]: PermissionError in _find_git_root() crashes system prompt building for gateway-mode agents
signals.text: ### Bug Description When an agent runs via hermes gateway run -p <profile>, the gateway bridges config.yaml’s terminal.cwd into the TERMINAL_CWD environment variable. During system prompt construction, build_context_files_prompt() calls resolve_context_cwd() which reads TERMINAL_CWD, then passes it to _find_git_root(Path(cwd)). If terminal.cwd points to a directory the agent process user cannot access (e.g., /root on a server where the agent runs as a non-root user like kduser), _find_git_root() crashes with: PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root/.git' This causes the entire system prompt build to fail, and the agent responds with “Sorry, I encountered an unexpected error” on every message. ### Steps to Reproduce Set terminal.cwd: /root in a profile’s config.yaml (this is the Docker sandbox default on many setups) Ensure the gateway process runs as a non-root user (e.g., kduser) that cannot access /root Start the agent via hermes gateway run -p <profile> Send a message to the agent (via webhook, yunzhijia, or any messaging platform) Agent responds with “Sorry, I encountered an unexpected error” — check agent.log for PermissionError ### Expected Behavior _find_git_root() should gracefully handle PermissionError by treating inaccessible directories as “no .git found” and continuing the search (or returning None). The system prompt should build successfully regardless of whether the cwd is accessible. ### Actual Behavior Traceback (most recent call last): File "/var/lib/hermes-agent/agent/system_prompt.py", line 473, in build_system_prompt_parts context_files_prompt = _r.build_context_files_prompt( File "/var/lib/hermes-agent/agent/prompt_builder.py", line 2074, in build_context_files_prompt _load_hermes_md(cwd_path, context_length) File "/var/lib/hermes-agent/agent/prompt_builder.py", line 1921, in _load_hermes_md hermes_md_path = _find_hermes_md(cwd_path) File "/var/lib/hermes-agent/agent/prompt_builder.py", line 100, in _find_hermes_md stop_at = _find_git_root(cwd) File "/var/lib/hermes-agent/agent/prompt_builder.py", line 85, in _find_git_root if (parent / ".git").exists(): File "/usr/lib/python3.11/pathlib.py", line 1236, in exists self.stat() File "/usr/lib/python3.11/pathlib.py", line 1014, in stat return os.stat(self, follow_symlinks=follow_symlinks) PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root/.git' ### Affected Component Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp) ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) N/A (CLI only) ### Debug Report ```shell <!-- Run hermes debug share and paste links here --> ``` ### Operating System Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (5.15.0-179-generic) ### Python Version Python 3.11.x ### Hermes Version v0.19.0 (git: v2026.7.20-995-ga61183b56f) ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell See Actual Behavior above for full traceback. ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) agent/prompt_builder.py, line 85, in _find_git_root(): def _find_git_root(start: Path) -> Optional[Path]: current = start.resolve() for parent in [current, *current.parents]: if (parent / ".git").exists(): # ← .exists() raises PermissionError on inaccessible dirs return parent return None Path.exists() calls os.stat(), which raises PermissionError when the directory itself is not accessible — not just when .git doesn’t exist. The function has no try/except PermissionError. Why it only affects gateway mode: gateway/run.py bridges config.yaml’s terminal.cwd into os.environ["TERMINAL_CWD"] (line ~2072-2087). resolve_context_cwd() in system_prompt.py reads TERMINAL_CWD and passes it to build_context_files_prompt(cwd=...). In CLI/Web UI mode, TERMINAL_CWD is not set, so resolve_context_cwd() returns None and build_context_files_prompt falls back to os.getcwd() — which is typically the user’s accessible home directory. Why /root: Docker sandbox deployments commonly set terminal.cwd: /root (the container’s default home). This works inside the container (overlay filesystem), but the gateway process runs on the host as a non-root user who cannot access /root. Verified: upstream origin/main also unfixed — same code without try/except PermissionError. ### Proposed Fix (optional) def _find_git_root(start: Path) -> Optional[Path]: current = start.resolve() for parent in [current, *current.parents]: try: if (parent / ".git").exists(): return parent except PermissionError: continue return None One-line try/except PermissionError — skip inaccessible directories, return None if no .git found. ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR
signals.author: shamolvshu

signals.title: [Feature]: Bridge $currentProvider into host.state so plugins can show the live provider
signals.text: ## Summary The plugin SDK bridges the live model (`host.state.model`) but not the live provider, even though the app store holds it (`$currentProvider`). A status-bar plugin that shows `provider · model` at a glance (to catch misconfigured provider kicks) therefore displays the *configured* provider, not the one actually selected for the session. ## Repro 1. Install a status-bar plugin reading `host.state.model` + `config.get {key:'full'}` → `config.model.provider` (the standard recipe). 2. Open the model picker and select provider `nous`, model `longcat`. 3. The pill updates to `… · longcat` (model is bridged) but the provider segment still shows the configured default (`opencode-go`). Expected: the pill shows `nous · longcat` — the pair the user actually selected. ## Why The picker writes **two separate atoms** (`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-model-controls.ts:183-184`): ```ts setCurrentModel(selection.model) setCurrentProvider(selection.provider) ``` but `host.state` bridges only one of them (`apps/desktop/src/sdk/index.ts:59-73`): ```ts state: { activeSessionId: readonlyAtom<null | string>($activeSessionId), cwd: readonlyAtom<string>($currentCwd), gateway: readonlyAtom<string>($gatewayState), /** Current main model slug. */ model: readonlyAtom<string>($currentModel), profile: readonlyAtom<string>($activeGatewayProfile), viewport: readonlyAtom<ViewportRect>($viewport) } ``` The provider atom exists and is persisted (`apps/desktop/src/store/session.ts:569`): ```ts export const $currentProvider = atom(storedString(COMPOSER_PROVIDER_KEY) ?? '') ``` Plugins have no RPC door to it either (the `/api/model/info` bridge endpoint is desktop-bridge-only, not reachable from a plugin). ## Proposed fix Mirror the `model` atom — add to `host.state`: ```ts /** Current main provider slug. */ provider: readonlyAtom<string>($currentProvider), ``` The import for `$currentProvider` is already in the SDK module's dependency chain (same store file as `$currentModel`). ~3 lines, no behavioral change for existing plugins (additive surface). ## Notes - The composer's own UI reads the same `$currentProvider` atom (`model-picker-overlay.tsx:26`), so the value bridged would be exactly what the picker shows. - Per-session overrides (tile/session-scoped picks) write the same atoms via `sessionTileDelegate().updateSession(…)` confirm path — the bridge would reflect the primary session the way `model` already does.
signals.author: exergonic

signals.title: fix(desktop): local profile switch reuses default socket after update
signals.text: ## Summary After a recent Desktop update, selecting any local named profile from the profile rail can leave Desktop attached to the default profile. The named backend starts successfully, but Desktop never opens its persistent WebSocket and continues using the primary/default socket. This affects current `main` and makes local multi-profile switching appear inert: the profile is selectable, but the sidebar/active agent remains on the same profile. ## Environment - Hermes Desktop on macOS 26.6.1 (Apple silicon) - Local primary profile: `default` - Local named profile: `fiction-writer` - Reproduced from current `main` around `486f4ace20ba75401681c0915ab79a0968fa6bb1` - Confirmed still present after fetching current `origin/main` ## Reproduction 1. Configure Desktop with the local `default` profile and at least one local named profile. 2. Launch Desktop on `default`. 3. Select the named profile from the profile rail. 4. Observe that the named backend starts and passes the one-shot WebSocket probe. 5. Observe that no persistent WebSocket is opened for the named profile and the Desktop context remains attached to the primary/default socket. ## Expected behavior A local named profile should use its own pooled backend and persistent WebSocket. The sidebar, sessions, model, tools, and agent context should move to that profile. ## Actual behavior The local pooled descriptor is mistaken for a shared-primary descriptor. Desktop reuses the primary/default socket instead of dialing the named profile's pooled backend. Representative log sequence: ```text Starting Hermes backend for profile "fiction-writer" ... HERMES_BACKEND_READY port=64271 Hermes backend listening on 127.0.0.1:64271 ... tui_gateway.ws: ws accepted ... tui_gateway.ws: ws closed ... messages=0 ``` The accepted/closed connection is the startup probe. There is no subsequent persistent profile WebSocket. ## Root cause `apps/desktop/src/store/gateway.ts::sharedPrimaryRoute()` currently treats the presence of `connection.profile` as proof that the descriptor uses the shared primary backend: ```ts return Boolean(conn && typeof conn === 'object' && (conn as { profile?: string }).profile) ``` However, `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts::spawnPoolBackend()` intentionally returns `profile` for local pooled descriptors as well. That profile value is needed so fresh WebSocket URL minting targets the correct backend. Therefore both of these descriptors carry `profile`: - a profile scoped onto the shared primary backend; - a dedicated local/remote pooled backend. The discriminator conflates those two routes. `ensureGatewayForProfile()` then takes the shared-primary branch for a local pool profile and never dials its socket. ## Proposed fix Add an explicit `sharedPrimary` marker only when `ensureBackend()` returns a profile-scoped primary descriptor, and make `sharedPrimaryRoute()` check that marker rather than inferring route ownership from `profile`. A regression test should assert both sides of the invariant: - `{ profile, sharedPrimary: true }` activates the primary socket; - a pooled descriptor carrying `{ profile }` still dials its own socket. ## Verification The proposed patch was tested locally: ```text Test Files 2 passed (2) Tests 13 passed (13) ``` Commands: ```bash cd apps/desktop npm test -- --run src/store/gateway-shared-remote.test.ts src/store/profile.test.ts npm run typecheck npm run pack ``` After installing the rebuilt package and restarting Desktop, switching between `default` and the local named profile works normally again.
signals.author: wdon

signals.title: [Bug]: grok-4.6 reasoning effort silently dropped; max/ultra 400 on send path
signals.text: ## Bug Description When using an xAI OAuth account (grok-4.6 / grok-4.5), the reasoning-effort setting is either **silently ignored** or **hard-fails the request with HTTP 400**, depending on the level chosen. Two distinct defects on the send path (not the picker): **A. `grok-4.6` is missing from the `grok_supports_reasoning_effort` allowlist** (`agent/model_metadata.py`, ~line 555). Any effort selected for grok-4.6 is never attached to the request at all — the UI shows a choice that has zero effect. Verified live against `api.x.ai` (`/v1/responses`): grok-4.6 **accepts** `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`. **B. Unsupported levels (`max`, `ultra`) are sent verbatim and fail the whole request** with `400 Invalid reasoning effort`. There is no per-model clamp on the send path — only a hard-coded xAI map in `agent/transports/codex.py` that predates 4.6 (it folds `xhigh`→`high`, which is wrong for 4.6) and is not driven by model metadata. Also: grok-4.6 **cannot disable thinking** (`reasoning: {effort: none}` / `thinking.disabled` unsupported), yet the picker offers an Off toggle. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure Hermes with an xAI OAuth account, select `grok-4.6`. 2. Set reasoning effort to `high` in the desktop model menu. 3. Inspect the outgoing request body: no `reasoning.effort` field at all (allowlist miss → silently dropped). Expected: `reasoning: {effort: "high"}`. 4. Set effort to `max` or `ultra` (e.g. a pre-existing saved value): request fails with `400 {"error": "Invalid reasoning effort"}` — the entire turn is lost. ## Expected Behavior - Every model auto-reports its **real** supported effort levels (from models.dev `reasoning_options`), the picker shows exactly those, and the send path **clamps** any stored value to the nearest supported level — no silent drops, no 400s. - Models whose `reasoning_options` include a `toggle` (e.g. DeepSeek) get the Off switch; models like grok-4.6 that cannot turn thinking off do not. ## Actual Behavior - `grok_supports_reasoning_effort` allowlist in `agent/model_metadata.py` predates grok-4.6 → effort silently dropped. - `agent/transports/codex.py` hard-codes an outdated xAI effort map (folds `xhigh`→`high`; no catalog-driven clamp) → `max`/`ultra` reach the wire and 400. - Picker always renders the full 7-level Hermes scale (`minimal…ultra`) + Off toggle, regardless of the model (this half is being addressed by #85246). ## Live-Verified Effort Matrix (grok-4.6, api.x.ai /v1/responses) | effort | result | |---|---| | minimal / low / medium / high / xhigh | accepted | | max / ultra | **400 Invalid reasoning effort** | | none / thinking.disabled | unsupported — model still reasons | ## Root Cause `agent/model_metadata.py` `grok_supports_reasoning_effort()`: hard-coded model-name allowlist, not updated for grok-4.6. `agent/transports/codex.py`: effort handling has a static xAI-only map; no shared "allowed efforts for this model" concept. Both stem from discarding models.dev `reasoning_options` after parsing only the `reasoning` bool — the exact level list is available in the catalog and thrown away. ## Proposed Fix Data-driven, no hand-maintained allowlist: 1. `agent/models_dev.py`: parse `reasoning_options` into `ModelCapabilities.reasoning_efforts` (filtered to Hermes' scale) + `thinking_off` (has `toggle` / `none`). 2. `hermes_cli/inventory.py` `_apply_capabilities`: carry `reasoning_efforts` / `thinking_off` into the model-options payload (picker side, complements #85246). 3. `agent/models_dev.py` `clamp_reasoning_effort(effort, allowed)`: nearest-neighbor clamp for the send path; unknown models fall back to the full Hermes scale (current behavior). 4. `agent/transports/codex.py`: clamp the wire value to the model's catalog efforts before sending; drop the stale hard-coded xAI map. 5. Desktop picker renders only `reasoning_efforts`, and hides the Off toggle when `thinking_off=false` (complements #85246). Local implementation exists and passes: pytest 108/108 (incl. new `tests/agent/test_reasoning_options.py`), vitest 11/11, `tsc --noEmit` clean. ## Related - #85246 (picker-side filtering — complements this) - #85683 (xAI picker refresh / pin grok-4.6) - #85153 (reasoning_effort: none mishandled for non-reasoning models — same family)
signals.author: PIXYGuo

signals.title: Prefer more official features as plugins to keep Hermes core minimal
signals.text: ## Summary Hermes already shows a strong direction I like: the core stays compact, while platform adapters, business flows, UI panes, and complex skills move into plugins. I would like the team to push this further so the default experience stays simple, and extra capabilities are explicitly opt-in. ## Why - A minimal core is easier to maintain, audit, and run. - Pluginized features can ship, roll back, and evolve independently. - Users can compose only the surfaces they actually need. ## Requested direction 1. Prefer pluginizing platform adapters, message-driven business modes, heavy UI surfaces, and expensive skills. 2. Keep core focused on runtime, sessions, memory, tool protocol, and security boundaries. 3. Make plugin discoverability and enablement clearer in docs and Desktop. ## Examples I like - Hermes-Bot-Mode as a Desktop plugin instead of a core UI change - Telegram Business Mode as an opt-in plugin - Separate plugin/skill/tool packages for heavy integrations ## Impact - Simpler default install - Lower maintenance surface in core - More modular user experience - Clearer upgrade path for optional capabilities
signals.author: HEROISM-WQL

signals.title: [Bug] Hermes Desktop (Linux/Wayland): image paste fails — clipboard image offered as application/octet-stream not recognized
signals.text: ## Bug Description Pasting a screenshot/image into the **Hermes desktop app** fails on a COSMIC/Wayland Linux desktop in every paste method (Ctrl+V, right-click paste, "paste image"), even though the system clipboard correctly holds the image and attaching the same image via the file picker / drag-and-drop works fine. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Press PrtScn (or capture with the COSMIC screenshot tool) to copy a screenshot. 2. Open the Hermes desktop app chat box. 3. Try to attach the image by pasting: Ctrl+V, right-click > paste, or the "+ / paste image" action. 4. Observe: a toast "No image found in clipboard" appears and the image does not attach. 5. As a control: attach the *same* image via the + file picker or drag-and-drop — it attaches correctly. ## Expected Behavior Copying an image (screenshot) to the system clipboard and pasting it into the Hermes desktop chat should attach the image, matching every other modern desktop app. ## Actual Behavior Image pasting fails with "No image found in clipboard"; only manual file attach works. ## Investigation / Root Cause Evidence - System clipboard holds the image fine: `wl-paste --list-types` shows the payload is offered as `application/octet-stream` (not `image/png`), and `wl-paste | od` returns valid PNG magic bytes (`89 50 4e 47`). - Hermes desktop's image-paste path is Electron `clipboard.readImage()` inside the IPC handler `hermes:saveClipboardImage` (`electron/main.ts`). Electron's `readImage()` only recognizes items advertised as `image/png`; an `octet-stream`-offered image returns empty, producing the `noClipboardImage` toast. - A patch adding a `wl-paste --type image/png` (and plain `wl-paste` + PNG-magic) fallback to that handler was built, deployed, and tested on the running app — it did NOT fix paste. This indicates the failure is not isolated to the clipboard-read layer but sits between the renderer paste event and the Electron main-process handler (the renderer's Ctrl+V paste path likely never invokes `saveClipboardImage` for an image-only clipboard). The patch was reverted. - The desktop app does not implement the `/paste` command (that is a CLI/TUI feature), so the documented reliable image-paste path is unavailable on desktop. ## Environment - OS: Pop!_OS 24.04 (COSMIC desktop), Wayland session (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`) - Hermes version: 0.20.0 (desktop app) - Electron main: `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` ## Suggested Direction Investigate the desktop renderer's paste handler (Electron desktop composer) so that a Wayland server offering an image-clipboard item as `application/octet-stream` is still recognized and attached (e.g., a fallback that shells out to `wl-paste` on Linux/Wayland, or broadening the accepted MIME types in `hermes:saveClipboardImage`).
signals.author: jasonswinney7466

signals.title: Custom providers not shared across profiles + no reliable add path in Desktop/CLI
signals.text: ## Summary Adding a custom provider is painful and inconsistent across profiles and surfaces. Three related problems: ### 1. Custom providers are not propagated to other profiles When I add a custom provider in one profile (e.g. `default`), it does **not** appear in my other profiles (`coding-agent`, `telegram`). There is no "apply to all profiles" option. To use the same custom provider everywhere I have to manually copy the `providers:` / `custom_providers:` block and the API key into every profile's `config.yaml` and `.env` by hand. This is error-prone (I ended up with mismatched provider names between profiles) and defeats the purpose of having isolated-but-shareable profiles. Expected: a custom provider added once should be selectable in every profile, or there should be a clear "copy provider to profile X" / "apply to all profiles" action. ### 2. No working way to add a custom provider from Desktop app or CLI - **Desktop app:** the "add custom provider" UI hangs / appears to succeed but then reports the provider is "already added" even when it is not present in the active profile's config. The provider never actually shows up in the model/provider picker. - **CLI:** `hermes config set` cannot be trusted for nested keys — it appends a duplicate top-level block instead of editing the existing key (tracked separately in #71047, still open). So there is no reliable CLI path to add a custom provider to a non-default profile either. Expected: a documented, working flow (`hermes model` picker, `hermes config`, or Desktop settings) to register a custom provider for the *currently active* profile. ### 3. Profile switching itself has open issues Related: #85777 (local profile switch reuses default socket after update) and #71047 (config set duplicates top-level key). Both make the multi-profile experience fragile, which amplifies problem #1. ## Environment - Hermes Agent: current `main` (pyproject ~0.20.x) - Platform: Windows 10 - Profiles: `default`, `coding-agent`, `telegram` - Custom providers involved: `9router` (local OpenAI-compatible endpoint `http://127.0.0.1:20128/v1`) and `AgentRouter` (`https://agentrouter.org/v1`) ## What I did (manual reproduction of the gap) 1. Registered `9router` + `AgentRouter` in `default` via Desktop app → worked there. 2. Switched to `coding-agent` / `telegram` → neither provider appeared in the picker. 3. Tried adding them again in the Desktop app for the active profile → UI hung / said "already added", nothing written to `config.yaml`. 4. Had to copy `providers:` and `custom_providers:` blocks + `.env` keys manually into each profile's files. ## Suggested improvement - Custom providers should be stored at a shared layer (or have an explicit "share with profile…" control) so they don't have to be re-added per profile. - Fix/provide a reliable add-custom-provider path in both the Desktop app and `hermes model` / `hermes config` (the Desktop "already added" hang and the `config set` duplicate-key bug must be resolved first).
signals.author: zoser69

signals.title: hermes skills update blocked when HERMES_HOME is a Windows junction (physical vs junction path mismatch)
signals.text: ## Summary `hermes skills update` fails for every skill when `HERMES_HOME` lives on a **Windows directory junction** (e.g. `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\hermes` → `D:\hermes`). All updates are blocked by the install-path validation with: ``` Installation blocked: 'D:\hermes\skills\<skill>' is not in the subpath of 'C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\hermes\skills' OR one path is relative and the other is absolute. ``` ## Environment - OS: Windows - Hermes: v0.20.0 (2026.8.3) - Python: 3.11.15 - `HERMES_HOME=C:\Users\xianff\AppData\Local\hermes` is a **junction** → `D:\hermes` ## Root cause When `HERMES_HOME` is a Windows junction, `Path.resolve()` in `_resolve_lock_install_path()` (tools/skills_hub.py) returns the **physical** path (`D:\hermes\skills\<skill>`), but the subsequent `is_relative_to()` / `relative_to()` comparison uses the **junction-form** skills dir (`C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\hermes\skills`). The drive-letter mismatch makes the check fail, so every `hermes skills update` is blocked — even though the skill is already installed and the target is legitimately inside the skills directory. This blocks the **update** path (`hermes skills update`). Related symptom also affects `hermes skills install` for new skills. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Set up `HERMES_HOME` under a Windows directory junction pointing to a physical dir on another drive (e.g. `mklink /J C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\hermes D:\hermes`). 2. Run `hermes skills check` → shows N skills `update_available`. 3. Run `hermes skills update`. 4. Every skill reports `Installation blocked: '<physical path>' is not in the subpath of '<junction path>'`. ## Expected behavior `hermes skills update` should update skills whose directory resolves (via junction/symlink) to a location inside the skills root — the junction is a legitimate filesystem layout, not a path escape. ## Related - PR #76885 "fix(skills): resolve install path against resolved skills dir (Windows junction)" — author's root-cause analysis matches this exactly, but it is **not yet merged** (blocked on requested E2E regression test). - #35674 — symlinked skills trigger false "outside trusted skills directory" warning (same junction/symlink resolution root cause). - #63369 — `hermes skills install` hit the same `subpath of` ValueError on Windows + git-bash.
signals.author: immortal111

signals.title: Add gateway.non_conversational guard for cron-only profiles
signals.text: Hermes supports cron-only gateway processes: a gateway with zero messaging platforms can still tick cron. For security-sensitive scheduled runners, operators need a first-class config option that makes a profile explicitly non-conversational and fails gateway startup if any messaging platform is enabled. Proposed shape: - config: `gateway.non_conversational: true` - startup behavior: before platform adapter creation, if any `platforms.*.enabled=true`, write `startup_failed` runtime status and exit with fatal config code - multiplex behavior: if the default gateway serves a secondary profile with `gateway.non_conversational=true` and any enabled platform, abort multiplexer startup with a config error - use case: split request intake from scheduled execution so conversational agents can record desired alerts while a separate cron-only profile runs them without any chat surface This avoids relying on documentation or systemd `ExecStartPre` alone, both of which are bypassable via direct `hermes --profile <name> gateway run`.
signals.author: michael-renjoy

signals.title: [Bug]: search_files fails on any pattern starting with "-" — missing "--" separator before the pattern (affects both the rg and grep paths)
signals.text: Summary search_files builds its shell command without the -- end-of-options separator before the pattern argument. Any search pattern that begins with - is therefore parsed as a flag by the underlying binary, and the search fails. This is not a quoting problem — _escape_shell_arg correctly wraps the pattern in single quotes, so the shell passes it as one argument. The issue is that rg/grep themselves treat a leading - as an option. The failure is silent from the agent's point of view: the tool returns total_count: 0 with an error string, and in an unattended context (cron job) the run still reports ok, so the model produces an incomplete answer that looks complete. Environment Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3) Install dir: /opt/hermes, Python 3.13.5 Docker (nousresearch/hermes-agent), Debian-based image ripgrep 14.1.1 at /usr/bin/rg (present and working) Reproduction Ask the agent to search for a Markdown task checkbox, which is an extremely common pattern in note vaults: search_files(pattern="- [ ]", path=".", target="content") Result: {"total_count": 0, "error": "Search failed: rg: unrecognized flag - "} Reproduced directly with the exact command shape the tool builds: $ rg --line-number --no-heading --with-filename '- [ ]' . rg: unrecognized flag - $ rg --line-number --no-heading --with-filename -- '- [ ]' . ./notes/Project.md:42:- [ ] pending task The grep fallback has the identical defect: $ grep -rnHE --exclude-dir='.*' '- [ ]' . grep: invalid option -- ' ' $ grep -rnHE --exclude-dir='.*' -- '- [ ]' . ./notes/Project.md:42:- [ ] pending task Root cause tools/file_operations.py, two places, both missing --: 1. _search_with_rg (defined at line 2543), lines 2572-2573: # Add pattern and path cmd_parts.append(self._escape_shell_arg(pattern)) cmd_parts.append(self._escape_shell_arg(path)) 2. _search_with_grep (defined at line 2684), lines 2708-2709: identical two lines. Suggested fix Insert the separator immediately before the pattern in both functions: # Add pattern and path. `--` stops option parsing so a pattern that # starts with "-" (e.g. the Markdown checkbox "- [ ]") is not read as a flag. cmd_parts.append("--") cmd_parts.append(self._escape_shell_arg(pattern)) cmd_parts.append(self._escape_shell_arg(path)) Both rg and GNU grep accept -- in that position, verified above. Impact Any pattern beginning with - is unsearchable. The most common real-world case is the Markdown task checkbox - [ ], plus list items, diff-style lines (-foo), and CLI flags being grepped for in code or logs. The failure mode matters as much as the failure. In a scheduled/cron context there is no user present to notice the tool error, the job still completes with status ok, and the delivered report is quietly missing whatever that search would have found. Workaround Escape the leading character so the pattern no longer starts with - — e.g. search \[ \] instead of - [ ]. This has to be enforced in the prompt, which is fragile: the model will "helpfully" revert to the natural pattern unless it is told why not to.
signals.author: MictlanPro

signals.title: feat(browser): support Camofox cookie import (#6109)
signals.text: Closes #6109. ## Summary Adds a new `browser_import_cookies` tool that imports Netscape-format `cookies.txt` files into a live Camofox session, so agents can authenticate to sites like LinkedIn or Amazon without interactive login every run. The upstream [camofox-browser](https://github.com/jo-inc/camofox-browser) already exposes `POST /sessions/:userId/cookies` with a Bearer-token auth gate; this PR wires that endpoint up on the Hermes side. ## What changed - **`tools/browser_camofox.py`** — new `_netscape_parse`, `_resolve_cookies_dir`, `_read_cookie_file`, and `camofox_import_cookies` functions. Parser mirrors upstream `lib/cookies.js` (BOM, `#HttpOnly_` prefix, CRLF, embedded-tab values). - **`tools/browser_tool.py`** — new `browser_import_cookies` delegate + schema entry + registry registration with a camofox-only `check_fn` so Browserbase / Firecrawl / agent-browser users don't see an unusable tool. - **`hermes_cli/config.py`** — two new env vars: `CAMOFOX_API_KEY` (secret) and `CAMOFOX_COOKIES_DIR`. - **`hermes_cli/tools_config.py`** — optional fields in the Camofox provider's setup flow. - **`tests/conftest.py`** — whitelist `CAMOFOX_COOKIES_DIR` in the hermetic-env fixture. - **Docs** — `website/docs/user-guide/features/browser.md` (new "Cookie import" section) and `website/docs/reference/environment-variables.md` (two rows). ## Safety rails - Paths are resolved strictly inside `CAMOFOX_COOKIES_DIR` — traversal (`../secret`) and absolute paths are rejected (`ValueError`). - 5 MB file cap and 500-cookie cap enforced **client-side** before the server request. - Cookie body sanitized to Playwright allowlist (`name`, `value`, `domain`, `path`, `expires`, `httpOnly`, `secure`, `sameSite`). - `CAMOFOX_API_KEY` registered with `password: True` so it gets redacted by downstream loaders. - Cookie values never logged — only counts + userId land in `hermes.log`. - Tool hidden from the schema unless `CAMOFOX_URL` is set (no cross-backend leakage). ## Test plan TDD throughout — 26 new tests, all green: - [x] `TestNetscapeParser` (7) — basic line, `#HttpOnly_`, comments, BOM, tab-embedded value, malformed-line skip, CRLF - [x] `TestReadCookieFile` (7) — in-dir read, `../` blocked, absolute-path blocked, 5MB cap, domain-suffix filter, missing file, default dir - [x] `TestCamofoxImportCookies` (8) — missing API key, Bearer header/body shape, field allowlist, 403/400 surfacing, 500-cookie cap, domain_suffix forwarding, empty-file error - [x] `TestBrowserImportCookiesRouting` (4) — delegation, non-camofox error, `check_fn` gating on/off - [x] `pytest tests/tools/test_browser_camofox.py tests/hermes_cli/test_config.py tests/hermes_cli/test_tools_config.py` → 128/128 pass Manual verification (run locally once camofox server is up): - [x] `openssl rand -hex 32` → set `CAMOFOX_API_KEY` on both server & Hermes - [x] Drop a real `cookies.txt` under `~/.camofox/cookies/` - [x] Ask the agent: "import my linkedin cookies and open feed" → expect authenticated session - [x] Unset `CAMOFOX_URL` → confirm tool disappears from schema ## References - Upstream spec: [jo-inc/camofox-browser README § Cookie Import](https://github.com/jo-inc/camofox-browser#cookie-import) - Upstream handler: `server.js:175-247` - Upstream parser mirrored in `tools/browser_camofox.py::_netscape_parse`

Closes a documentation gap: Hermes already ships the `copilot-acp` provider entry and the `agent/copilot_acp_client.py` shim, but there was no skill teaching the agent how to delegate work to GitHub Copilot CLI the way it does for the other coding agents. ## What's in the skill Three orchestration modes are documented end-to-end: 1. **ACP delegation (preferred)** — `delegate_task(acp_command="copilot")`, including `acp_args` overrides for `--allow-all-tools`, `--add-dir`, `--model`, `--effort`. 2. **Print mode** — `copilot -p ... --allow-all-tools --silent` for one-shot scripted runs from `terminal()`, with permission-pattern syntax (`shell(git:*)`, `write`, `url(...)`, `<mcp>(<tool>)`). 3. **Interactive TUI** — background + PTY pattern matching the `codex` / `opencode` skills, with the slash-command reference (`/init`, `/plan`, `/diff`, `/pr`, `/review`, `/research`, `/agent`, `/skills`, `/mcp`, `/model`, `/effort`, `/context`, `/share`, etc.). No new Python code is required because the ACP client shim already exists in the repo. ## Verification - Cross-checked the SKILL.md flag/env-var reference against `copilot --help`, `copilot help permissions`, and `copilot help environment` from `@github/copilot` (current release at the time of writing). - Verified the ACP transport path matches `agent/copilot_acp_client.py` (binary resolution + default args `['--acp', '--stdio']`). - Verified `delegate_task` honours `acp_command` / `acp_args` overrides via `tools/delegate_tool.py`. ## Files - `skills/autonomous-ai-agents/copilot-cli/SKILL.md` (new, 283 lines)

signals.title: fix(profiles): prevent credential leaks and SQLite data loss in exports
signals.text: ## Summary Current `main` includes #83458, which force-redacts recognized secret-shaped strings in supported text files before profile archives are written. That substantially reduces risk, but it does not fully enforce the profile-export security boundary. Named-profile exports still exclude only the exact files `auth.json` and `.env`. Backups, renamed credential stores, opaque authorization state, private-key formats, binary databases, and sensitive caller-supplied extras can still enter a portable archive without matching the text redactor. This PR complements #83458 by adding structural path/type filtering before archive creation while retaining its final text-scrubbing pass. ## What this fixes - Excludes renamed and backup credential files at every copy depth. - Excludes canonical OAuth, token, pairing, and profile-home credential trees. - Excludes private PEM, PuTTY `.ppk`, and keystore formats while preserving public certificates. - Blocks sensitive paths supplied through `extra_files`. - Covers Feishu pairing state, reason-labelled credential-directory backups, and Hermes-generated corrupt-config backups. - Scrubs every explicitly portable dotenv template. - Creates consistent snapshots of live `.db`, `.sqlite`, and `.sqlite3` databases before omitting WAL/SHM/journal sidecars. - Preserves safe negative controls such as public certificates, ordinary same-named directories, desktop metadata, and non-sensitive rules files. ## Security impact Profile exports are intended to be portable and shareable. Exploitation requires a user to create and expose an archive, so this is not a passive remote vulnerability. However, affected archives can contain live credentials, private keys, pairing authorization state, or inconsistent database contents. Avoiding or manually sanitizing exports is the current workaround. ## Validation - 125 focused profile-export tests passed. - 100 profile/distribution tests passed, 2 skipped. - 103 SharedMetricsStore/SQLite-backup tests passed, 7 skipped. - Final immutable review run: 373 passed, 2 skipped. - Ruff, compilation, diff checks, and adversarial archive probes passed. - Final independent exact-SHA review found no blockers. The branch is 3 commits ahead, 0 behind current `main`, with contributor authorship preserved and no merge conflicts.

signals.title: fix(auth): respect exhausted cooldowns in codex pool fallback resolver
signals.text: ### The Issue: When the singleton credentials are empty/invalid, Hermes falls back to resolving a token from the `openai-codex` credential pool using `_pool_codex_access_token()`. However, the inner helper `_entry_usable()` only checked `last_error_reset_at`. If an account in the pool hits a rate limit (HTTP 429) but the API error response parsing yields a `null` reset timestamp, `last_error_reset_at` is saved as `None` (or `null` in `auth.json`). Because of this, `_entry_usable()` evaluated the entry as usable despite its status being marked as `last_status: "exhausted"`, causing Hermes to get wedged on the exhausted token instead of rotating to the next available pooled accounts. ### Changes Made: 1. Updated `_entry_usable()` in `hermes_cli/auth.py` to check for `dead` or `exhausted` status, falling back to default cooldowns if `last_error_reset_at` is null. 2. Added unit tests covering pool fallback with null reset timestamps and dead status. 3. Updated Codex usage resolution to fallback to pool when singleton access token is missing.

signals.title: Fix Azure Foundry Responses post-tool replay
signals.text: ## Summary This patch fixes Azure Foundry Responses post-tool replay under `codex_responses`. Current upstream main reaches the post-tool follow-up request, but the follow-up input includes `function_call`, `function_call_output`, and `reasoning` items together. Azure Foundry rejects that payload with HTTP 400 `invalid_payload`. This patch scopes the behavior to Azure Foundry Responses and suppresses reasoning replay on post-tool turns while preserving `function_call` and `function_call_output` continuity. ## Why The initial model request and tool schema shape are not the root cause. The failure happens after tool execution, when the Responses follow-up input is constructed. On current upstream main, the debug harness reports: ```text likely failing phase: post-tool follow-up input input type values: function_call,function_call_output,reasoning invalid_payload: The provided data does not match the expected schema ``` With this patch branch, the same Foundry Project endpoint + Responses API debug harness completes successfully. The patched post-tool follow-up input contains `function_call` and `function_call_output`, but no replayed `reasoning` item. ## Validation * `uv run --with pytest --with pytest-timeout --with-editable ./hermes-agent python -m pytest hermes-agent/tests/agent/transports/test_codex_transport.py -q` * 62 passed * Validated with a Foundry Project endpoint + Responses API debug harness: * health passed: yes * capabilities HTTP status: 200 * model HTTP status: 200 * model marker returned: yes * tool HTTP status: 200 * tool request passed: yes * Also validated in an Azure Container Apps Sandboxes integration harness using a patched Hermes image: * model-directed Hermes tool routing passed: yes * workspace marker independently verified: yes ## Scope This change is intended to be narrow: * Azure Foundry Responses behavior is detected through the configured provider or Foundry Project endpoint host. * Reasoning replay suppression is scoped to Azure Foundry post-tool turns. * `function_call` and `function_call_output` continuity is preserved. * Existing non-Azure Responses behavior is covered by tests. ## Notes No secrets, endpoints, deployment names, tenant IDs, subscription IDs, client IDs, request IDs, or credentials are included.

signals.title: fix(models): use native Ollama tags without breaking generic discovery
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Use Ollama's native installed-model catalog for verified local Ollama endpoints, while preserving generic OpenAI-compatible discovery everywhere else. Local Ollama exposes its authoritative catalog at: ```text GET /api/tags ``` Hermes previously depended too heavily on `/v1/models` for discovery and model validation. A local Ollama deployment can expose the native catalog without exposing the OpenAI-compatible catalog, causing installed models to disappear from pickers or appear to be unavailable. ## Why this matters This PR makes model discovery follow the endpoint's actual protocol instead of the provider label alone: - verified local Ollama roots use `/api/tags`; - Ollama Cloud and ordinary custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints retain `/v1/models` discovery; - explicit model lists remain authoritative; - a reachable empty native catalog is distinct from an unreachable endpoint; - setup, picker, validation, model switching, and ACP catalog paths use the same discovery decision. That distinction prevents both failure modes: local Ollama models being hidden because `/v1/models` is unavailable, and generic or cloud endpoints being incorrectly forced through a local-only `/api/tags` path. ## Credential and origin safety Native catalog requests resolve configured `api_key`/`key_env` credentials and preserve explicitly supplied endpoint headers. Provider-configured credentials and headers are retained only for the matching normalized endpoint origin; they are not forwarded when an alias, fallback, or custom endpoint changes origin. Cache handling also preserves the protocol distinction: a reachable empty catalog can replace stale entries, while a transient probe failure can retain same-fingerprint stale data rather than turning an outage into an authoritative empty catalog. ## Scope and implementation The change is intentionally limited to model discovery and its existing consumers: - `hermes_cli/models.py`: native Ollama detection, `/api/tags` probing, URL normalization, credential/header handling, cache semantics, validation, and generic fallback; - `hermes_cli/model_setup_flows.py`, `hermes_cli/model_switch.py`, and `hermes_cli/main.py`: setup, picker, and switching parity; - `acp_adapter/server.py` and provider/runtime helpers: catalog identity and origin-safe propagation; - focused regression coverage across model discovery, validation, picker/setup, switching, ACP catalogs, cache state, URL normalization, headers, credentials, and cloud/custom exclusions. This is the active Vadelma-authored continuation of closed PR #49728, not a duplicate open implementation. The current series contains additional cache, URL, origin, header, credential-isolation, and selector-parity hardening beyond that predecessor. ## Why merge? The patch fixes a real local-Ollama compatibility gap without changing the generic provider contract. It keeps the server as the source of truth, preserves explicit configuration, fails conservatively on ambiguous endpoints, and exercises the same decision across the user-facing paths that consume model catalogs. The change is covered by deterministic regression tests and does not require a live model service for its hermetic verification. ## Related Issue No standalone issue. Supersedes closed PR #49728. ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## How to Test Validated on the exact published head `90c844718077a417676932311390479846288caf`. HERMES_HOME=$(mktemp -d) GH_CONFIG_DIR=$(mktemp -d) \ CODEX_HOME=$(mktemp -d) CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$(mktemp -d) XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$(mktemp -d) \ scripts/run_tests.sh -j 4 \ tests/hermes_cli/test_models.py signals.title: test(kanban): preserve non-zero exit for delegated-child refusals
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Adds regression coverage for the delegated-child Kanban CLI process boundary. A delegated child is forbidden from mutating Kanban. The refusal must be visible both in the diagnostic output and in the process exit status: ```text $ HERMES_DELEGATED_CHILD_CONTEXT=1 hermes kanban comment <task-id> "text" kanban: delegate_task child contexts cannot mutate Kanban tasks via the CLI $ echo $? 1 ``` This PR launches `python -m hermes_cli.main` in real subprocesses, creates a disposable task in a temporary Hermes home, attempts the forbidden mutation with delegated-child context, and verifies both the refusal message and exit status `1`. ## Why this matters The existing guard and production exit-status propagation are already on `main`. The missing protection was at the real CLI process boundary. Without this regression test, a future change could continue printing the refusal while accidentally returning status `0`; shell scripts, CI jobs, cron workers, or agent orchestration could then interpret a rejected mutation as success. The existing delegated-isolation tests cover the guard in their own testing layer. This test adds distinct end-to-end process-boundary coverage for the user-visible CLI contract. ## Scope - Test-only change; no production behavior change. - Adds one regression test in `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_cli_exit_status.py`. - Clears ambient Kanban environment overrides so the subprocess uses the disposable test home. - Bounds each CLI subprocess with `timeout=30` so a startup or dispatch regression cannot hang the test worker indefinitely. ## Related Issue No linked issue; this PR preserves the delegated-child CLI exit-status contract already implemented on `main`. ## Type of Change - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_cli_exit_status.py`: exercise delegated-child refusal through separate CLI subprocesses. - Assert that the refusal is reported on stderr and returns exit status `1`. - Use a temporary Hermes home and remove ambient Kanban path overrides from the child environment. - Add a finite `timeout=30` to the subprocess helper. ## How to Test Validated on the exact published head `336c7cb734dc6c5bb84e97169376da6ed9301a3e` against base `main` `005dfcbfcc5d3384986bb276b6d5c788324d2559`: ```text scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_cli_exit_status.py -q 1 passed uv run --no-project --python 3.14 python -m py_compile \ hermes_cli/main.py hermes_cli/kanban.py \ tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_cli_exit_status.py git diff --check pass ``` The full repository suite and broader overlap suites were not run for this metadata refresh. The focused regression, syntax compilation, and diff check are the current exact-head evidence. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — the full repository suite was not run - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on Linux ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — N/A - [ ] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A - [ ] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact — the test uses Python subprocesses and standard environment handling - [ ] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A ## Provenance - Published head: `336c7cb734dc6c5bb84e97169376da6ed9301a3e` - Base `main`: `005dfcbfcc5d3384986bb276b6d5c788324d2559` - Source fork: `vadelma-agent/hermes-agent` - Human sponsor and review-response owner: @tmielika No external service or production Kanban database is modified by the test.

signals.title: fix(tool-search): keep MCP bridge cache-stable
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? Fixes Tool Search's stale embedded catalog while keeping ordinary MCP catalog changes and context compression prompt-cache stable. The three bridge schemas (`tool_search`, `tool_describe`, and `tool_call`) are fixed and remain present whenever Tool Search is enabled, including when the live deferred catalog is empty. Bridge calls resolve the current session-scoped registry at invocation time, so MCP additions, removals, equal-count swaps, and schema edits no longer mutate the model-facing `tools=` prefix. The model receives discovery context through an API-only catalog snapshot attached to a real user turn. String user content stays clean while the exact API sidecar is persisted for byte-identical replay. When the catalog changes, Hermes attaches a superseding snapshot to the next real user turn instead of rebuilding bridge schemas or inserting a synthetic user-role message. Slow MCP startup is handled without waiting for every server. A snapshot lists tools currently ready plus the names of in-scope MCP servers still initializing. Pending-server state participates in the fingerprint, so a later real user turn carries a superseding snapshot when those servers become ready or fail. Snapshot construction does not import the MCP stack merely to inspect status. Compression also preserves discovery continuity. A turn may decide that an older snapshot is already present and then compress that older user row before its next model call. Before committing a successful compression boundary, Hermes re-anchors the current snapshot onto the newest surviving real user message's `api_content` (or a multimodal text part). If no genuine user row survives, it reuses an existing compression user scaffold rather than creating another message. Repeated compression checks for the exact current snapshot, so it is sent after every boundary without stacking duplicate copies in one message. ## Why Embedding the deferred-tool count and catalog inside bridge descriptions made every toolset edit change `tools=`, invalidating the cached conversation prefix. Moving discovery metadata out of the bridge solves that, but two additional boundaries matter: - waiting for all MCP servers would move potentially long startup latency onto the chat critical path; - compression can remove the catalog-bearing historical turn and continue calling the model in the same turn, before the normal next-turn re-announcement runs. This PR separates those concerns: - stable bridge schemas preserve the cached prefix; - append-only metadata on real user turns preserves role alternation; - pending server names keep not-yet-ready capability domains discoverable; - live registry lookup makes newly registered tools usable immediately; - compression re-anchors the current snapshot before persistence and retry; - resumed sessions compare the live schema/pending fingerprint with persisted `api_content`, reusing an identical snapshot or superseding a stale one. This PR does not change surface-specific MCP startup scheduling. It makes Tool Search catalog construction and replay safe when discovery is incomplete or conversation history is compressed. ## Related Issue Fixes #72560 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [x] 📝 Documentation update - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - Replaced dynamic bridge counts/listings with byte-stable schemas and live registry discovery. - Kept the bridge present across the zero-tool boundary. - Moved compact catalog snapshots onto the API copy of real user turns. - Fingerprinted complete scoped schemas, rendered manifest form, and pending MCP server names. - Added a non-blocking pending-server probe that never imports `tools.mcp_tool` solely for snapshot generation. - Published a superseding snapshot on the next real user turn when a pending server becomes ready or fails. - Re-anchored the current snapshot at every successful compression boundary before in-place or rotation persistence. - Preserved existing plugin/memory sidecar content, handled multimodal turns, and deduplicated repeated compression anchors. - Covered zero-human-turn compression by reusing an existing user scaffold without changing role alternation. - Kept direct-schema mode schema-sensitive while preserving the exact `agent.tools` object in stable-bridge mode. - Updated Tool Search documentation and regression coverage. ## How to Test 1. Start a session with Tool Search enabled while an MCP server is connecting. 2. Verify the first real user turn lists ready tools and pending server names without changing bridge schemas. 3. Let the server connect; verify `tool_search` sees the live tools and the next real user turn carries a superseding snapshot. 4. Compress a later turn after the original snapshot-bearing user row has entered the compressible region. 5. Verify the compressed request and persisted transcript contain exactly one current snapshot on the newest surviving user message. 6. Repeat in both in-place and rotation compression modes, then resume the session and verify byte-identical `api_content` replay. 7. Set `tools.tool_search.enabled: off`; verify direct tool definitions continue to rebuild normally. Validated on the pushed commit: ```shell scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 \ tests/agent/test_turn_context.py \ tests/run_agent/test_compression_persistence.py -q # 36 passed scripts/run_tests.sh -j 6 \ tests/tools/test_tool_search.py \ tests/tools/test_refresh_agent_mcp_tools.py \ tests/agent/test_turn_context.py \ tests/agent/test_api_content_sidecar.py \ tests/run_agent/test_compression_persistence.py \ tests/agent/test_compression_rotation_state.py \ tests/agent/test_compression_concurrent_fork.py \ tests/agent/test_context_compressor_zero_user_provenance.py \ tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins.py \ tests/cli/test_cli_mcp_config_watch.py \ tests/hermes_cli/test_mcp_reload_confirm_gate.py \ tests/gateway/test_mcp_reload_refreshes_cached_agents.py \ tests/tui_gateway/test_mcp_reload_rev.py \ tests/test_tui_mcp_late_refresh.py \ tests/tui_gateway/test_mcp_late_refresh_thread_owner.py -q # 215 passed # Under a heavily loaded run, the existing concurrent-compression lock test # exceeded its 10s timing window once and passed on the runner retry. scripts/run_tests.sh -j 1 tests/agent/test_compression_concurrent_fork.py -q # 16 passed cleanly in isolation .venv/bin/ruff check \ agent/conversation_compression.py \ tests/agent/test_turn_context.py \ tests/run_agent/test_compression_persistence.py # All checks passed git diff --check # clean ``` ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) - [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix - [ ] I've run the complete `pytest tests/ -q` suite; the targeted cross-entry regression suites above pass - [x] I've added tests for the changed behavior - [x] I've tested on macOS 27.0, Python 3.13 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] Relevant documentation is updated - [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` update — N/A (no config keys changed) - [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md` update — N/A - [x] Cross-platform impact considered; signals.title: test(gateway): make unset model override explicit in background fixture
signals.text: ## Summary Make the `/background` gateway tests exercise the real **no model override** path instead of a truthy mock value that looks like a persisted override. ## Why this matters `GatewayRunner` rehydrates a session's model override before starting a background task. In production, `SessionStore.get_model_override()` returns `None` when the user has not set a `/model` override. The test fixture used an unconfigured `MagicMock` session store. Its default return value is truthy, so the test could accidentally create a fake model override and pass a `MagicMock` into the session-scoped reasoning resolver. That means the test was not reliably exercising the normal no-override path, and its result could depend on mock behavior rather than the production contract. This is a test correctness issue: the fixture can mask regressions or fail for the wrong reason even though production behavior is unchanged. ## Fix Set: ```python mock_store.get_model_override.return_value = None ``` in `_make_runner()`, matching the real `SessionStore` contract. ## Scope - One test fixture in `tests/gateway/test_background_command.py`. - Four added lines; no production-code, dependency, configuration, or formatter changes. - Existing background-command scenarios now run with an explicit absent override. This should merge because it is a minimal, behavior-preserving correction that makes the gateway regression tests represent the production no-override state they intend to cover. ## Verification Against upstream `main` at `8d4b1e4b0e240af67c1f4eb6601aee99eac0bc49`, exact head `903c867cf8ba0d1737ae52d4ee296a71b09dd0aa`: ```text scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_background_command.py -q 7 passed uv run --extra dev ruff check tests/gateway/test_background_command.py All checks passed git diff --check refs/remotes/upstream/main...HEAD passed ``` The canonical test harness ran with its clean environment (`TZ=UTC`, `LANG=C.UTF-8`, `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`). ## Checklist - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] The change is narrowly scoped to one test fixture. - [x] The focused regression tests pass with `scripts/run_tests.sh`. - [x] Focused Ruff and whitespace checks pass. - [x] No production behavior, dependency, configuration, or platform adapter changes are included. - [x] The current upstream overlap and existing PR history were checked. No issue link: this is a narrowly scoped upstream test-fixture correction. Human sponsor and review-response owner: @tmielika

signals.title: feat(langfuse): trace auxiliary LLM calls for full usage accounting (config.yaml + async)
signals.text: ## Summary Auxiliary LLM calls (context compression, vision, web_extract, MoA, session search, ...) were invisible to the Langfuse observability plugin: they go through `agent/auxiliary_client.call_llm` / `async_call_llm`, which bypass the agent-turn hooks the plugin subscribes to. Over time this makes Langfuse token totals diverge from provider billing (e.g. api.deepseek.com), breaking reconciliation between observability and the provider's own usage report. This reworks the previous attempt (#76874) per the standing maintainer policy and fixes its two blockers: ## Policy compliance (per #76874 close comment + AGENTS.md) 1. **Behavioral flag moved from env var to config.yaml.** The opt-in is now `plugins.entries.observability/langfuse.track_aux` in `config.yaml` — no new `HERMES_*` env var. `.env` stays reserved for secrets (AGENTS.md: "All behavioral settings ... go in config.yaml"). 2. **Async coverage added (the "not full auxiliary accounting" gap).** The original PR wrapped only synchronous `call_llm`, but the vision path calls `async_call_llm` (`tools/vision_tools.py:1278`). The observer now fires for **both** sync `call_llm` and async `async_call_llm` (start/end/error). ## Changes **agent/auxiliary_client.py** - Observer registry (`register_aux_llm_observer` / `unregister_aux_llm_observer` / `_notify_aux_llm`) — empty by default, zero overhead; observers are fail-open. - `call_llm` thin wrapper around `_call_llm_impl` emitting start/end/error. - `async_call_llm` thin wrapper around `_async_call_llm_impl` emitting the same events — covers the vision path. **plugins/observability/langfuse** - `_track_aux_enabled()` resolves `plugins.entries.observability/langfuse.track_aux` from config.yaml (cached per process, fail-closed to False on config read errors). - When enabled, registers the observer and records each auxiliary call as a standalone `Hermes aux: <task>` trace with a GENERATION child carrying token usage — including DeepSeek cache hit/miss via the existing `_usage_and_cost` path. - README documents the config.yaml opt-in. **tests/plugins/test_langfuse_plugin.py** - `TestAuxTracking`: default-off, config.yaml resolution, observer registration, usage recording (cache_read/input/output), error-path cleanup. - `TestAuxObserversOnCallLlm`: sync AND async call_llm both emit start/end/error events. ## Verification - `pytest tests/plugins/test_langfuse_plugin.py` → 33 passed (incl. 9 new). - `pytest tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client.py` → 169 passed. - `pytest tests/tools/test_vision_tools.py tests/agent/test_auxiliary_compression_timeout_floor.py tests/agent/test_unsupported_parameter_retry.py tests/agent/test_unsupported_temperature_retry.py tests/tools/test_video_analyze.py` → 67 passed. - E2E against a local Langfuse instance: sync `call_llm` and async `async_call_llm` both produced `Hermes aux: <task>` traces in ClickHouse with correct usage details (input/output/cache_read/reasoning/total); async error path closes the trace cleanly.

signals.title: fix(tools): stop browser_cdp frame_id routing from skipping private-page SSRF guard
signals.text: ## What does this PR do? `browser_cdp(..., frame_id=...)` had two private-page / SSRF gaps on the OOPIF path: (1) a non-dict `params` value skipped the clear validation error and could let the guard fail open, and (2) even with valid params, the guard only checked the top-level page URL before supervisor dispatch, so a public parent could embed a private OOPIF and still receive page-content CDP such as `Runtime.evaluate`. This PR closes both paths with shared fail-closed checks before child-session dispatch. ### Symptom A `browser_cdp` call that sets `frame_id` and passes a truthy non-dict `params` (for example a string) does not return `'params' must be an object/dict`. Separately, when the top-level page is public but the selected OOPIF URL/origin is private (or still empty), page-content CDP can still reach the child session. ### Impact Malformed `params` on the `frame_id` path can silently skip the private-page / SSRF boundary that other `browser_cdp` entry points enforce after validating `params`. A public top-level page with a private child OOPIF can also expose private frame content through `frame_id` routing. Blast radius beyond these paths was not measured. ### Bug Cause **Trigger:** `tools/browser_cdp_tool.py` `browser_cdp()` / `_browser_cdp_via_supervisor()` - `frame_id` early-return before `isinstance(params, dict)`; private-page guard uses top-level `_current_page_private_url` only; selected-frame metadata is available but was not checked before child-session dispatch. **Causal chain:** 1. Caller passes `frame_id` with either non-dict `params`, or a well-formed call targeting a private OOPIF under a public top page. 2. Non-dict `params` AttributeErrors inside the guard probe; broad except fail-opens. Or the top-page probe returns public while the child frame is private / metadata-empty. 3. Call reaches `_browser_cdp_via_supervisor` and dispatches into the child CDP session without a validation error or frame-level private-page block. **Why it is wrong:** Params validation lived only on the post-early-return / stateless branch, while the guard is intentionally fail-open for probe failures. Frame routing resolves child URL/origin but never validated them before page-content sinks. **Working sibling / contrast:** Without `frame_id`, non-dict `params` already returned a clear validation error. Top-level private pages already blocked restricted methods; the gap is specifically the selected OOPIF address. **Ruled out:** Not a missing private-page guard call on `frame_id` for well-formed top-level-private cases - that path already invoked the top-page guard. The remaining gaps are malformed params + child-frame address coverage. ### Fix Validate `params` as a dict before the `frame_id` early-return. After resolving the selected frame (frame_tree or raw `_frames` fallback), validate URL/origin for private/internal addresses before dispatch; fail closed when an OOPIF has a `session_id` but empty URL/origin metadata. Retain `_CDP_PRIVATE_PAGE_ALLOWED_METHODS` so navigation/inspection still works on blocked frames. ## Related Issue Fixes #80846 ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [x] Security fix ## Changes Made - `tools/browser_cdp_tool.py` - move params dict validation above the `frame_id` early-return; validate selected frame URL/origin (and empty-metadata OOPIF) before supervisor dispatch; keep navigation/inspection allowlist - `tests/tools/test_browser_cdp_tool.py` - regression coverage for non-dict params, public-top/private-child OOPIF, raw `_frames` fallback, allowlist survival, and empty URL/origin fail-closed ## How to Test 1. Manual: with the private-page guard active, call `browser_cdp(method='Runtime.evaluate', params='not-a-dict', frame_id='...')` and confirm the tool returns a params object/dict validation error (not a successful supervisor dispatch). 2. Manual / unit: public top-level page + private OOPIF `frame_id` must block `Runtime.evaluate` / `DOM.getDocument`; allowlisted methods such as `Page.reload` must still dispatch; OOPIF with `session_id` but empty url/origin must block page-content CDP. 3. Automated: ```bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_browser_cdp_tool.py -q ``` ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [x] I've run `scripts/run_tests.sh` on relevant tests and all tests pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 (WSL test runner) ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) - N/A - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys - N/A - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows - N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) - N/A (validation helpers are platform-agnostic) - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior - N/A (behavior matches the documented params object contract and private-page boundary on sibling paths)
