signal.title: copilot-acp: fallback providers not triggered when Copilot monthly quota is exhausted
signal.text: ## Description When using `copilot-acp` as the primary provider with `fallback_providers` configured, the fallback chain does **not** activate when GitHub Copilot returns a monthly quota exhaustion error. Instead of falling back to the next provider, the error is surfaced directly to the user. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure `copilot-acp` as primary provider: ```yaml model: provider: copilot-acp default: auto base_url: acp://copilot api_mode: chat_completions ``` 2. Configure fallback providers: ```yaml fallback_providers: - provider: opencode-zen model: big-pickle base_url: https://opencode.ai/zen/v1 api_mode: chat_completions - provider: openrouter model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash base_url: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 api_mode: chat_completions - provider: openai-codex model: gpt-5.4-mini base_url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex ``` 3. Have valid API keys for fallback providers (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `OPENCODE_ZEN_API_KEY`). 4. Exhaust Copilot's monthly quota. 5. Send a message via Telegram or CLI — the agent returns the raw error instead of falling back. ## Error Message ``` Error: You have exceeded your monthly quota (Request ID: A540:22A007:3849658:44F52D9:6A541F53) ``` ## Analysis The Copilot ACP client (`agent/copilot_acp_client.py`) raises a `RuntimeError` when the subprocess exits early. The error message contains the word `"quota"` which exists in `_USAGE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` in `agent/error_classifier.py`, which should classify it as `FailoverReason.billing` with `should_fallback=True`. However, in practice the fallback chain is never activated. There appear to be two potential issues: 1. **Missing billing pattern**: `_BILLING_PATTERNS` has `"exceeded your current quota"` but the Copilot message says `"exceeded your *monthly* quota"` — the substring `"exceeded your current quota"` does not match `"exceeded your monthly quota"`. While `_USAGE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` does contain `"quota"`, the matching logic may not be reaching that check for ACP RuntimeErrors. 2. **ACP error path**: The RuntimeError from the ACP subprocess may be caught at a different level before reaching `classify_api_error()` in the conversation loop, bypassing the classification entirely. ## Environment - Hermes Agent (latest) - Provider: `copilot-acp` - Platform: Telegram gateway (also reproducible via CLI) - API keys for fallback providers are configured and valid ## Expected Behavior When Copilot ACP returns a quota exhaustion error, the fallback chain should activate and switch to the next configured provider (opencode-zen, then openrouter, etc.). ## Actual Behavior The error is surfaced directly without attempting fallback providers.
signal.author: craftpip

signal.title: ACP adapter: turns ending in text_response are silently dropped on Buzz-connected sessions (never published to relay)
signal.text: # ACP adapter: turns ending in `text_response` are silently dropped on Buzz-connected sessions (never published to relay) ## Summary On a Buzz-connected ACP persona ("Leo", running as a systemd-managed `buzz-acp-leo.service`), a conversation turn that ended with `reason=text_response` (i.e. the model's final output was plain assistant text with no accompanying tool call) was silently lost — never published to the Nostr relay, never retried, and never logged as an error. The user received no reply for 47 minutes and the ~1897-character status update is permanently unrecoverable. Turns that end via an explicit tool call (e.g. a "send to Buzz" action) are delivered correctly and logged as such, which strongly suggests the ACP↔Buzz bridge only treats tool-call-driven sends as requiring an explicit relay-publish step, and silently drops bare `text_response` turns. ## Environment - Hermes Agent, ACP adapter mode (`buzz-acp` persona integration) - Persona: "Leo", running as systemd service `buzz-acp-leo.service` on a self-hosted Hetzner box - Transport: Buzz relay (self-hosted), Nostr protocol backend for message publish/subscribe - Observed: 2026-08-12, via `journalctl -u buzz-acp-leo.service` ## Steps to Reproduce / Conditions Observed Not yet reproduced on demand — this is a single confirmed incident reconstructed from production logs. Condensed timeline (all UTC, 2026-08-12): 1. **01:45:26** — Leo sends a DM committing to two tracks of work ("On it. Splitting into two tracks: ..."). 2. **01:46:44** — New conversation turn begins, session `20260812_014644_fc0f12`, executing track 1. 3. **01:52:13** — Track 1 completes successfully: a review request is sent via an explicit tool call to a ticket-lane channel (confirmed via tool-call log line, event `fcbdf2cc...`). **This confirms the normal send path works when a turn ends via an explicit tool call.** 4. **01:55:57** — API call #13 completes (in=134509, out=676 tokens, latency=11.2s, cache=99%). Immediately followed by: `Turn ended: reason=text_response(finish_reason=stop) ... response_len=1897 session=20260812_014644_fc0f12` — the agent composed a ~1897-character status update as plain text, with **no tool call**. 5. **01:55:57 → 01:56:28** (31s, relay connection healthy) — **no publish/send/outbound log line appears anywhere** for this response. Delivery was never even attempted. 6. **01:56:28 → 02:20:39** — Unrelated relay websocket disconnect ("no pong received within 10s — connection dead, reconnecting"), ~24 min outage. Confirmed **coincidental, not causal** — the response vanished 31s *before* this outage began, while the connection was still up. 7. **02:20:39** — Relay reconnects and resubscribes to channels. No queue-flush, resend, or retry of the missing message occurs in the following 15+ minutes. 8. **Ground truth check** — Direct fetch of the DM channel from the relay shows nothing from Leo between 01:45:26 and 02:32:59 (47 minutes of silence). Human (Nick) pinged at 01:50:42 ("I don't understand. Are you working or not?") with no reply logged. Only after a second nag at 02:32:33 did Leo produce a **new, differently-worded** reply — not a delayed delivery of the original. The original 1897-char update is permanently lost with no trace, no error, no retry. ## Expected vs Actual Behavior **Expected:** Any final assistant response intended for the user — regardless of whether the turn ends via a tool call or via plain `text_response` — is published to the Buzz/Nostr relay, or a delivery failure is logged/retried/alerted. **Actual:** Turns ending in `reason=text_response` with no tool call appear to close without any publish attempt to the relay. No error, warning, or retry is logged. The message is silently and permanently dropped. ## Root Cause Analysis **Caveat: this is evidence-based inference from log analysis, not a traced code path.** We have not stepped through the actual ACP adapter / Buzz bridge source to confirm the exact mechanism — treat the following as a strong hypothesis, not a confirmed diagnosis. The pattern observed is consistent with the ACP↔Buzz bridge only wiring an explicit "publish to relay" action to tool-call-based sends (e.g. a `send_to_buzz`-style tool), while turns that end purely on `text_response` (plain final assistant text, `finish_reason=stop`, no tool call) are not recognized by the bridge as requiring an outbound publish at all. No error is raised because — from the adapter's perspective — nothing went wrong; it simply never routed that text anywhere. Likely candidate code areas (unverified, offered as starting points for investigation): - `acp_adapter/server.py` — turn completion / response handling - `buzz_acp` Rust relay client — outbound publish invocation sites - `agent/turn_finalizer.py` (or equivalent) — specifically the `text_response` finish-reason branch ## Related Issues This matches a broader known bug class already partially tracked upstream — same failure symptom (final assistant response generated but never delivered), different transport in each case: - **#10748** — "streaming mode silently drops final response when `already_sent` is true" (response stored in DB, never delivered). Same failure class; different transport (streaming path, not ACP/Buzz). - **#31884** — Telegram gateway can silently drop a turn with `response=0 chars` while internal work continues. Same failure class; Telegram gateway, not ACP/Buzz. - **#31588** — Messages sent while agent is busy get silently queued with no feedback. Related failure mode (silent loss of user-facing signal) but different trigger condition. Filing this as a **new issue** rather than a comment on #10748 because the transport and adapter code involved (ACP adapter, Buzz relay client, `text_response` turn-finalization path) is distinct from whatever code #10748/#31884/#31588 cover — but cross-linking all three here since they may share a root cause or fix pattern (i.e. "final response delivery must not depend on which finish_reason ended the turn"). ## Suggested Fix (suggestions only — not implemented or tested) **(a) Route text_response through the same explicit publish mechanism as tool-call sends.** For ACP/Buzz-bound sessions, make the bare "turn ends in plain text" case invoke the same explicit publish/send call used by tool-call-based sends, so there is no code path where a text-ending turn can complete without an outbound relay event being attempted. **(b) Add a post-turn delivery integrity check.** If a Buzz-bound session's turn ends with `reason=text_response` and no corresponding outbound Nostr event is emitted within a short window (e.g. a few seconds), log an ERROR and either retry the publish or alert, rather than allowing the turn to close silently. Either approach (or both, as belt-and-suspenders) would have caught this incident — (a) prevents the drop, (b) would have at minimum surfaced it as a visible error instead of 47 minutes of silent user-facing failure. ## Reproduction Status **Not reproduced on demand.** This report is based entirely on `journalctl` log analysis of a live production instance (`buzz-acp-leo.service`) after the incident was noticed via user complaint ("I don't understand. Are you working or not?"). No isolated repro case has been constructed yet. Happy to assist with building one if adapter maintainers can point to the relevant turn-finalization code, or if there's a known way to force a turn to end in `finish_reason=stop` with no tool call in a Buzz-connected test session.

signal.title: Fix Azure Foundry Responses post-tool replay
signal.text: ## Summary This patch fixes Azure Foundry Responses post-tool replay under `codex_responses`. Current upstream main reaches the post-tool follow-up request, but the follow-up input includes `function_call`, `function_call_output`, and `reasoning` items together. Azure Foundry rejects that payload with HTTP 400 `invalid_payload`. This patch scopes the behavior to Azure Foundry Responses and suppresses reasoning replay on post-tool turns while preserving `function_call` and `function_call_output` continuity. ## Why The initial model request and tool schema shape are not the root cause. The failure happens after tool execution, when the Responses follow-up input is constructed. On current upstream main, the debug harness reports: ```text likely failing phase: post-tool follow-up input input type values: function_call,function_call_output,reasoning invalid_payload: The provided data does not match the expected schema ``` With this patch branch, the same Foundry Project endpoint + Responses API debug harness completes successfully. The patched post-tool follow-up input contains `function_call` and `function_call_output`, but no replayed `reasoning` item. ## Validation * `uv run --with pytest --with pytest-timeout --with-editable ./hermes-agent python -m pytest hermes-agent/tests/agent/transports/test_codex_transport.py -q` * 62 passed * Validated with a Foundry Project endpoint + Responses API debug harness: * health passed: yes * capabilities HTTP status: 200 * model HTTP status: 200 * model marker returned: yes * tool HTTP status: 200 * tool request passed: yes * Also validated in an Azure Container Apps Sandboxes integration harness using a patched Hermes image: * model-directed Hermes tool routing passed: yes * workspace marker independently verified: yes ## Scope This change is intended to be narrow: * Azure Foundry Responses behavior is detected through the configured provider or Foundry Project endpoint host. * Reasoning replay suppression is scoped to Azure Foundry post-tool turns. * `function_call` and `function_call_output` continuity is preserved. * Existing non-Azure Responses behavior is covered by tests. ## Notes No secrets, endpoints, deployment names, tenant IDs, subscription IDs, client IDs, request IDs, or credentials are included.
signal.author: AshuJoshi

signal.title: fix(azure-foundry): scope Responses reasoning suppression to post-tool turns
signal.text: ## Summary Salvage of #59981, rebuilt on current `main`. Same root cause and same fix direction as @AshuJoshi's original; the diagnosis there was correct and is preserved. This version resolves the three blockers found in review and keeps his tests plus five new ones. Azure Foundry's OpenAI-compatible Responses surface rejects the **post-tool follow-up** payload with HTTP 400 `invalid_payload` when a replayed encrypted `reasoning` item is sent alongside `function_call` / `function_call_output`. The initial function-call request and ordinary multi-turn continuity are both accepted, so the failure only appears after the first tool executes and the follow-up input is constructed. `ResponsesApiTransport.build_kwargs` now detects the Foundry endpoint and drops only the encrypted reasoning replay on that follow-up turn, leaving `function_call` / `function_call_output` continuity intact. ## What changed relative to #59981 **1. No `chat_completion_helpers.py` change at all.** `main` already forwards `provider` and `base_url` to the Responses transport (lines 1443 and 1447). The original PR re-added both, which auto-merged into invalid Python: ``` SyntaxError: keyword argument repeated: provider ``` That is why the PR showed as `CONFLICTING`. Dropping the hunk entirely removes the conflict and the syntax error together — the detection has everything it needs from the existing call site. **2. Host matching uses `utils.base_url_host_matches`, not a substring test.** `".services.ai.azure.com" in base_url` also matches URLs that merely *carry* the domain: | base_url | substring | this PR | |---|---|---| | `https://myres.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/p/openai/v1` | ✅ | ✅ | | `https://proxy.example.com/.services.ai.azure.com/v1` | ✅ ❌ | ❌ | | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1?upstream=.services.ai.azure.com` | ✅ ❌ | ❌ | | `https://services.ai.azure.com.evil.example/v1` | ✅ ❌ | ❌ | Suppressing reasoning replay on an unrelated provider silently degrades its cross-turn coherence. `base_url_host_matches` exists for exactly this false-positive class, its docstring names it, and every sibling detector in this transport already uses it. **3. `_is_post_tool_replay` tests the trailing messages, not the whole history.** The original scanned the entire history for *any* assistant tool call plus *any* tool result, so it latched on permanently: ``` user → assistant(tool_calls) → tool → assistant("done") → user("explain recursion") ^ reasoning suppressed here, and on every later turn ``` That is the all-turns behavior the scoping was meant to avoid, reached one turn later. The rejected payload is specifically the turn *ending* on a tool result, so that is what is matched — including a trailing run of parallel tool results. ## Validation Verified with `scripts/run_tests.sh`, the repo's canonical per-file-isolation runner that matches CI: ``` scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/ tests/run_agent/ 532 files, 5595 tests passed, 0 failed, 21 skipped ``` `ruff check` clean on all three touched files. **27 tests** (@AshuJoshi's, plus new coverage for the two defects above): - post-tool suppression on Foundry; reasoning preserved on non-Azure Responses - detection by provider id and by endpoint host, independently - three non-Foundry host lookalikes (path, query, suffix) keep reasoning - non-tool Foundry follow-up keeps reasoning - user turn after a completed tool call keeps reasoning — sticky-history guard - parallel tool results still suppress - an explicit `replay_encrypted_reasoning=False` is never re-enabled - live `build_api_kwargs` path for the post-tool, non-tool, and post-tool-then-user-turn shapes Each new guard was confirmed to catch its defect by reverting to the unscoped host match and whole-history scan: the three lookalike cases and both sticky-history guards fail, and pass with the fix. ## Not verified here I have no Azure Foundry credentials, so I did not reproduce the original HTTP 400 or re-confirm the fix against a live endpoint. **This change is verified at the payload-construction layer only.** The live evidence — the Foundry Project + Responses API debug harness and the Azure Container Apps integration run — is @AshuJoshi's, from #59981. A live re-check by someone with a Foundry deployment before merge would be worth having. Closes #59981.

signal.title: fix(discord): preserve thread routing for progress edits
signal.text: ## Summary Fix Discord progress-message edits that target the parent channel even when the message was originally sent inside a thread. - Resolve Discord edit targets from `metadata.thread_id`, falling back to `chat_id` when thread metadata is absent. - Preserve thread routing for long-running heartbeat edits, stale streamed-finalize reconciliation, and plugin-transformed final edits. - Keep legacy platform adapters compatible by passing metadata only when their `edit_message()` signature supports it. ## Root cause Discord progress sends honor `metadata.thread_id`, but `DiscordAdapter.edit_message()` previously fetched the message from the parent `chat_id`. Discord therefore returned `10008 Unknown Message` / HTTP 404 for a message that existed in the thread. ## Tests - Reproduced RED for adapter, heartbeat, stale-finalize, and transformed-response paths. - Focused routing tests: 5/5 normal and 5/5 optimized. - Discord edit/overflow tests: 9/9 normal and 9/9 optimized. - Kanban notifier tests: 9/9 normal and 9/9 optimized. - `py_compile`: 6/6. - `git diff --check`: PASS. - Independent pre-commit review: PASS (B0/M0/m0). ## Scope Six files changed. No schema, database, daemon, retry-policy, or credential changes.

signal.title: fix(redaction): mask array-style query credentials
signal.text: ## Summary - recognize PHP/Rails-style array query keys at strict credential-redaction boundaries - mask both literal `access_token[]=...` and percent-encoded `access_token%5B%5D=...` forms while preserving the original key spelling - preserve similarly named public parameters such as `token_count[]` and `access_tokenized[]` - cover the shared redactor plus compaction-summary and pre-compression memory-context paths ## Why Strict URL redaction decodes parameter names before exact sensitive-name matching. Array-style keys decoded to `access_token[]`, so they missed the canonical `access_token` entry and their values remained visible in persisted compaction summaries and memory context sent for compression. This focused PR extracts the independently useful shared-redactor fix from #35601, following the suggestion in [this review comment](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/35601#issuecomment-5288097879). It does not change default navigation redaction behavior; the stricter handling remains opt-in through `redact_url_credentials=True`. ## Validation - `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_redact.py tests/agent/test_compaction_redaction_boundaries.py tests/agent/test_pre_compress_memory_context.py tests/agent/test_context_compressor.py tests/test_redaction_registry.py -q` - 268 passed - regression-proof run against the pre-fix implementation - 5 focused assertions failed, then passed with the fix restored - Ruff on all changed Python files - Python compilation and `git diff --check` Related to #35601.

signal.title: fix(security): bind exec-approval clicks to session owner (#80281)
signal.text: Command-approval button clicks were only checked against the general allowlist — any admitted user could approve a dangerous command that another user triggered in a shared thread. In a shared/thread context User B could approve a `rm -rf` that User A's session queued. Fix: thread `requesting_user_id` (the session owner from SessionSource.user_id) through send_exec_approval → ExecApprovalView and enforce an owner match in _check_auth. A new `approval_scope` config key (`owner` | `admins` | `any`, default `owner`) controls the policy: - `owner` (default, new): only the requesting user may approve - `admins`: any user in `allow_admin_from` may approve - `any`: legacy behavior — any admitted user may approve When `requesting_user_id` is None (CLI sessions, platforms without user identity), the check falls back to the legacy behavior so existing single-user installs are unaffected. All six platform adapters (Discord, Telegram, Slack, Feishu, Teams, Matrix) accept the new parameter. Enforcement is in the Discord adapter (ExecApprovalView._check_auth); other adapters accept the parameter for forward compatibility. Tests: 12 new tests in test_discord_component_auth.py covering owner approval, non-owner rejection, no-requesting-user fallback, any/admins scope behavior, invalid scope fallback, and the _resolve_approval_scope helper. All 44 tests in the affected test suite pass. Fixes #80281 ## What does this PR do? When a dangerous command is queued for approval, the gateway sends approve/deny buttons to the chat platform. The authorization check for the button click only verified that the clicking user was some admitted user — it did not verify that the clicker was the user whose session triggered the command. In a shared thread context, User B could approve a rm -rf that User A's session queued. This PR threads requesting_user_id (from SessionSource.user_id) through send_exec_approval → ExecApprovalView._check_auth and enforces an owner match. A new approval_scope config key (owner | admins | any, default owner) controls the policy: owner (default, new): only the requesting user may approve admins: any user in allow_admin_from may approve any: legacy behavior — any admitted user may approve When requesting_user_id is None (CLI sessions, platforms without user identity), the check falls back to the legacy behavior so existing single-user installs are unaffected. All six platform adapters (Discord, Telegram, Slack, Feishu, Teams, Matrix) accept the new requesting_user_id parameter. Enforcement is in the Discord adapter (ExecApprovalView._check_auth); other adapters accept the parameter for forward compatibility. ## Related Issue https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/80281 Fixes #80281 ## Type of Change <!-- Check the one that applies. --> - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [X] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [X] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py: Core fix — ExecApprovalView.__init__ now accepts requesting_user_id and approval_scope; _check_auth enforces owner match when scope is owner; new _resolve_approval_scope() helper reads the config key from the platform's extra block; send_exec_approval accepts and passes through requesting_user_id - gateway/run.py: Passes ctx.source.user_id (the session owner from SessionSource) through to send_exec_approval - plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py: Accepts requesting_user_id parameter (forward compatibility) - plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py: Same - plugins/platforms/feishu/adapter.py: Same - plugins/platforms/teams/adapter.py: Same - plugins/platforms/matrix/adapter.py: Same - tests/gateway/test_discord_component_auth.py: 12 new tests covering owner approval, non-owner rejection, no-requesting-user fallback, any/admins scope behavior, invalid scope fallback, and the _resolve_approval_scope helper ## How to Test <!-- Steps to verify this change works. For bugs: reproduction steps + proof that the fix works. --> 1. Run the test suite: python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_discord_component_auth.py -v — all 28 tests pass (16 existing + 12 new) 2. Run sibling test suites to confirm no regressions: python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_discord_exec_approval_content.py tests/gateway/test_approval_prompt_redaction.py tests/gateway/test_discord_prompt_timeout_config.py tests/gateway/test_discord_lazy_install_views.py tests/gateway/test_discord_prompt_content_siblings.py -v — all 15 pass 3. Manual scenario: configure two allowed Discord users, have User A trigger a dangerous command, verify User B cannot click the approve button (gets "You're not authorized" ephemeral reply). Set approval_scope: "any" in the Discord platform's extra config to restore legacy behavior where any admitted user can approve. ## Checklist <!-- Complete these before requesting review. --> ### Code - [X] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [X] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [X] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [X] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [X] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass - [X] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [X] I've tested on my platform: <!-- e.g. Ubuntu 24.04, macOS 15.2, Windows 11 --> ### Documentation & Housekeeping <!-- Check all that apply. signal.title: fix(auth): respect exhausted cooldowns in codex pool fallback resolver
signal.text: ### The Issue: When the singleton credentials are empty/invalid, Hermes falls back to resolving a token from the `openai-codex` credential pool using `_pool_codex_access_token()`. However, the inner helper `_entry_usable()` only checked `last_error_reset_at`. If an account in the pool hits a rate limit (HTTP 429) but the API error response parsing yields a `null` reset timestamp, `last_error_reset_at` is saved as `None` (or `null` in `auth.json`). Because of this, `_entry_usable()` evaluated the entry as usable despite its status being marked as `last_status: "exhausted"`, causing Hermes to get wedged on the exhausted token instead of rotating to the next available pooled accounts. ### Changes Made: 1. Updated `_entry_usable()` in `hermes_cli/auth.py` to check for `dead` or `exhausted` status, falling back to default cooldowns if `last_error_reset_at` is null. 2. Added unit tests covering pool fallback with null reset timestamps and dead status. 3. Updated Codex usage resolution to fallback to pool when singleton access token is missing.

signal.title: feat(providers): add Inworld model provider
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Adds **Inworld** as a first-class model provider. Inworld exposes an OpenAI-compatible completions endpoint at `https://api.inworld.ai/v1` that fronts its own models (`inworld/models/…`) alongside several upstream providers (`openai/`, `anthropic/`, `deepinfra/`, …). Chat needs no adapter and no new `api_mode`, so this follows the documented plugin fast path — **zero core edits**. The one part that needs real code is the model catalog, which differs from the OpenAI convention in three independent ways that `ProviderProfile.fetch_models` cannot absorb through configuration: | | Base `fetch_models` | Inworld | |---|---|---| | URL | `{base_url}/models` → `/v1/models` | `/llm/v1alpha/models` — host-absolute, outside the `/v1` prefix | | Auth | `Bearer` | `Basic` (completions still take `Bearer`, which the OpenAI client builds itself — Inworld accepts both) | | Shape | `{"data": [{"id": …}]}` | `{"models": [{provider, model, spec}]}` | `fetch_models` is overridden for those, and filters to models advertising `functionCalling` — Hermes drives every turn through tool calls, so a model without them cannot run the agent. A model that declines to state the capability is treated as lacking it rather than guessed into the picker. Discovery is best-effort and cached per catalog URL. Any failure — no credential, unreachable host, empty catalog — degrades to the router's `auto` model, which selects server-side and so works with no catalog at all. That is why `auto` is the sole `fallback_models` entry: pinning stale ids there would route users to models an upstream may have retired. ## Related Issue Closes #85666 Relationship to #85716, which also implements this issue: that PR is a plain declarative profile with `fallback_models=()`, `default_aux_model=""`, and no catalog override, so it relies on the base `fetch_models` hitting `/v1/models` with `Bearer`. If that endpoint does not serve the router catalog, the `/model` picker is left empty and users must type a full model id by hand. This PR adds the catalog path/auth/shape handling, the `auto` fallback, an aux model, and `INWORLD_BASE_URL`. Happy to fold this into that PR instead if maintainers prefer it there — the goal is a working integration, not authorship. ## Type of Change - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) ## Changes Made - `plugins/model-providers/inworld/__init__.py` — `ProviderProfile` with `fetch_models` override for the router catalog - `plugins/model-providers/inworld/plugin.yaml` — manifest - `tests/providers/test_inworld_profile.py` — 22 tests: registration/aliases, catalog parsing, and fetch behaviour - `website/docs/integrations/providers.md` — CLI example, base-URL override, model-ID note - `website/docs/reference/environment-variables.md` — `INWORLD_API_KEY`, `INWORLD_BASE_URL` Everything else wires up from the registry: credential resolution, `--provider inworld`, the `hermes model` menu, `hermes setup`, `provider:model` aliases, runtime resolution, and the doctor health check. ## How to Test 1. Put `INWORLD_API_KEY` in `~/.hermes/.env` (get one at https://portal.inworld.ai/) 2. `hermes model` → **Inworld** → the live catalog lists tool-calling models, with `auto` first 3. `hermes chat --provider inworld --model auto -q "Say hello"` 4. Unset the key and re-run step 2 — the picker still offers `auto` rather than failing Verify the registry wiring directly: ```python from hermes_cli.runtime_provider import resolve_runtime_provider resolve_runtime_provider(requested="inworld") # {'provider': 'inworld', 'api_mode': 'chat_completions', # 'base_url': 'https://api.inworld.ai/v1', 'source': 'env:INWORLD_API_KEY'} ``` ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate — see the note on #85716 above - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this feature - [x] I've run the tests and they pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes - [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 15 (Darwin 25.5.0), Python 3.11 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (`website/docs/`) - [x] N/A — no new config keys, so `cli-config.yaml.example` is unchanged - [x] N/A — no architecture or workflow change - [x] Cross-platform: pure-Python, no file I/O, no process or terminal handling - signal.title: fix(wake): stop client-capture wake from arming a deaf listener and blaming the wrong machine
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Three bugs on the `wake_word.capture: client` path (desktop streams PCM to a remote backend). Together they made "hey Hermes" appear broken with no usable diagnosis. **1. Auto-arm died silently after every backend restart.** `armWakeWord` awaits `wake.status` before `wake.start`, but only `wake.start` carried the 180s timeout. `wake.status` runs the same requirements probe (imports faster-whisper, TTS and tflite on a cold backend), blew the 30s default, and threw into a bare `catch {}`. The ear never came back and showed no reason — while a manual click still worked, which reads as a UI bug rather than a timeout. Several "wake is still broken" reports turned out to have nothing listening at all. **2. The silent-audio hint pointed at the wrong machine.** Under client capture the microphone is on the *desktop*; the backend host has none. The hint unconditionally said "grant the Hermes backend microphone access", which sends users to debug a machine that was never involved. It also collapsed two distinct failures — no frames arrived (desktop never opened its mic) versus silent frames (desktop opened a virtual loopback like BlackHole/MMAudio) — into one message, discarding the only signal that separates them. **3. `wake.status` surfaced the backend's own PortAudio error** (`Wake-word input device could not be resolved: Error querying device -1`) as the ear's tooltip even under client capture, where the backend is *not supposed to* have a mic. Now gated on the effective capture mode. Also adds a log line on the no-PCM path, which previously set `audio_silent` with no log at all, and exposes `frames_seen` via `detector_frame_info()` so the two failures stay distinguishable. Timing already tells you which one you have — the silence alert after ~10s means frames arrived but were silent, after ~38s means no frames arrived (0.25s queue timeout x 125) — but nothing recorded it. ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) ## Changes Made - `tools/wake_word.py` — `silent_audio_hint()` takes `external_audio` + `frames_seen` and branches on them; `_external_frames_seen` tracking; log on the no-PCM path; `frames_seen` exposed via `detector_frame_info()` - `tui_gateway/server.py` — `wake.status` passes the capture flags through and no longer reports a backend device error under client capture - `apps/desktop/src/lib/wake-client-capture.ts` — enumerate inputs, deprioritise known virtual loopbacks by label, and probe each candidate for any nonzero sample before committing - `apps/desktop/src/store/wake-word.ts` — surface the silent-mic notice in the ear tooltip; `wake.status` gets the same 180s timeout as `wake.start` - `tests/tools/test_wake_silent_audio_hint.py` — new The device probe uses an **exact-zero** test rather than a loudness threshold: a real mic in a silent room still has a noise floor, while a virtual or dead input is bit-perfect zeros. `noiseSuppression` is turned off for the probe because a gate can zero a quiet room and defeat it; `echoCancellation` stays on so Hermes' own TTS cannot trigger its wake word. ## How to test Reproducing #2 needs a host with no real input device, which is the configuration that makes client capture worth using: ```bash # hint branches, no hardware needed pytest tests/tools/test_wake_silent_audio_hint.py -v ``` Manually, with `wake_word.capture: client` and a desktop connected to a remote backend: 1. Restart the backend, then watch the desktop auto-arm — before this, the ear silently stayed off; now a `wake.start` line appears in the log. 2. Select a virtual loopback (BlackHole) as the desktop's default input. The tooltip now says the *desktop* is streaming silence, and names loopbacks as the cause, instead of telling you to grant the backend mic access. ## What platforms Tested on macOS 15.5 (Apple Silicon): backend on a Mac mini with zero input devices, desktop on a Mac Studio over Tailscale. The hint tests cover the win32/linux branches via patched `sys.platform`; the desktop-side device probe is browser API code and platform-independent, but I have not exercised it on Windows or Linux hardware.

signal.title: feat(tts): add a MiniMax chunked-PCM streaming provider
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? `tts.provider: minimax` had no chunked API, so `resolve_streaming_provider` returned `None` and the desktop fell back to synthesizing an entire reply, base64-encoding it, and shipping one data URL. Over a remote gateway that means multi-megabyte payloads and a 15s playback watchdog with nothing to re-arm it — replies simply fail with "Playback stalled". The only workaround was pointing `tts.streaming.provider` at a different, paid provider, which also silently changes the user's voice. MiniMax's `/v1/t2a_v2` already supports what the streaming interface wants: `stream: true` plus `audio_setting.format = "pcm"` emits SSE `data:` lines whose `data.audio` is hex-encoded PCM at the requested sample rate. No decode or transcode step, so frames go straight to the client's Web Audio scheduler. Region, endpoint, credential and voice all resolve through the **same** helpers as the sync path (`_resolve_minimax_tts_runtime`, the `tts.minimax` section), so enabling streaming cannot silently change the configured voice. ## Type of Change - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) ## Changes Made - `tools/tts_streaming.py` — `MiniMaxStreamer`, registered as `minimax` - `hermes_cli/web_server.py` — one-line-per-reply summary of frames/bytes/duration actually sent - `tests/tools/test_tts_minimax_streaming.py` — new ### The summary-event trap MiniMax terminates the stream with a **summary** event (`status=2`, carrying `extra_info`) whose `data.audio` is the *entire utterance repeated*, not a final increment. Yielding it makes every sentence play twice at exactly 2x the bytes. The streamer filters on `status == 2 or extra_info`. Worth flagging for reviewers because of how it hides: a round-trip check does **not** catch it — Whisper transcribes the duplicated audio back to one clean sentence. Only duration/byte count reveals it. `test_summary_event_is_not_yielded` pins this; removing the filter fails that test and `test_extra_info_alone_marks_a_summary_event`, and nothing else. That is also why the reply summary log line is here. It is the only signal separating "the backend never produced audio" from "the client never played what it was sent" — identical from the UI, and without it a silent-playback report cannot be falsified. ## How to test ```bash pytest tests/tools/test_tts_minimax_streaming.py -v # no network ``` End to end, with `tts.provider: minimax` and a MiniMax key: ```python from hermes_cli.config import load_config import tools.tts_streaming as ts, time inst = ts.resolve_streaming_provider(load_config()["tts"]) t = time.monotonic(); first = None; total = 0 for c in inst.stream("Short spoken sentence for timing."): first = first or time.monotonic() - t total += len(c) print(first, total / (inst.sample_rate * 2)) # first-chunk secs, audio secs ``` Check the reported audio duration against the text — roughly `words / 2.6` seconds. A ~2x ratio means the summary event is being yielded. ## Measurements On a Mac mini M4, `speech-02-turbo`, 18-word utterance: | | first chunk | audio produced | |---|---|---| | previous chunked provider (ElevenLabs) | 3.65s | — | | MiniMaxStreamer | **0.80s** | 5.18s of audio in 1.73s wall | Generation runs faster than realtime, so playback never starves. A 107s reply streamed in 13s. ## What platforms Tested on macOS 15.5 (Apple Silicon), backend serving a desktop client over Tailscale. The provider is `requests` + SSE with no platform-specific code; the unit tests are network-free and run anywhere.

signal.title: fix(desktop): honour voice.silence_duration instead of hardcoding 1250ms
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? The desktop conversation loop passed a literal `silenceMs: 1_250`, so `voice.silence_duration` existed in config and in the setup wizard but only ever drove the CLI path in `tools/voice_mode.py`. On the desktop the key was silently inert — setting it changed nothing, with no warning that it had been ignored. That value is dead air at the end of **every** spoken turn: the user has stopped talking and the loop is still waiting before it will even begin transcribing. It is the cheapest latency in the whole voice pipeline to tune, and it was the one knob a user could not reach. ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) ## Changes Made - `apps/desktop/src/store/voice-prefs.ts` — mirror `voice.silence_duration` into a store atom alongside the other `voice.*` prefs, clamped to 300-3000ms - `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-hermes-config.ts` — apply it when config loads - `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-voice-conversation.ts` — read the atom instead of the literal - `apps/desktop/src/types/hermes.ts` — type the config key The clamp is deliberate in both directions: below ~300ms an ordinary mid-sentence pause cuts the speaker off, and above 3s the turn feels broken rather than patient. Absent or malformed config keeps the previous 1250ms, so nothing changes for anyone who has not set the key. ## How to test 1. Set `voice.silence_duration: 0.7` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` 2. Restart the desktop app and start a voice conversation 3. Stop speaking and time the gap before transcription begins — ~0.7s, previously always ~1.25s regardless of the setting To confirm the clamp, set `0.05` and `30`: both fall back to the 300ms / 3000ms bounds rather than being applied literally. ```bash cd apps/desktop && npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json # passes clean ``` ## What platforms Tested on macOS 15.5 (Apple Silicon), desktop app against a remote backend over Tailscale. The change is renderer-side config plumbing with no platform-specific code. ## Note I have not been able to find an existing test suite covering the desktop conversation loop's timing behaviour, so this ships with a typecheck only. Happy to add a vitest case if you can point me at the pattern you'd want for the store atoms.

signal.title: [Feature]: Bridge $currentProvider into host.state so plugins can show the live provider
signal.text: ## Summary The plugin SDK bridges the live model (`host.state.model`) but not the live provider, even though the app store holds it (`$currentProvider`). A status-bar plugin that shows `provider · model` at a glance (to catch misconfigured provider kicks) therefore displays the *configured* provider, not the one actually selected for the session. ## Repro 1. Install a status-bar plugin reading `host.state.model` + `config.get {key:'full'}` → `config.model.provider` (the standard recipe). 2. Open the model picker and select provider `nous`, model `longcat`. 3. The pill updates to `… · longcat` (model is bridged) but the provider segment still shows the configured default (`opencode-go`). Expected: the pill shows `nous · longcat` — the pair the user actually selected. ## Why The picker writes **two separate atoms** (`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-model-controls.ts:183-184`): ```ts setCurrentModel(selection.model) setCurrentProvider(selection.provider) ``` but `host.state` bridges only one of them (`apps/desktop/src/sdk/index.ts:59-73`): ```ts state: { activeSessionId: readonlyAtom<null | string>($activeSessionId), cwd: readonlyAtom<string>($currentCwd), gateway: readonlyAtom<string>($gatewayState), /** Current main model slug. */ model: readonlyAtom<string>($currentModel), profile: readonlyAtom<string>($activeGatewayProfile), viewport: readonlyAtom<ViewportRect>($viewport) } ``` The provider atom exists and is persisted (`apps/desktop/src/store/session.ts:569`): ```ts export const $currentProvider = atom(storedString(COMPOSER_PROVIDER_KEY) ?? '') ``` Plugins have no RPC door to it either (the `/api/model/info` bridge endpoint is desktop-bridge-only, not reachable from a plugin). ## Proposed fix Mirror the `model` atom — add to `host.state`: ```ts /** Current main provider slug. */ provider: readonlyAtom<string>($currentProvider), ``` The import for `$currentProvider` is already in the SDK module's dependency chain (same store file as `$currentModel`). ~3 lines, no behavioral change for existing plugins (additive surface). ## Notes - The composer's own UI reads the same `$currentProvider` atom (`model-picker-overlay.tsx:26`), so the value bridged would be exactly what the picker shows. - Per-session overrides (tile/session-scoped picks) write the same atoms via `sessionTileDelegate().updateSession(…)` confirm path — the bridge would reflect the primary session the way `model` already does.

signal.title: Desktop: pin/unpin still reverted by a list page that lands after the PATCH ack (follow-up to #74570)
signal.text: ## Bug After the #74570 fix (`090d14647`), a fresh local pin/unpin is protected **while the PATCH is in flight** (`unconfirmed` guard). But the guard is cleared on the PATCH's own ack, and a **session-list request issued before the write can land after the ack** still carrying the pre-write value. The pull pass then reads that stale row with no guard left and reverts the user's action — and because the reverted state is pushed back to the server by the next reconcile, the wrong value becomes durable. User-visible symptom: pin/unpin works **intermittently** — clicking "unpin" in the sidebar sometimes sticks, sometimes instantly reverts and the session stays pinned (the server row is re-PATCHed back to `pinned=true` by the resurrection). ## Timeline (unpin example) ``` t-1 list request #N issued (server row still pinned=true) <- stale page in flight t0 user unpins -> reconcile -> PATCH pinned=false issued <- unconfirmed.set(id, false) t1 PATCH ack -> unconfirmed.delete(id) <- guard gone (090d14647 clears on ack) t2 list response #N lands (pinned=true) -> $sessions change -> reconcile -> pullRemotePins() -> no pending, no unconfirmed -> row.pinned && !heldLocally -> pinSession() -> PIN RESURRECTED t3 resurrection fires reconcile -> PATCH pinned=true -> server row flipped back ``` The symmetric race hits pin too (stale `pinned=false` page after a pin's ack -> `unpinSession()`). Why the ack is not enough: the `unconfirmed` guard's lifetime is the PATCH request itself, but the stale list page's lifetime can be longer — list requests are heavier and slower, and `refreshSessions()` runs on every `message.complete`/turn/focus, so the window is real and recurring. ## Evidence - `pullRemotePins()` in `apps/desktop/src/store/session-pin-sync.ts` (current main): `unconfirmed` is deleted in `writePin()`'s `.then()` — the pull pass can no longer distinguish "page issued before the write" from "genuinely newer truth" once the ack landed. - The existing test `ignores a stale page that contradicts a write still in flight` only covers a stale page arriving **before** the ack; the post-ack window is untested. Its final assertion ("once acked, later server truth is honoured") assumes every post-ack page is new — not true for requests issued pre-write. - Reproduced in practice on macOS (Desktop 0.17.0 build containing `090d14647`): a just-unpinned session reappears pinned in the sidebar and `sessions.pinned` in state.db reads back `1`. ## Suggested fix Keep the write guard until a list page **confirms the written value**, with a cooldown fallback so it can't go stale forever: - `writePin()`: record `{ value, at: Date.now() }` and do NOT clear on ack. - `pullRemotePins()`: if a guard exists for the row and `guard.value !== row.pinned` **and** `Date.now() - guard.at < COOLDOWN_MS` (e.g. 5s), skip the row (stale page). Otherwise delete the guard and reconcile normally — the page confirms the write, or is old enough that it must be fresh truth. - A failed PATCH still clears the guard so later pages are honoured. This preserves the cross-app sync (a genuinely newer page from another app is adopted) while closing the post-ack stale-page window. I have a working patch + regression tests (pin and unpin directions, guard confirmation, cooldown expiry) ready to open as a PR if this approach is accepted. ## Environment - Hermes Desktop 0.17.0 (build containing `090d14647`), Hermes Agent v0.19.x, macOS 27.0 (arm64) - Upstream main @ `4983c576b` — `apps/desktop/src/store/session-pin-sync.ts` unchanged since `090d14647`

signal.title: fix(desktop): persist dropped screenshot bytes before attach
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Fixes macOS Finder screenshot drops that preview correctly in Desktop but fail when the prompt is submitted with `image not found`. Finder can expose the dropped screenshot through a short-lived `TemporaryItems/NSIRD_screencaptureui...` path. Desktop previously preferred that native path over the dropped `File` bytes. The preview could read the file immediately, but `image.attach` later received the same path after macOS had removed it. Native image drops now persist the `File` bytes into Desktop's composer-image cache first. The attachment therefore carries a durable path through prompt submission, while the native path remains a compatibility fallback if buffer persistence is unavailable. ## Related Issue Discord support report: https://discord.com/channels/1053877538025386074/1536857447917031535 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/hooks/use-composer-actions.ts`: persist native dropped-image bytes before trusting the OS-provided path. - `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/hooks/use-composer-actions.test.ts`: cover a disappearing macOS screenshot path and prove the attachment uses the durable composer-image path instead. ## How to Test 1. On macOS, take a screenshot and drag the saved screenshot from Finder or Desktop into a normal Hermes Desktop conversation. 2. Wait briefly, then submit the prompt. The image should remain attached and reach the agent without an `image not found` error for the temporary screenshot path. 3. signal.title: Add a "Move session to project" action in Desktop
signal.text: ## Problem If a session is created under the wrong project, or later needs to be reorganized, there is currently no clear way to move it to another project. Because project membership is derived from workspace/CWD state, users can end up with sessions under an unexpected project or auto-project. Once that happens, the only practical option is to leave the session where it is or edit internal state manually. ## Suggested UX Add a simple action for non-running local sessions: - `Move to project...` - `Move to Home / detached` Possible entry points: - session context menu - drag-and-drop between project groups - command palette ## Expected behavior For a stopped local Desktop/CLI session: 1. Choose a target project. 2. Reassign the session workspace to that project's primary path. 3. Clear or recompute stale Git workspace metadata if necessary. 4. Refresh the session list and `projects.tree` so the session immediately appears in the new project. For `Move to Home`, the session should become detached instead of inheriting another project's workspace. Running sessions, cron runs, messaging-platform sessions, subagent sessions, and tool sessions can simply have this action disabled. ## Why The current project model is powerful, but without a move action, one mistaken or unexpected session placement is difficult to correct. This would also complement #75537, which requests predictable creation rules: - Global New Chat -> Home - Project + -> session inside that project Even with predictable creation, users still need a way to reorganize existing sessions. Thanks for considering it!

signal.title: fix(setup): pin kittentts wheel sha256 — refuse tampered third-party releases
signal.text: fix(setup): pin kittentts wheel sha256 — refuse tampered third-party releases ## Who should enable this Anyone who runs `hermes setup` and selects **KittenTTS** as the local TTS provider (or any user who trusts a pip install from a third-party GitHub release). The change is in the install path — no config change, no user action needed. ## Platform compatibility | Platform | Compatibility | |---|---| | macOS | ✅ Verified (sha256 verify + tamper-detection harness, py_compile, ruff) | | Linux | ✅ Same Python code path | | Windows | ✅ Same Python code path (wheel download via curl is available on Windows 10+; identical verification logic) | ## Quick-start guide 1. `hermes update` (or pull this PR branch) 2. Run `hermes setup` → choose KittenTTS 3. Installer now: downloads the wheel → verifies sha256 against the pinned hash → installs the local file only on match 4. Success message shows `kittentts installed (wheel sha256 verified)` ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Cause | Fix | |---|---|---| | `kittentts wheel sha256 mismatch (expected 482a436c…, got …)` | Release artifact tampered/replaced, or upstream bumped the wheel without a version bump | Refused to install (fail-closed). If upstream legitimately rebuilt 0.8.1, update BOTH the URL and the pinned hash in `hermes_cli/tools_config.py` | | `kittentts wheel download failed: …` | Network can't reach GitHub release | Manual hint preserved: `uv pip install -U '<wheel_url>' soundfile` | | `kittentts install failed: …` | pip-level failure | Manual hint preserved with the full URL | --- ## Story: a wheel is code, and this one shipped off-PyPI The #81883 supply-chain review (mirror fallback must never self-issue integrity proof for executable content) has a sibling in the post-setup hooks: KittenTTS is installed by pip-installing a wheel URL straight from a third-party GitHub release. A wheel is **executable code** — pip runs build/import hooks at install time — and the release was version-pinned but byte-unverified. A compromised KittenML release (or a replaced artifact on the same tag) would execute attacker code in the venv with zero indication. The fix applies the same principle as the mirror work: **executable content must be verified against a proof that didn't come from its supplier.** The wheel is downloaded to a temp file, its sha256 is compared against the hash recorded from the official 0.8.1 artifact, and only a match gets installed. Mismatch is fail-closed with expected/got printed — the user sees a refusal, not silent code execution. ## Design decisions - **Download-then-verify-then-install-local** instead of `pip install <url>`: verification happens before pip ever touches the bytes. - **Fail-closed**: sha mismatch → refusal. The old code would have installed anything. - **Hash pinned with the URL**: version bump must update both together (comment in code). - **Temp file cleaned up** in `finally`; no leftover artifact. - **No UX regression**: one extra ~22KB download step inside the existing flow; all failure messages keep the manual-install hint. ## Security review - Wheel bytes are verified against a hash recorded from the official artifact — the supplier can no longer silently swap code. - Mismatch = refusal, never a warning-then-continue. - The hash is embedded in the repo (defense-in-depth: attacker who compromises only the release cannot change what our code expects; attacker who compromises our repo has bigger problems). - No new network surface beyond the existing wheel URL; download uses the same curl flags as other fetches (`--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120`). ## Self-test ``` VERIFY OK # real 0.8.1 wheel hash matches the pinned value TAMPER DETECTED # single-byte flip → sha mismatch detected py_compile clean ruff clean ```

signal.title: [Bug]: hermes config set agent.reasoning_effort emits a false unrecognized-key warning
signal.text: ### Bug Description `agent.reasoning_effort` is a documented and runtime-consumed configuration key, but setting it through `hermes config set` emits an unrecognized-key warning. The value is still saved to `config.yaml` and returned by `hermes config get`, so the problem is the false warning rather than persistence or runtime behavior. This report concerns the scalar global key `agent.reasoning_effort`, not the per-model `agent.reasoning_overrides` mapping. The documentation only excludes nested `reasoning_overrides` entries from `hermes config set` because model names may contain dots. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Run: ```shell hermes config set agent.reasoning_effort high ``` 2. Observe the warning. 3. Confirm that the value was saved: ```shell hermes config get agent.reasoning_effort ``` ### Expected Behavior Because `agent.reasoning_effort` is a documented and runtime-supported key, it should be saved without an unrecognized-key warning. If `/reasoning high --global` is intentionally the only supported setter, the CLI should direct users to that command instead of saying Hermes may not read the saved value. ### Actual Behavior The value is saved, ```text ✓ Set agent.reasoning_effort = high in <config path> ``` but the CLI prints: ```text ⚠ 'agent.reasoning_effort' is not a recognized config key — it was saved anyway, but Hermes may not read it. Did you mean: agent.reasoning_overrides ``` `hermes config get agent.reasoning_effort` subsequently returns: ```text high ``` ### Affected Component CLI (interactive chat), Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup) ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) N/A (CLI only) ### Debug Report ```shell hermes debug share output can be attached if needed. ``` ### Operating System Debian 13 ### Python Version 3.13.5 ### Hermes Version 0.20.0 ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) _No response_ ### Proposed Fix (optional) _No response_ ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

signal.title: Fix/per profile remote ws routing
signal.text: # PR: fix(desktop): per-profile remote overrides attach chat WS to the local primary ## What A Desktop profile configured with its own remote gateway override (connection.json `profiles[name] = { mode: "remote", url, token }`) silently runs its chat on the **local** primary backend: - new sessions on the remote profile identify as the local host (e.g. macOS) - resuming a remote-native session fails with "session not found" - REST (session list, fs, git) correctly hits the remote via the override Regression from #85665 (d16e2366d), merged 2026-08-13. ## Root cause `sharedPrimaryRoute()` (apps/desktop/src/store/gateway.ts) decides a profile is "served by the shared primary" when the descriptor has a `.profile` field: ```ts return Boolean(conn && typeof conn === 'object' && (conn as { profile?: string }).profile) ``` But **two** routes produce a `.profile`-tagged descriptor: 1. Shared-primary (case 3, global remote): `ensureBackend` returns `{ ...connection, profile: route.descriptorProfile }` — the intended target of the check. 2. **Per-profile remote override (case 2): `spawnPoolBackend` returns `{ ...remote, profile, ... }` (electron/main.ts:8117) — the pool descriptor is tagged with the profile name too.** The check cannot distinguish them, so a per-profile remote override is misclassified as shared-primary → `ensureGatewayForProfile` activates the PRIMARY (local) socket instead of dialing the profile's remote WS. The commit message claims "per-profile remote overrides are untouched (pinned by test)" — the test missed the `spawnPoolBackend` return path. ## Fix Tag only the true shared-primary descriptor with a dedicated marker and check for that, not `.profile`: - `electron/main.ts` — primary route with `descriptorProfile`: `{ ...connection, profile: route.descriptorProfile, sharedPrimary: true }` - `apps/desktop/src/store/gateway.ts` — `sharedPrimaryRoute` checks `conn.sharedPrimary === true`; pool descriptors never carry the marker. Covers both callers (`openGatewayForProfile` pre-warm and `ensureGatewayForProfile`) — the whole bug class, not just one path. ## Reproduction 1. Local primary profile; add a second profile with a remote gateway override. 2. Select the remote profile; open/resume a session. 3. Chat answers from the LOCAL host; remote sessions say "session not found", while the sidebar (REST) lists remote sessions. ## Test - Unit: `sharedPrimaryRoute` — descriptor `{ profile: 'x' }` → false; `{ profile: 'x', sharedPrimary: true }` → true (covers both route shapes). - E2E guidance: per-profile remote override + local primary must dial the override's WS URL (assert the chat socket target, not just REST). ## Related - #85237 (same config shape, different symptom) - #81198 (notes per-profile overrides worked pre-#85665)

signal.title: fix(models): use native Ollama tags without breaking generic discovery
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Use Ollama's native installed-model catalog for verified local Ollama endpoints, while preserving generic OpenAI-compatible discovery everywhere else. Local Ollama exposes its authoritative catalog at: ```text GET /api/tags ``` Hermes previously depended too heavily on `/v1/models` for discovery and model validation. A local Ollama deployment can expose the native catalog without exposing the OpenAI-compatible catalog, causing installed models to disappear from pickers or appear to be unavailable. ## Why this matters This PR makes model discovery follow the endpoint's actual protocol instead of the provider label alone: - verified local Ollama roots use `/api/tags`; - Ollama Cloud and ordinary custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints retain `/v1/models` discovery; - explicit model lists remain authoritative; - a reachable empty native catalog is distinct from an unreachable endpoint; - setup, picker, validation, model switching, and ACP catalog paths use the same discovery decision. That distinction prevents both failure modes: local Ollama models being hidden because `/v1/models` is unavailable, and generic or cloud endpoints being incorrectly forced through a local-only `/api/tags` path. ## Credential and origin safety Native catalog requests resolve configured `api_key`/`key_env` credentials and preserve explicitly supplied endpoint headers. Provider-configured credentials and headers are retained only for the matching normalized endpoint origin; they are not forwarded when an alias, fallback, or custom endpoint changes origin. Cache handling also preserves the protocol distinction: a reachable empty catalog can replace stale entries, while a transient probe failure can retain same-fingerprint stale data rather than turning an outage into an authoritative empty catalog. ## Scope and implementation The change is intentionally limited to model discovery and its existing consumers: - `hermes_cli/models.py`: native Ollama detection, `/api/tags` probing, URL normalization, credential/header handling, cache semantics, validation, and generic fallback; - `hermes_cli/model_setup_flows.py`, `hermes_cli/model_switch.py`, and `hermes_cli/main.py`: setup, picker, and switching parity; - `acp_adapter/server.py` and provider/runtime helpers: catalog identity and origin-safe propagation; - focused regression coverage across model discovery, validation, picker/setup, switching, ACP catalogs, cache state, URL normalization, headers, credentials, and cloud/custom exclusions. This is the active Vadelma-authored continuation of closed PR #49728, not a duplicate open implementation. The current series contains additional cache, URL, origin, header, credential-isolation, and selector-parity hardening beyond that predecessor. ## Why merge? The patch fixes a real local-Ollama compatibility gap without changing the generic provider contract. It keeps the server as the source of truth, preserves explicit configuration, fails conservatively on ambiguous endpoints, and exercises the same decision across the user-facing paths that consume model catalogs. The change is covered by deterministic regression tests and does not require a live model service for its hermetic verification. ## Related Issue No standalone issue. Supersedes closed PR #49728. ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## How to Test Validated on the exact published head `90c844718077a417676932311390479846288caf`. signal.title: test(kanban): preserve non-zero exit for delegated-child refusals
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Adds regression coverage for the delegated-child Kanban CLI process boundary. A delegated child is forbidden from mutating Kanban. The refusal must be visible both in the diagnostic output and in the process exit status: ```text $ HERMES_DELEGATED_CHILD_CONTEXT=1 hermes kanban comment <task-id> "text" kanban: delegate_task child contexts cannot mutate Kanban tasks via the CLI $ echo $? 1 ``` This PR launches `python -m hermes_cli.main` in real subprocesses, creates a disposable task in a temporary Hermes home, attempts the forbidden mutation with delegated-child context, and verifies both the refusal message and exit status `1`. ## Why this matters The existing guard and production exit-status propagation are already on `main`. The missing protection was at the real CLI process boundary. Without this regression test, a future change could continue printing the refusal while accidentally returning status `0`; shell scripts, CI jobs, cron workers, or agent orchestration could then interpret a rejected mutation as success. The existing delegated-isolation tests cover the guard in their own testing layer. This test adds distinct end-to-end process-boundary coverage for the user-visible CLI contract. ## Scope - Test-only change; no production behavior change. - Adds one regression test in `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_cli_exit_status.py`. - Clears ambient Kanban environment overrides so the subprocess uses the disposable test home. - Bounds each CLI subprocess with `timeout=30` so a startup or dispatch regression cannot hang the test worker indefinitely. ## Related Issue No linked issue; this PR preserves the delegated-child CLI exit-status contract already implemented on `main`. ## Type of Change - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_cli_exit_status.py`: exercise delegated-child refusal through separate CLI subprocesses. - Assert that the refusal is reported on stderr and returns exit status `1`. - Use a temporary Hermes home and remove ambient Kanban path overrides from the child environment. - Add a finite `timeout=30` to the subprocess helper. ## How to Test Validated on the exact published head `336c7cb734dc6c5bb84e97169376da6ed9301a3e` against base `main` `005dfcbfcc5d3384986bb276b6d5c788324d2559`: ```text scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_cli_exit_status.py -q 1 passed uv run --no-project --python 3.14 python -m py_compile \ hermes_cli/main.py hermes_cli/kanban.py \ tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_cli_exit_status.py git diff --check pass ``` The full repository suite and broader overlap suites were not run for this metadata refresh. The focused regression, syntax compilation, and diff check are the current exact-head evidence. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — the full repository suite was not run - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on Linux ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — N/A - [ ] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A - [ ] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact — the test uses Python subprocesses and standard environment handling - [ ] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A ## Provenance - Published head: `336c7cb734dc6c5bb84e97169376da6ed9301a3e` - Base `main`: `005dfcbfcc5d3384986bb276b6d5c788324d2559` - Source fork: `vadelma-agent/hermes-agent` - Human sponsor and review-response owner: @tmielika No external service or production Kanban database is modified by the test.

signal.title: test(gateway): make unset model override explicit in background fixture
signal.text: ## Summary Make the `/background` gateway tests exercise the real **no model override** path instead of a truthy mock value that looks like a persisted override. ## Why this matters `GatewayRunner` rehydrates a session's model override before starting a background task. In production, `SessionStore.get_model_override()` returns `None` when the user has not set a `/model` override. The test fixture used an unconfigured `MagicMock` session store. Its default return value is truthy, so the test could accidentally create a fake model override and pass a `MagicMock` into the session-scoped reasoning resolver. That means the test was not reliably exercising the normal no-override path, and its result could depend on mock behavior rather than the production contract. This is a test correctness issue: the fixture can mask regressions or fail for the wrong reason even though production behavior is unchanged. ## Fix Set: ```python mock_store.get_model_override.return_value = None ``` in `_make_runner()`, matching the real `SessionStore` contract. ## Scope - One test fixture in `tests/gateway/test_background_command.py`. - Four added lines; no production-code, dependency, configuration, or formatter changes. - Existing background-command scenarios now run with an explicit absent override. This should merge because it is a minimal, behavior-preserving correction that makes the gateway regression tests represent the production no-override state they intend to cover. ## Verification Against upstream `main` at `8d4b1e4b0e240af67c1f4eb6601aee99eac0bc49`, exact head `903c867cf8ba0d1737ae52d4ee296a71b09dd0aa`: ```text scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_background_command.py -q 7 passed uv run --extra dev ruff check tests/gateway/test_background_command.py All checks passed git diff --check refs/remotes/upstream/main...HEAD passed ``` The canonical test harness ran with its clean environment (`TZ=UTC`, `LANG=C.UTF-8`, `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`). ## Checklist - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] The change is narrowly scoped to one test fixture. - [x] The focused regression tests pass with `scripts/run_tests.sh`. - [x] Focused Ruff and whitespace checks pass. - [x] No production behavior, dependency, configuration, or platform adapter changes are included. - [x] The current upstream overlap and existing PR history were checked. signal.title: fix(profiles): prevent credential leaks and SQLite data loss in exports
signal.text: ## Summary Current `main` includes #83458, which force-redacts recognized secret-shaped strings in supported text files before profile archives are written. That substantially reduces risk, but it does not fully enforce the profile-export security boundary. Named-profile exports still exclude only the exact files `auth.json` and `.env`. Backups, renamed credential stores, opaque authorization state, private-key formats, binary databases, and sensitive caller-supplied extras can still enter a portable archive without matching the text redactor. This PR complements #83458 by adding structural path/type filtering before archive creation while retaining its final text-scrubbing pass. ## What this fixes - Excludes renamed and backup credential files at every copy depth. - Excludes canonical OAuth, token, pairing, and profile-home credential trees. - Excludes private PEM, PuTTY `.ppk`, and keystore formats while preserving public certificates. - Blocks sensitive paths supplied through `extra_files`. - Covers Feishu pairing state, reason-labelled credential-directory backups, and Hermes-generated corrupt-config backups. - Scrubs every explicitly portable dotenv template. - Creates consistent snapshots of live `.db`, `.sqlite`, and `.sqlite3` databases before omitting WAL/SHM/journal sidecars. - Preserves safe negative controls such as public certificates, ordinary same-named directories, desktop metadata, and non-sensitive rules files. ## Security impact Profile exports are intended to be portable and shareable. Exploitation requires a user to create and expose an archive, so this is not a passive remote vulnerability. However, affected archives can contain live credentials, private keys, pairing authorization state, or inconsistent database contents. Avoiding or manually sanitizing exports is the current workaround. ## Validation - 125 focused profile-export tests passed. - 100 profile/distribution tests passed, 2 skipped. - 103 SharedMetricsStore/SQLite-backup tests passed, 7 skipped. - Final immutable review run: 373 passed, 2 skipped. - Ruff, compilation, diff checks, and adversarial archive probes passed. - Final independent exact-SHA review found no blockers. The branch is 3 commits ahead, 0 behind current `main`, with contributor authorship preserved and no merge conflicts.

signal.title: fix(cron): clear tool-definitions cache after reloading .env
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Fixes a stale-cache bug that caused cron jobs with `enabled_toolsets: ["web", "file"]` to lose `web_search` / `web_extract` after the gateway process had previously computed tool definitions while the web backend was unavailable. Cron re-reads `.env` before every job so credential/provider changes take effect without a gateway restart. `model_tools.get_tool_definitions(quiet_mode=True)` memoizes results with a cache key that does **not** include env state, so a prior call made before `TAVILY_API_KEY` was available could permanently cache a `file`-only result. signal.title: fix(cli): drop the shell=True editor fallback in /prompt compose
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? `/prompt` opens `$VISUAL`/`$EDITOR` on a temp file. The primary launch path is safe (`subprocess.call([*shlex.split(editor), path])`), but if it raises for any reason the code falls back to `subprocess.call(f"{editor} {shlex.quote(path)}", shell=True)` at `hermes_cli/cli_commands_mixin.py:2871`. Only the temp path is quoted. The editor string comes straight from the environment, so shell metacharacters in `EDITOR` execute. The fallback is reachable in normal use: any `OSError` from the argv call lands there, for example an `EDITOR` whose flags parse into a binary that does not exist. This removes the fallback. The editor string is split once, run as argv, and a failure now cancels the compose by returning `""` instead of retrying through a shell. **Why this approach.** The fallback exists for editors whose values are not simple argv-splittable strings, but a shell retry cannot make that case safer, only less safe: anything the argv parser chokes on is exactly what a shell will happily reinterpret. Cancelling is the correct failure mode for an interactive compose, and it matches how the surrounding code already treats an empty buffer (no seed, no send). **Overlap with #59506.** That PR removes the same line, but bundles the change with a quick-commands rewrite, `tui_gateway` changes, docs and an `.aider` history file in one diff. This is the minimal standalone version, one function plus a regression test, so it can land on its own. Happy to close this if the maintainers would rather shepherd #59506 through. ## Related Issue Fixes #81364 ## Type of Change - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [x] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `hermes_cli/cli_commands_mixin.py`: delete the `shell=True` fallback in `_compose_in_editor`. The editor string is split into argv once (`ValueError` from `shlex.split` cancels), and any failure from the argv call returns `""` instead of retrying through a shell. - `tests/hermes_cli/test_prompt_compose_command.py`: new `test_editor_failure_never_falls_back_to_shell` drives an `EDITOR` the argv path cannot run and asserts the compose cancels and no invocation ever passes `shell=True`. ## How to Test 1. `EDITOR='nonexistent-editor; touch /tmp/pwned' hermes`, then `/prompt` 2. Before this change: the fallback runs the string through the shell and `/tmp/pwned` is created 3. After: the compose is cancelled, no shell runs, nothing is created Automated: ```bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_prompt_compose_command.py -q ``` One disclosure: `test_compose_reads_and_strips_header` in this file fails on Windows both before and after this change, because the test's fake editor is a `.sh` script that Windows cannot exec directly. It is a pre-existing platform issue, unrelated to this fix. The new test passes, and the file goes from 2/3 to 3/4 passing on Windows. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [x] I've run the test suite via `scripts/run_tests.sh` (targeted files, see How to Test) and all tests pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, Python 3.11.15 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A ## Screenshots / Logs N/A
