signal.title: fix(whatsapp): stop local bridge impersonation from hijacking messages
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? This change prevents an arbitrary local process from impersonating the WhatsApp bridge and intercepting or forging messages. It gives each WhatsApp session a persistent random secret, authenticates every bridge API request, and requires a challenge-bound proof before an existing listener can be reused. Legitimate bridge reuse across gateway restarts remains supported. ### Symptom A process that binds the configured local bridge port before Hermes starts can return the public bridge source hash from `/health`. Hermes then adopts that process as the WhatsApp bridge, accepts forged inbound messages from it, and sends outbound message payloads to it. ### Impact On a shared or compromised machine, another local process can silently read WhatsApp message traffic handled by Hermes or impersonate the user through bridge operations. The remote blast radius was not measured; the verified boundary is any process able to bind and serve the local bridge port under the same host. ### Bug Cause **Trigger:** `plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py` / `WhatsAppAdapter.connect()` reuses a listener whose unauthenticated `/health` response reports `connected` and the expected source hash. **Causal chain:** 1. A local process binds the configured bridge port before the managed bridge starts. 2. The adapter sends unauthenticated HTTP requests and treats the public source hash as sufficient identity for listener reuse. 3. The impostor receives outbound requests and supplies forged inbound responses as though it were the user's bridge. **Why it is wrong:** The source hash detects stale bridge code but is derivable from the shipped source, so it cannot authenticate a local process. The Host header guard only limits DNS rebinding and does not establish caller or server identity. **Working sibling / contrast:** A bridge spawned by Hermes can receive a per-session secret without user configuration. Persisting that secret in the session directory also lets a legitimate bridge prove its identity after a gateway restart. **Ruled out:** Binding only to `127.0.0.1` is not sufficient because the reported attacker is another process on the same host. Randomizing the port is unnecessary for identity once every endpoint and listener reuse are cryptographically authenticated. ### Fix - Generate and persist an owner-readable per-session bridge token, then pass it only to the managed bridge process. - Require a bearer token on every Express endpoint and configure every persistent adapter request to send it. - Bind health responses to a fresh adapter challenge with an HMAC proof before startup readiness or listener reuse succeeds. - Include the authentication helper in bridge staleness identity and refresh read-only installation mirrors without deleting `node_modules`. - Add Python and Node regressions for rejection, authenticated access, legitimate reuse, token lifecycle, and stale mirrored sources. ## Related Issue Closes #83395 ## Type of Change - [x] Security fix ## Changes Made - `plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py` - manage the bridge secret, authenticate requests, verify health proofs, and include authentication code in source identity. - `scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge.js` - protect all bridge routes and return challenge-bound health proofs. - `scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge_auth.js` - provide constant-time bearer validation and HMAC proof generation. - `gateway/platforms/whatsapp_common.py` - refresh packaged bridge mirrors while preserving installed dependencies. - `tests/gateway/` and `scripts/whatsapp-bridge/*.test.mjs` - cover authentication, reuse, token persistence, and stale-source behavior. ## How to Test 1. Start an unauthenticated fake listener on the configured bridge port and verify Hermes refuses to adopt it. 2. Start the managed bridge, verify missing or incorrect credentials receive HTTP 401, then restart the gateway and verify the authenticated existing bridge is reused. 3. Run the focused automated suites (verified locally: 12 Python tests and 25 Node tests passed on the reviewed tip): ```bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_whatsapp_bridge_auth.py tests/gateway/test_whatsapp_bridge_dir_resolution.py tests/gateway/test_whatsapp_stale_bridge.py node --test scripts/whatsapp-bridge/*.test.mjs node --check scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge.js node --check scripts/whatsapp-bridge/bridge_auth.js ``` ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [x] I've run the repository test entry on the relevant tests and all tests pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 10 with Python 3.11 and Node.js ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] Relevant documentation update: N/A - this change preserves the existing user-facing configuration. - [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` update: N/A - no configuration keys changed. - [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` update: N/A - no contributor workflow changed. - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility); token permissions use portable best-effort hardening. - [x] Tool descriptions/schemas update: N/A - no model tool behavior changed. ## Screenshots / Logs N/A - the verification is process and HTTP behavior covered by the commands above.

signal.title: [Bug]: PermissionError in _find_git_root() crashes system prompt building for gateway-mode agents
signal.text: ### Bug Description When an agent runs via hermes gateway run -p <profile>, the gateway bridges config.yaml’s terminal.cwd into the TERMINAL_CWD environment variable. During system prompt construction, build_context_files_prompt() calls resolve_context_cwd() which reads TERMINAL_CWD, then passes it to _find_git_root(Path(cwd)). If terminal.cwd points to a directory the agent process user cannot access (e.g., /root on a server where the agent runs as a non-root user like kduser), _find_git_root() crashes with: PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root/.git' This causes the entire system prompt build to fail, and the agent responds with “Sorry, I encountered an unexpected error” on every message. ### Steps to Reproduce Set terminal.cwd: /root in a profile’s config.yaml (this is the Docker sandbox default on many setups) Ensure the gateway process runs as a non-root user (e.g., kduser) that cannot access /root Start the agent via hermes gateway run -p <profile> Send a message to the agent (via webhook, yunzhijia, or any messaging platform) Agent responds with “Sorry, I encountered an unexpected error” — check agent.log for PermissionError ### Expected Behavior _find_git_root() should gracefully handle PermissionError by treating inaccessible directories as “no .git found” and continuing the search (or returning None). The system prompt should build successfully regardless of whether the cwd is accessible. ### Actual Behavior Traceback (most recent call last): File "/var/lib/hermes-agent/agent/system_prompt.py", line 473, in build_system_prompt_parts context_files_prompt = _r.build_context_files_prompt( File "/var/lib/hermes-agent/agent/prompt_builder.py", line 2074, in build_context_files_prompt _load_hermes_md(cwd_path, context_length) File "/var/lib/hermes-agent/agent/prompt_builder.py", line 1921, in _load_hermes_md hermes_md_path = _find_hermes_md(cwd_path) File "/var/lib/hermes-agent/agent/prompt_builder.py", line 100, in _find_hermes_md stop_at = _find_git_root(cwd) File "/var/lib/hermes-agent/agent/prompt_builder.py", line 85, in _find_git_root if (parent / ".git").exists(): File "/usr/lib/python3.11/pathlib.py", line 1236, in exists self.stat() File "/usr/lib/python3.11/pathlib.py", line 1014, in stat return os.stat(self, follow_symlinks=follow_symlinks) PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root/.git' ### Affected Component Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp) ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) N/A (CLI only) ### Debug Report ```shell <!-- Run hermes debug share and paste links here --> ``` ### Operating System Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (5.15.0-179-generic) ### Python Version Python 3.11.x ### Hermes Version v0.19.0 (git: v2026.7.20-995-ga61183b56f) ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell See Actual Behavior above for full traceback. ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) agent/prompt_builder.py, line 85, in _find_git_root(): def _find_git_root(start: Path) -> Optional[Path]: current = start.resolve() for parent in [current, *current.parents]: if (parent / ".git").exists(): # ← .exists() raises PermissionError on inaccessible dirs return parent return None Path.exists() calls os.stat(), which raises PermissionError when the directory itself is not accessible — not just when .git doesn’t exist. The function has no try/except PermissionError. Why it only affects gateway mode: gateway/run.py bridges config.yaml’s terminal.cwd into os.environ["TERMINAL_CWD"] (line ~2072-2087). resolve_context_cwd() in system_prompt.py reads TERMINAL_CWD and passes it to build_context_files_prompt(cwd=...). In CLI/Web UI mode, TERMINAL_CWD is not set, so resolve_context_cwd() returns None and build_context_files_prompt falls back to os.getcwd() — which is typically the user’s accessible home directory. Why /root: Docker sandbox deployments commonly set terminal.cwd: /root (the container’s default home). This works inside the container (overlay filesystem), but the gateway process runs on the host as a non-root user who cannot access /root. Verified: upstream origin/main also unfixed — same code without try/except PermissionError. ### Proposed Fix (optional) def _find_git_root(start: Path) -> Optional[Path]: current = start.resolve() for parent in [current, *current.parents]: try: if (parent / ".git").exists(): return parent except PermissionError: continue return None One-line try/except PermissionError — skip inaccessible directories, return None if no .git found. ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

signal.title: [Feature]: Live upgrade — update Hermes without killing running subagents (zero-downtime update)
signal.text: ## Summary Currently, updating Hermes (via `hermes update`, WebUI auto-update, or cron-triggered update) kills ALL running subagents. This is because subagents are child processes of the parent Hermes — when the parent restarts, children become orphaned zombies. **The result:** users who click "update" in the WebUI, or have an automatic cron update, lose all in-progress subagent work. Long-running delegations (kanban workers, batch processing, research tasks) are silently killed. ## The Problem - **WebUI update** → version mismatch → blocks user → restart kills subagents - **Cron auto-update** → `hermes update` runs → gateway restarts → subagents orphaned - **CLI update** → user runs `hermes update` → unaware subagents will die - **Recovery:** impossible — subagent results lost forever, no checkpoint ## Proposed Solution: Blue-Green Live Upgrade ### Architecture (blue-green pattern) ```text BEFORE: Hermes(old) → [Subagent A, B, C running] DURING: Hermes(old) draining → [Subagents finish naturally] Hermes(new) ready on staging port AFTER: Hermes(new) → socket migration → old exits ``` ### Implementation for v1: Checkpoint + Orphan Adoption (~50-100 lines) 1. **Checkpoint file**: before restart, serialize all active subagent state (session_id, goal, pid) to `$HERMES_HOME/state/subagent_checkpoints.json` 2. **Orphan recovery on startup**: new Hermes process scans checkpoint, checks alive PIDs via `os.kill(pid, 0)`, re-attaches via `os.waitpid` 3. **Result collection**: subagents that finish during update — their stdout/stderr are still in the pipe buffer **Key insight:** orphaned subagents dont die — they keep running until they try to write to a broken pipe. We just pick up their exit status. ## Advantages | Aspect | Before | After | |--------|--------|-------| | WebUI update | Blocks + kills subagents | Zero-downtime | | Cron auto-update | Jobs lost | Jobs complete naturally | | Kanban workers | Reset from zero | Continue where they left off | | Long research tasks | Results lost forever | Results preserved | | Reliability | Low (update = risk) | High (update = safe) | | Auto-update adoption | Users hesitate | Fully automatic | ## Related - #70755 — WebUI auto-reload (complementary) - #70721 — Plugin update guard (different scope) --- Would be happy to contribute the implementation if the direction is acceptable.

signal.title: feat(approval): surface invisible Unicode, control bytes, and padding in approval prompts (Claude Code v2.1.223-inspired)
signal.text: ## Summary Approval prompts can no longer be lied to: invisible Unicode, terminal control bytes, and whitespace-padding runs in a dangerous command are now rendered as visible escape markers in every approval surface, so the human approver sees exactly what will execute. Port of Claude Code v2.1.223's approval-dialog hardening ("Fixed permission prompts so commands padded with tabs or invisible Unicode can no longer hide part of the command from the approval dialog"), adapted for Hermes' CLI + gateway approval paths. **Source:** [Claude Code changelog v2.1.223, Aug 6 2026](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog#2-1-223) · [GitHub release](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.223) ## The problem The displayed copy of a command in an approval prompt could diverge from what runs, three ways: 1. **Invisible/format Unicode** — zero-width chars, bidi embeddings/overrides/isolates (Trojan Source), variation selectors, and the U+E0000 tag block render as nothing in terminals and chat platforms. 2. **Raw control bytes** — an embedded ANSI/OSC escape can erase or recolor the just-printed prompt line; a bare `\r` lets the tail overwrite the visible head. 3. **Whitespace padding** — a few hundred spaces/tabs push the dangerous tail out of view, or past the gateway's ~200-char preview truncation, where it silently disappears. Secrets were already redacted at every display-mint site (`redact_sensitive_text`), but none of these display-integrity classes were handled. ## How our implementation differs from Claude Code's | | Claude Code | Hermes | |---|---|---| | Behavior | Undisclosed (closed source); prompt "no longer hides" the command | Hidden content made **visible** as escape markers (`\u202e`, `\x1b`), padding collapsed to explicit `⟨+300 whitespace chars⟩` markers — literal IOCs preserved for the approver, per house policy | | Surfaces | Terminal permission dialog | CLI prompt, gateway dangerous-command / execute_code / tool-approval payloads (Telegram, Discord, Slack, …), pending-approval fallbacks | | Execution | — | Display-only: the executed command, smart-approval assessment, and pattern-key persistence are untouched | Legitimate formatting is preserved: `\t`, `\n`, and short space runs pass through untouched; clean commands are byte-identical. ## Changes - `agent/redact.py`: new `sanitize_command_for_display()` + character classes (invisible Unicode incl. tag block, C0/C1 minus `\t`/`\n`, padding-run collapse) - `tools/approval.py`: composed onto redaction at all 5 display-mint sites (CLI prompt, gateway dangerous-command payload, execute_code payload, tool-approval payload, pending fallbacks) - `gateway/run.py`: `_redact_approval_command()` now sanitizes too (covers gateway + api_server event path) - `tests/agent/test_sanitize_command_display.py`: 25 tests incl. gateway-wiring checks ## Validation | Check | Result | |---|---| | New tests | 25/25 | | `tests/agent/test_redact.py` | 97/97 | | `tests/tools/test_approval.py` + mode parity | 103/103 | | Gateway approval-format tests | 10 passed, 1 skipped | | E2E (real imports, CLI callback + gateway redactor + fallback formatter) | zero-width/RLO/ESC/CR all surfaced as escapes; dangerous tail visible after padding collapse; clean commands byte-identical | | ruff + py_compile | clean | ## Infographic ![Approval prompt integrity infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aa57215/yXYR5qQZShbCd21zMhFrG_8NbMVzFS.png)

signal.title: fix(redact): stop over-rejecting safe plugin redaction patterns
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Stops the two redaction-registry validators from rejecting safe plugin patterns. Because registration fails soft (warning log, pattern skipped), every over-rejection meant a vendor token silently going unredacted rather than a visible error, so the strictness was costing exactly the thing the registry exists to protect. Two shapes were caught that shouldn't be: 1. `_has_top_level_alternation` rejected any depth-0 `|`, including patterns where every branch has its own literal prefix (`nvapi-...|nvkey_...`). The check protects the pre-screen's literal-prefix guarantee, but that guarantee is per branch, not per pattern. The blanket check is replaced with per-branch validation: split at top-level `|`, require a 2+ char literal prefix on every branch, and feed every branch's prefix into `_PREFIX_SUBSTRINGS` so the pre-screen stays free of false negatives on the second form. `ab|.*` stays rejected (unprefixed branch), and the built-in patterns are unaffected (none have a top-level alternation, verified). 2. `_has_nested_unbounded_repeat` flagged all `(...+...)+` nesting structurally, so the unambiguous separator shape `(?:[0-9]+-)+` (Slack-style tokens) was rejected alongside `(a+)+`. The check now clears exactly that shape: the repeated group must end with a required unquantified literal separator that's disjoint from every inner unbounded atom, with no alternation inside the group. Everything the analysis can't positively clear stays rejected: quantified or optional separators, wildcard (`.`) or zero-width (`$`) separators, opaque escapes (`\x41`, backrefs), repeats of repeats, and the classic catastrophic shapes. Why this approach rather than loosening the failure mode: fail-soft on registration is deliberate (a broken plugin must not break startup), so the fix has to be making the validators accept what's actually safe while keeping every rejection they were added for. ## Related Issue Fixes #85123 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [x] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `agent/redact.py`: replaced `_has_top_level_alternation` with `_split_top_level_alternation` (same scanner, returns the branches). Registration now validates the literal prefix per branch, which subsumes both the old alternation check and the old whole-pattern prefix check. `_PREFIX_SUBSTRINGS` (module load and `_rebuild_prefix_matcher`) is built per branch. - `agent/redact.py`: rewrote `_has_nested_unbounded_repeat` from a contains-unbounded flag stack to a small per-group scan that tracks unbounded simple atoms (chars, classes, `\d`-style class escapes), the group's last atom, and alternation. An unbounded-quantified group is cleared only when its last atom is a required literal the inner repeats can't match (checked with `re.fullmatch` per atom). Anything opaque to the analysis counts as complex and stays rejected. - `tests/test_redaction_registry.py`: updated the two pinned tests that encoded the blanket behavior (`ab|cd` rejected, `ab((x+)y)*` rejected, both are safe and now accepted) and added coverage: multi-prefix alternation registers and both prefixes reach the pre-screen, separator repetition registers and masks end to end, ambiguous separators (`(?:[0-9a-f]+a)+`, optional/wildcard/zero-width separators, alternation in the group, repeat-of-repeat) all still rejected. ## How to Test 1. `pytest tests/test_redaction_registry.py -q` (22 pass, was 18 before; the new tests fail on main) 2. Regression repro from the issue: `register_redaction_patterns([r"nvapi-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}|nvkey_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}"])` returns 1 and both token forms are masked by `redact_sensitive_text` 3. ReDoS safety spot-check: the classic shapes still fail validation, and the accepted Slack shape scans a 50k-char adversarial input (`xoxb-` + `1`*50000 + `!`) in under a millisecond ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [x] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass (redaction-related selection run in full; the only failures are 19 pre-existing pytest-asyncio collection issues that fail identically on main) - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — the `register_redaction_patterns` docstring documents the per-branch rule and the separator carve-out - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — pure regex/string logic, no platform surface - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A

signal.title: fix: voice dictation broken in profiles created via profiles.create (missing stt/tts config)
signal.text: Desktop dictation is profile-scoped: `/api/audio/transcribe` runs `transcribe_recording` under `_config_profile_scope(profile)`, resolving the `stt` section from the TARGET profile's config.yaml. Profiles created via `profiles.create` (#85093) get only a `model` section — so STT falls back to defaults and dictation breaks in every created-profile chat while working fine on the primary ('voice dictation doesn't work in bot mode but is fine in regular mode' — Bot Mode user report). Fix: mirror the launch profile's `stt`/`tts`/`voice` config sections into the new profile, key-wise (sections a clone already carries are never overwritten), gated on the same `mirror_credentials` flag as .env/auth mirroring, reported as `mirrored.voice`. Verified live: profiles.create → new profile's config.yaml carries stt+tts+model → cleanup. Same pattern as the #85111 credential mirroring.

signal.title: Desktop: same assistant message rendered twice in chat view (DB stores single record; frontend rendering issue)
signal.text: ## Summary In the Hermes Desktop app (Windows), an assistant message occasionally appears **twice** in the chat view. The message is stored **once** in `state.db` (no duplicate rows, no duplicate IDs), which points to a **frontend rendering-layer** issue rather than storage/sync duplication. ## Observed in two independent sessions (same day) 1. Session analyzing CGM (continuous glucose monitor) data, 2026-08-13 afternoon: a long assistant reply (blood-glucose meal analysis) rendered twice in the scrollback. 2. Session "境外手机号必要性分析" (overseas phone number analysis), 2026-08-13 13:24 UTC+8: same duplicate display behavior. Both are local desktop sessions (no Telegram/Discord/etc. delivery involved). ## Investigation already done (user-side) - `state.db` → `messages` table: the duplicated assistant reply exists as **exactly 1 row**; `SELECT id, COUNT(*) FROM messages GROUP BY id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1` returns **0 rows** across all 11k+ messages. → Storage layer is clean. - `platform_message_id` is NULL for local desktop sessions → no external delivery layer involved. → Delivery layer is clean. - The affected session's model (deepseek direct, no provider fallback involved) shows **no** `No response from provider` / `stream drop` / `Reconnecting` entries in `desktop.log` around the incident → not caused by provider stream-reconnect re-rendering (an earlier hypothesis involving an unrelated background review task that uses a different model via OpenRouter was investigated and ruled out — the GLM-5.2 timeout in the log belonged to that background task, not the affected session). - Only GUI-related log noise: benign `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications` messages from the renderer. ## Expected behavior Each assistant message appears exactly once in the chat view. ## Actual behavior The same message content is rendered twice, both copies visible in the conversation scrollback (appear to share the same/very close timestamp). Restarting the app clears the duplicate (memory-state rendering issue). ## Environment - OS: Windows 10 - Hermes Desktop (Electron app), backend commit `f5be9236` (2026-08-04) - Provider: deepseek direct for main conversation; openrouter only for auxiliary tasks (approval / background_review) ## Suggested debugging direction Most likely in the frontend message-list rendering: React list key collisions, virtualized-list duplicate append, or overlap between the initial API-fetched history and a live WebSocket push of the same message (duplicate insertion on merge). Reproduces intermittently. A pointer to where the chat message list merges API-fetched history with live-streamed messages would help narrow it down. Happy to provide more logs or run a debug build if useful.

signal.title: fix(desktop): stop offering unsupported GitHub MCP OAuth
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Stops Hermes Desktop from advertising GitHub's hosted MCP server through the generic one-click OAuth path. The Desktop MCP directory assumes every hosted remote supports OAuth Dynamic Client Registration. GitHub requires each MCP host to provide its own GitHub OAuth app, or authenticate with a PAT. Clicking `Add GitHub` therefore saved `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/`, attempted registration, received `Registration failed: 404 404 page not found`, and rolled the entry back. This removes GitHub from the DCR-backed directory until Desktop has a GitHub-specific OAuth or PAT setup flow. It also prevents the agent-driven `setup_mcp` card from reaching the same broken directory fallback. Manual PAT configuration under Capabilities > MCP remains available. ## Related Issue No GitHub issue. Reproduced from a Discord support report against the newly shipped Desktop suggestion. ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - Removed the GitHub hosted endpoint from `apps/desktop/src/lib/mcp-directory.ts`, the directory shared by composer suggestions and the `setup_mcp` fallback. - Documented why GitHub cannot use the directory's generic DCR contract. - Added a regression proving the shipped directory does not offer GitHub through that path. ## How to Test 1. Run `npm --workspace apps/desktop run test:ui -- src/store/suggestion-providers/mcp.test.ts`. 2. In Desktop, type `connect github` in the composer. 3. Confirm Desktop no longer offers the broken `Add GitHub` OAuth pill. Existing manually configured GitHub MCP servers remain unaffected. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass (N/A: JS-only Desktop change; no Python tests run) - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11, focused Vitest plus Desktop typecheck and targeted ESLint ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — N/A; the source comment records the provider constraint - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — renderer-only directory data - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A ## Screenshots / Logs Focused validation: - `mcp.test.ts`: 12 tests passed - Desktop TypeScript typecheck: passed - Targeted ESLint: passed - Prettier and `git diff --check`: passed

signal.title: [Feature]: Native desktop/mobile client app
signal.text: ## Feature Description A native desktop/mobile client app for Hermes Agent that interacts directly with the local Gateway/API Server, without relying on third-party messaging platforms as intermediaries. ## Motivation Current interaction methods each have limitations imposed by the platforms themselves: - URLs in tool output get truncated, making links unclickable - Message length limits force HTML file workarounds - Interactive approval buttons degrade to plain text across versions - Gateway restarts disconnect the session - Technical config must be done via CLI separately A native client would provide a purpose-built interface for AI agent interaction. ## Proposed Solution Cross-platform native app (Tauri/Flutter) reusing existing API Server + Gateway: - Desktop: Windows/macOS/Linux - Mobile: iOS/Android - Shared sessions, skills, memory with CLI/Web UI - Native push notifications, file handling, proper URL rendering

signal.title: fix(config): stop valid reasoning effort settings from triggering warnings
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? `hermes config set agent.reasoning_effort high` now saves the supported global reasoning setting without also printing a false unrecognized-key warning. The default config schema now declares the same global key that the runtime and example configuration already consume. ### Symptom Setting `agent.reasoning_effort` succeeds and `hermes config get agent.reasoning_effort` returns the saved value, but the set command also warns that the key is unrecognized and suggests `agent.reasoning_overrides`. ### Impact Users configuring the documented global reasoning effort receive misleading guidance even though their setting is valid and persisted. The warning can make them replace a global scalar setting with the separate per-model override mapping. ### Bug Cause **Trigger:** `hermes_cli/config.py:5009` in `_validate_config_key`, when it walks `DEFAULT_CONFIG` for `agent.reasoning_effort`. **Causal chain:** 1. A user runs `hermes config set agent.reasoning_effort high`. 2. Key validation reaches the `agent` mapping in `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, where `reasoning_effort` was missing even though runtime consumers support it. 3. Validation reports the valid key as unknown and fuzzy-matches the sibling `agent.reasoning_overrides`; the later write still persists the value. **Why it is wrong:** The validation schema was incomplete relative to the documented and runtime-supported configuration contract. **Working sibling / contrast:** `agent.reasoning_overrides` validates without a warning because that sibling was already declared in the same default schema. **Ruled out:** This is not a persistence failure. The public set path writes `reasoning_effort: high`, and reading the key returns `high`; only schema recognition was incorrect. ### Fix Add `agent.reasoning_effort` to `DEFAULT_CONFIG` and cover the public `set_config_value` path with a regression test that verifies both warning suppression and persistence. ## Related Issue Closes #85741 ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) ## Changes Made - `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py` - declare the supported global reasoning effort setting in the default schema. - `tests/hermes_cli/test_set_config_value.py` - verify that the global key persists without an unknown-key warning or the override suggestion. ## How to Test 1. Run the focused config-set regression suite: ```bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_set_config_value.py ``` 2. Confirm `TestConfigYamlRouting::test_global_reasoning_effort_is_recognized` passes. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [x] I've run the repository test entry on the relevant test file and all tests pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] Relevant documentation is already present; this change aligns validation with it - [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` already documents `agent.reasoning_effort`; no update is needed - [x] No architecture or workflow documentation changes are needed - [x] Cross-platform impact was considered; the schema validation path is platform-independent - [x] No tool descriptions or schemas changed ## Screenshots / Logs N/A - covered by the focused automated regression test.

signal.title: fix(config): recognize agent.reasoning_effort as a known key
signal.text: Fixes #85741 `hermes config set agent.reasoning_effort high` saved the value but emitted a false "not a recognized config key" warning suggesting `agent.reasoning_overrides`. ## Root cause `hermes_cli/config.py` `_validate_config_key()` walks `DEFAULT_CONFIG` to decide whether a dotted key is recognized. The `agent` section declared `reasoning_overrides` (the per-model mapping) but not the global scalar `agent.reasoning_effort`, even though that scalar is read at runtime at session start (`cli.py` → `_parse_reasoning_config(...)` → `CLI_CONFIG["agent"].get("reasoning_effort", "")`). The key is honored at runtime but was misreported as unknown by the CLI, complete with a misleading "did you mean" hint pointing at the per-model mapping. ## Fix Add the documented `agent.reasoning_effort` default (`""`) to `DEFAULT_CONFIG["agent"]`, alongside `reasoning_overrides`. The recognizer now accepts the scalar key without a warning; the value remains written to and read from `config.yaml` exactly as before. ## Validation - New regression test `test_agent_reasoning_effort_is_recognized` reproduces the bug (pre-fix it fails with the exact warning text) and passes post-fix. - Full `tests/hermes_cli/test_set_config_value.py`: 84 passed. - `ruff check` on `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py` and the test file: clean.

signal.title: [Bug]: hermes update stalls at autostash restore prompt on macOS — post-update gateway restart never runs, gateway serves stale code
signal.text: ## Summary On macOS, `hermes update` can stall at the autostash-restore interactive prompt ("Restore local changes now? [Y/n]"). When that happens the process never reaches the post-update gateway-restart block, so a launchd-supervised gateway keeps running with pre-update modules in memory while lazily importing post-update code from disk — a mixed/stale runtime that fails later with confusing errors. ## Environment - macOS (launchd-managed gateway, `ai.hermes.gateway`) - Direct upstream checkout (NOT a fork — the #73108 fork case is a different trigger) - Hermes v0.20.0 (2026.8.3), updated 2026-08-13 to `fa83af3f9` ## Observed timeline (from ~/.hermes/logs/update.log and gateway-exit-diag.log) 1. `2026-08-13T22:25:06` — `hermes update` starts. Local changes detected → autostash created (`hermes-update-autostash-20260813-142640`). Found 4231 new commits, pulled them. 2. Update prints the restore prompt and **stalls there**. `update.log` ends at `Restore local changes now? [Y/n]` — no further output. The stash entry is still present afterwards (`git stash list` shows `stash@{0}: On main: hermes-update-autostash-20260813-142640`), i.e. the update never completed its restore step, hence never reached the restart block. 3. The gateway process (PID 20465, started 2026-08-13 21:45) kept running on the pre-update code for ~12 hours. 4. `2026-08-14 01:40:22 UTC` — gateway exits non-zero (`gateway.exit_nonzero` in gateway-exit-diag.log), 30s later a manual `launchctl kickstart -k` brings it back on the new code. Only then does the mixed-runtime error go away. The same autostash pattern also appears at 07-25 and 05-20 (older `hermes-update-autostash-*` entries), suggesting the prompt regularly stalls when the update runs in a context where stdin is not attended (e.g. run from an IDE/terminal that closed, or a non-interactive wrapper). ## Root cause In `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py`, `_restore_stashed_changes()` blocks on `input()` (or `_gateway_prompt`) before the gateway-restart block in `_cmd_update_impl()` runs. If the prompt never gets a response (closed stdin, unattended terminal, EOF handling paths), the update either hangs or takes the skip-restore path and the **gateway fleet restart is skipped entirely** — there is no timeout on the prompt and no "restart gateways even though restore was skipped" guarantee. The post-update restart logic exists (launchd/systemd/manual-PID branches, added around 84a875ca0 / 988ecc742) but it is downstream of an interactive prompt that can block indefinitely. Related: #73108 is the same symptom family (post-update restart skipped) but triggered by the fork "Already up to date" early-exit; its fix PR #73679 is still open. This report is the direct-upstream counterpart: the restart is skipped whenever the update path is interrupted before the restart block, and the autostash prompt is one such interruption point. ## Expected behavior - The post-update gateway restart should run even when stash restore is skipped or times out (restart is independent of restore). - The autostash prompt should have a timeout / non-interactive default so an unattended `hermes update` does not hang mid-update with a gateway left on stale code. - At minimum, when a running gateway could not be restarted, print explicit guidance (the managed-runtime repair path already does this with "Restart required to finish..." — plain source-tree updates emit neither a warning nor a restart). ## Workaround Manually restart the launchd service after every `hermes update` (e.g. kickstart the `ai.hermes.gateway` label), or chain the restart onto the update command.
signal.author: Feahter

signal.title: session_search discovery hides ALL hits from the current session's own /new-reset lineage (gateway recall goes blind)
signal.text: ## Summary In gateway conversations (QQ/Telegram/etc.), every `/new` creates a child session via `parent_session_id`. `session_search` discovery excludes any hit whose lineage root equals the *current* session's lineage root (`tools/session_search_tool.py`, the `current_lineage_root == lineage_root` guard), on the assumption that same-lineage content is already in the active context. That assumption holds for compression continuations but is false for manual `/new` resets, which carry no transcript. Result: after each `/new`, the agent cannot recall *any* previous session of the same chat — `session_search` returns 0 results even though messages, FTS, and vector indexes are all intact. ## Reproduction (real state.db) Chain: `20260812_152906` → child `20260813_083223` → child `20260814_083525` (current). - `session_search(query="布洛芬")` from the current session → **0 results** - Direct SQL on the same DB: `messages_fts_trigram MATCH '布洛芬'` → 12 rows, all joined correctly to `20260813_083223` - Browse mode (`session_search()` with no args) shows only cron sessions, because every recent interactive session has a `parent_session_id` and is skipped Concrete user impact: the user asked the agent "do you remember what we talked about last night?" — the agent searched, got 0 results, and wrongly concluded no conversation had happened, when in fact a full 167-message session existed. ## Root cause - Discovery guard: `tools/session_search_tool.py` (~L641) `if current_lineage_root and lineage_root == current_lineage_root: continue` - Browse skip: (~L451) `if s.get("parent_session_id"): continue` - `_resolve_lineage()` already computes `has_compression_hop` to distinguish compression splits from other children, but both guards ignore it and treat all lineage children as in-context. ## Expected behavior The current-lineage exclusion should apply only when the lineage hop is a compression continuation (content actually carried forward). `/new`-reset children should be discoverable and browsable like any other session. ## Related, not duplicate - #82988 — browse drops resumed conversations (the list-side symptom) - #6507 — child hit summarized at the lineage root (the transcript-side symptom) - This one is the *current-lineage exclusion* — a third defect in the same neighborhood.

signal.title: fix(security): validate Bitwarden server_url and terminate bws argv (#77480)
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? The `bws` child process receives the BSM access token, so the two values that steer it — where it connects and which project it reads — are security-relevant inputs. Neither was validated. This closes both, plus the environment-inherited variant of the first. **1. `server_url` accepted anything, including plaintext `http://`.** A phished setup answer or a committed `config.yaml` pointing at `http://attacker.example` sent the access token to that endpoint, unencrypted. It is now required to be `https://`, with a real host and no embedded `user:pass@` credentials. Plaintext `http://` is still accepted for loopback (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`) — self-hosted users tunnelling to a local port rely on it, and there is no network there to sniff. **2. An ambient `BWS_SERVER_URL` from the parent shell bypassed even that.** When the config key was empty, whatever `BWS_SERVER_URL` the caller happened to export was passed through untouched (`bitwarden.py:686-689`). That is a deliberate override escape hatch, so it stays — but it now goes through the same validator, and a value that fails is dropped with a warning instead of silently redirecting the token. **3. `project_id` was interpolated into the argv with no `--` terminator.** A value starting with `-` was parsed by `bws` as a flag. Verified against the real bws 2.0.0 binary: ``` $ bws secret list "--help" --output json # current main's argv shape Usage: bws.exe secret list [OPTIONS] [PROJECT_ID] <- parsed as a flag $ bws secret list --output json -- "--help" # this PR's shape error: invalid value '--help' for '[PROJECT_ID]' <- stays a positional ``` `--` is what `op read` already does when it assembles its argv (`onepassword.py:279`, `cmd += ["--", reference]`). On top of that, `project_id` must now be UUID-shaped, which is what the config key is documented to hold (`"BSM project UUID"`) and the only thing `bws secret list` accepts. Validation runs **before** the cache lookup, so a rejected value can never serve a cached fetch, and the cache key holds the checked form. ### Why this shape `validate_server_url` / `validate_project_id` are module-level and public because `hermes_cli/secrets_cli.py` needs the same rules at setup time — persisting an endpoint the fetch path will later refuse is its own bug. `apply_server_url_to_env` keeps the env-var handling in one place so the two `bws` spawn sites (`_run_bws_list`, `_list_projects`) can't drift. Deliberately **not** a host allowlist: self-hosted Bitwarden means arbitrary hosts are legitimate. The scheme is what protects the token in transit. ## Related Issue Fixes #77480 ## Type of Change - [x] 🔒 Security fix ## Changes Made - `agent/secret_sources/bitwarden.py` - new `validate_server_url()`, `validate_project_id()`, `apply_server_url_to_env()` - `fetch_bitwarden_secrets()` validates both inputs before the cache lookup - `_run_bws_list()` passes the project id after `--`, and routes the env var through the shared helper; a dropped ambient override is logged and returned in `warnings` - `server_url` config-schema description notes the https requirement - `hermes_cli/secrets_cli.py` - `_resolve_server_url()` validates the `--server-url` flag, the `BWS_SERVER_URL` env var, and the interactive custom URL. A stored-but-invalid config value no longer dead-ends setup — it's dropped with a warning and the region menu is shown, since fixing it is why the user ran setup. The interactive prompt re-asks instead of aborting. This replaces the old "warning: doesn't start with http:// or https://, bws may reject it" advisory. - `_list_projects()` uses `apply_server_url_to_env()` - `tests/test_bitwarden_secrets.py` — 28 new test cases across 11 test functions (see below); existing fixtures moved off placeholder project ids (`"p"`, `"proj-1"`) to a well-formed UUID constant - `website/docs/user-guide/secrets/bitwarden.md` — documents the https requirement and the inherited-env-var rule ## How to Test ```bash pytest tests/test_bitwarden_secrets.py tests/hermes_cli/test_bitwarden_status.py \ tests/hermes_cli/test_secrets_bitwarden_non_tty.py -q ``` New coverage: - `validate_server_url` accepts `""`, both cloud regions, a self-hosted `https://` URL with port and path, and `http://` on loopback; rejects `http://` elsewhere (incl. a private IP), `user:pw@`, `ftp://`, `file://`, a bare hostname, and `https://` with no host - `validate_project_id` accepts a UUID (any case, surrounding whitespace); rejects empty, `"proj-1"`, `"aaaa-bbbb"`, `"--help"`, `"-o /tmp/x"`, and a near-miss UUID - a fetch with `server_url="http://attacker.example"` or `project_id="--config=/tmp/evil.toml"` raises before `subprocess.run` is reached at all (the fake asserts it is never called) - the argv ends with `["--", <uuid>]` - an inherited `BWS_SERVER_URL=http://attacker.example` is dropped and surfaces a warning; an inherited `https://` one is preserved; a configured value wins over an inherited one Manual verification of the `--` behaviour used the real pinned binary (`bws 2.0.0`, downloaded via `bw.install_bws()`) — output in the section above. Both argv shapes reach the identical token-decryption stage for a valid UUID, so the terminator changes nothing for the normal path. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate — see note below - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix - [x] I've run the relevant tests and they pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes - [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 (26100), Python 3.12.10 On duplicates: #77027 also touches Bitwarden child-process env, but it strips the **token** and `*_PASSWORD` from children — a different variable and the opposite direction (keeping secrets out of children, rather than validating where the token is sent). No overlap in the lines changed. I found no open PR touching `server_url` validation or the `bws` argv. Test-run note: on Windows, `test_install_bws_happy_path` and `test_encrypted_cache_writes_without_plaintext` fail on this branch — but they fail identically on unmodified `main` (chmod/0600 semantics), so they're pre-existing and unrelated. Everything else passes: 44 passed in `test_bitwarden_secrets.py` (23 before this PR), plus `tests/secret_sources/`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_bitwarden_status.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_secrets_bitwarden_non_tty.py` and `tests/hermes_cli/test_secrets_token_rotation.py` green. Related: #68226 is already open for Windows portability in these tests. ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (`website/docs/user-guide/secrets/bitwarden.md`, docstrings, config-schema description) - [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` — N/A (no new config keys) - [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md` — N/A (no architecture or workflow change) - [x] Cross-platform impact considered — pure-Python string/URL validation, no OS-specific paths; `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py` reports nothing on the changed lines - [x] Tool descriptions/schemas — N/A ## Compatibility Three configs that used to "work" now fail fast with an actionable message: - `server_url` on plaintext `http://` to a non-loopback host — this is the vulnerability, and the error names the key and the fix - `server_url` with embedded credentials, or a non-http(s) scheme - a non-UUID `project_id` — which `bws` rejects anyway, just with a less clear error Failures surface through the existing `SecretSource` error path, so they warn and continue rather than blocking startup. --- 🤖 Written with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code); reviewed and tested by me.

signal.title: fix(aux): stop probe stubs poisoning the client cache
signal.text: ## Summary `_store_cached_client()` refuses to cache an `_AuxProbeClientStub`. `_get_cached_client()` assigns to `_client_cache` directly and never reaches that guard — so the one function that *is* protected is not the function the availability probes actually go through. The result: a tool-gating `check_fn` caches a non-functional stub, and the next runtime caller with the same cache key gets it back and dies. ``` RuntimeError: _AuxProbeClientStub used as a real client (attribute 'chat'); aux_probe_mode is for availability checks only ``` ## How it happens 1. Tool-schema assembly calls `check_browser_vision_requirements()` → `check_vision_requirements()`. 2. That resolves inside `aux_probe_mode()`, which is correct — it only wants to know whether a client is *resolvable*, and building a real SDK client for that answer costs an `openai` import plus httpx/SSL setup on the cold-start path. 3. Resolution runs through `_get_cached_client()`, which stores the returned stub in `_client_cache`. The cache key has no probe/runtime field, so nothing marks the entry as poisoned. 4. The next real vision call hits that key, receives the stub, and raises on attribute access. ## Why it stayed hidden The cache key's second field is `async_mode`. The probe caches the **sync** variant: ``` ('<provider>', False, '', '', '', (), True, '', '', '<model>') -> _AuxProbeClientStub ``` So the two consumers diverge: - `analyze_image` resolves **async**, misses the poisoned key, builds a real client, and works. - `browser_vision` resolves **sync**, hits the poisoned key, and fails on every call. A setup that only ever attaches images directly never sees this. It surfaces the moment a sync vision consumer runs after tool gating — for us, as soon as `browser_vision` became reachable. Reproduced deterministically against a local OpenAI-compatible vision endpoint: ``` [after probe] cache entries: 1 (..., False, ..., True, '<model>') -> _AuxProbeClientStub <-- STUB real resolve -> <provider> _AuxProbeClientStub <model> BOOM: _AuxProbeClientStub used as a real client (attribute 'chat') ``` With the patch, the probe leaves the cache empty and the real resolve builds and caches a genuine client. ## The fix Guard the inline store in `_get_cached_client()` the same way `_store_cached_client()` already guards its own, and return the stub to the probe caller without caching it. Two lines of behavior, no change to resolution policy, no change to the probe's fast path. ## Why the existing test did not catch it `test_probe_stub_never_cached` asserts the invariant by calling `_store_cached_client()` — the door that was already locked. The new test drives `_get_cached_client()` under `aux_probe_mode()` and asserts no stub reaches `_client_cache`. It fails on `main` and passes with the fix: ``` AssertionError: probe stub reached the cache: [('probe-guard-test', False, ...)] ``` ## Tests ``` tests/tools/test_startup_latency_regressions.py 17 passed tests/agent/test_vision_routing_31179.py 8 passed tests/tools/test_browser_use_cli.py 79 passed ``` Run with a Python 3.10+ interpreter (the codebase uses `X | Y` unions): ```sh ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python -m pip install --target /tmp/prlibs pytest cd ~/hermes-agent PYTHONPATH=/tmp/prlibs ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/tools/test_startup_latency_regressions.py -q ``` ### Unrelated pre-existing failure, noted for the reviewer Running `tests/agent/test_vision_routing_31179.py` and `tests/tools/test_browser_use_cli.py` **in the same pytest process** produces 10 failures in the latter. This reproduces on pristine `main` without this patch, and both files pass when run separately. It is cross-file state leakage in the existing suite, not a regression from this change, and is left alone here.

signal.title: feat(langfuse): trace auxiliary LLM calls for full usage accounting (config.yaml + async)
signal.text: ## Summary Auxiliary LLM calls (context compression, vision, web_extract, MoA, session search, ...) were invisible to the Langfuse observability plugin: they go through `agent/auxiliary_client.call_llm` / `async_call_llm`, which bypass the agent-turn hooks the plugin subscribes to. Over time this makes Langfuse token totals diverge from provider billing (e.g. api.deepseek.com), breaking reconciliation between observability and the provider's own usage report. This reworks the previous attempt (#76874) per the standing maintainer policy and fixes its two blockers: ## Policy compliance (per #76874 close comment + AGENTS.md) 1. **Behavioral flag moved from env var to config.yaml.** The opt-in is now `plugins.entries.observability/langfuse.track_aux` in `config.yaml` — no new `HERMES_*` env var. `.env` stays reserved for secrets (AGENTS.md: "All behavioral settings ... go in config.yaml"). 2. **Async coverage added (the "not full auxiliary accounting" gap).** The original PR wrapped only synchronous `call_llm`, but the vision path calls `async_call_llm` (`tools/vision_tools.py:1278`). The observer now fires for **both** sync `call_llm` and async `async_call_llm` (start/end/error). ## Changes **agent/auxiliary_client.py** - Observer registry (`register_aux_llm_observer` / `unregister_aux_llm_observer` / `_notify_aux_llm`) — empty by default, zero overhead; observers are fail-open. - `call_llm` thin wrapper around `_call_llm_impl` emitting start/end/error. - `async_call_llm` thin wrapper around `_async_call_llm_impl` emitting the same events — covers the vision path. **plugins/observability/langfuse** - `_track_aux_enabled()` resolves `plugins.entries.observability/langfuse.track_aux` from config.yaml (cached per process, fail-closed to False on config read errors). - When enabled, registers the observer and records each auxiliary call as a standalone `Hermes aux: <task>` trace with a GENERATION child carrying token usage — including DeepSeek cache hit/miss via the existing `_usage_and_cost` path. - README documents the config.yaml opt-in. **tests/plugins/test_langfuse_plugin.py** - `TestAuxTracking`: default-off, config.yaml resolution, observer registration, usage recording (cache_read/input/output), error-path cleanup. - `TestAuxObserversOnCallLlm`: sync AND async call_llm both emit start/end/error events. ## Verification - `pytest tests/plugins/test_langfuse_plugin.py` → 33 passed (incl. 9 new). - `pytest tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client.py` → 169 passed. - `pytest tests/tools/test_vision_tools.py tests/agent/test_auxiliary_compression_timeout_floor.py tests/agent/test_unsupported_parameter_retry.py tests/agent/test_unsupported_temperature_retry.py tests/tools/test_video_analyze.py` → 67 passed. - E2E against a local Langfuse instance: sync `call_llm` and async `async_call_llm` both produced `Hermes aux: <task>` traces in ClickHouse with correct usage details (input/output/cache_read/reasoning/total); async error path closes the trace cleanly.

signal.title: Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (2026.8.13)
signal.text: # Hermes Agent v0.20.1 (v2026.8.13) **Release Date:** August 13, 2026 > Patch release. This tag rolls up the ~656 PRs merged since v0.20.0 into a stable tagged release for downstream consumers (Docker images, hosted deployments, and anyone installing from the latest tag). --- ## About this release Since v0.20.0 (August 3), this window landed **1,444 commits** across **~656 merged PRs**, touching **2,172 files** (+233,872 / −75,244), and closed **~481 issues**. It is a broad stabilization-and-fixes rollup spanning the desktop app, gateway platforms, installers, tool system, and provider catalogs. **Full curated release notes for this window will ship with v0.21.0**, which will document everything from v0.20.0 onward — highlights, feature areas, and complete contributor credits. Nothing in this window is skipped. ## Updating - Existing installs: `hermes update` - Fresh install: see the installer one-liner in the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent#readme) **Full Changelog**: [v2026.8.3...v2026.8.13](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/compare/v2026.8.3...v2026.8.13)
